## Descent of heavier payloads

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mars_landing&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Descent of heavier payloads")]

[![Image 6](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/79/PIA23301-MarsInSightLander-PitsMadeByThrusters-20181214.jpg/250px-PIA23301-MarsInSightLander-PitsMadeByThrusters-20181214.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PIA23301-MarsInSightLander-PitsMadeByThrusters-20181214.jpg)

The thrusters of the [InSight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/InSight "InSight") lander dug pits during landing beneath it at its landing site.

For landers that are even heavier than the [_Curiosity_ rover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curiosity_rover "Curiosity rover") (which required a 4.5 meter (15 feet) diameter aeroshell), engineers are developing a combination rigid-inflatable [Low-Density Supersonic Decelerator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low-Density_Supersonic_Decelerator "Low-Density Supersonic Decelerator") that could be 8 meters (26 feet) in diameter. It would have to be accompanied by a proportionately larger parachute.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-8)

[Landing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landing "Landing") robotic [spacecraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spacecraft "Spacecraft"), and possibly some day humans, on Mars is a technological challenge. For a favorable landing, the lander module has to address these issues:[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-:0-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-10)

*   Thinness of [Mars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars "Mars")'s [atmosphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atmosphere "Atmosphere")
*   Measurement of distance to surface
*   Inadequate technology for [ballistic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballistics "Ballistics")[aerocapture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aerocapture "Aerocapture")
*   Inadequate technology for [retropropulsive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retropropulsive_landing "Retropropulsive landing") powered descent
*   Inadequate mission designs
*   Shorter time to perform [entry, descent and landing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entry,_descent_and_landing "Entry, descent and landing") (EDL)

In 2018, NASA successfully landed the [InSight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/InSight "InSight") lander on the surface of Mars, re-using [Viking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viking_Lander "Viking Lander")-era technology.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-11) But this technology cannot afford the ability to land large number of cargoes, habitats, ascent vehicles and humans in case of crewed Mars missions in near future. In order to improve and accomplish this intent, there is need to upgrade technologies and [launch vehicles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Launch_vehicle "Launch vehicle"). Some of the criteria for a lander performing a successful soft-landing using current technology are as follows:[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-12)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-:0-9)

Lander requirements | Feature | Criterion |
| --- | --- |
| Mass | Less than 0.6 tonnes (1,300 lb) |
| [Ballistic coefficient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballistic_coefficient "Ballistic coefficient") | Less than 35 kg/m 2 (7.2 lb/sq ft) |
| Diameter of [aeroshell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aeroshell "Aeroshell") | Less than 4.6 m (15 ft) |
| Geometry of aeroshell | 70° spherical cone shell |
| Diameter of parachute | Less than 30 m (98 ft) |
| Descent | Supersonic [retropropulsive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VTVL "VTVL")[powered descent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Powered_descent "Powered descent") |
| Entry | [Orbital entry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aerocapture "Aerocapture") (i.e. entry from Mars orbit) |

## Communicating with Earth

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mars_landing&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Communicating with Earth")]

Beginning with the Viking program,[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-13) all landers on the surface of Mars have used orbiting spacecraft as [communications satellites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communications_satellite "Communications satellite") for relaying their data to Earth. The landers use [UHF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultra_high_frequency "Ultra high frequency") transmitters to send their data to the orbiters, which then relay the data to Earth using either [X band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X_band "X band") or [Ka band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ka_band "Ka band") frequencies. These higher frequencies, along with more powerful transmitters and larger [parabolic reflectors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parabolic_reflector "Parabolic reflector"), permit the orbiters to send the data much faster than the landers could manage transmitting directly to Earth, which conserves valuable time on the [receiving antennas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Deep_Space_Network "NASA Deep Space Network").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-14)

## List of Mars landings

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mars_landing&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: List of Mars landings")]

[![Image 7](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/60/PIA22871_Full_View_of_InSight%27s_Deck_and_Two_Science_Instruments.jpg/250px-PIA22871_Full_View_of_InSight%27s_Deck_and_Two_Science_Instruments.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PIA22871_Full_View_of_InSight%27s_Deck_and_Two_Science_Instruments.jpg)

Insight Mars lander view in December 2018

In the 1970s, several USSR probes unsuccessfully tried to land on Mars. [Mars 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_3 "Mars 3") landed successfully in 1971 but failed soon afterwards. But the American _Viking_ landers made it to the surface and provided several years of images and data. However, the next successful Mars landing was not until 1997, when [Mars Pathfinder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_Pathfinder "Mars Pathfinder") landed.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-space.com-15) In the 21st century there have been several successful landings, but there have also been many crashes.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-space.com-15)

The first probe intended to be a Mars [impact](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_(mechanics) "Impact (mechanics)") lander was the Soviet _[Mars 1962B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars\_1962B "Mars 1962B")_, unsuccessfully launched in 1962.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-16)

In 1970 the Soviet Union began the design of _[Mars 4NM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars\_4NM "Mars 4NM")_ and _[Mars 5NM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars\_5NM "Mars 5NM")_ missions with super-heavy uncrewed Martian spacecraft. First was _[Marsokhod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marsokhod "Marsokhod")_, with a planned date of early 1973, and second was the Mars sample return mission planned for 1975. Both spacecraft were intended to be launched on the [_N1_ rocket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N1_rocket "N1 rocket"), but this rocket never flew successfully and the Mars 4NM and Mars 5NM projects were cancelled.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-17)

In 1971 the Soviet Union sent probes _[Mars 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars\_2 "Mars 2")_ and _[Mars 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars\_3 "Mars 3")_, each carrying a lander, as part of the [Mars probe program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_probe_program "Mars probe program") M-71. The Mars 2 lander failed to land and impacted Mars. The Mars 3 lander became the first probe to successfully [soft-land](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soft_landing_(rocketry) "Soft landing (rocketry)") on Mars, but its data-gathering had less success. The lander began transmitting to the Mars 3 orbiter 90 seconds after landing, but after 14.5 seconds, transmission ceased for unknown reasons. The cause of the failure may have been related to the extremely powerful Martian dust storm taking place at the time. These space probes each contained a Mars rover, [PrOP-M](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PrOP-M "PrOP-M"), although they were never deployed.

In 1973, the Soviet Union sent two more landers to Mars, _[Mars 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars\_6 "Mars 6")_ and _[Mars 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars\_7 "Mars 7")_. The Mars 6 lander transmitted data during descent but failed upon impact. The Mars 7 probe separated prematurely from the carrying vehicle due to a problem in the operation of one of the onboard systems ([attitude control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spacecraft_attitude_control "Spacecraft attitude control") or retro-rockets) and missed the planet by 1,300 km (810 mi).

The double-launching [_Mars 5M_ (Mars-79)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_5M "Mars 5M") sample return mission was planned for 1979, but was cancelled due to complexity and technical problems.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

[![Image 8](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5a/Mars_Viking_11h016.png/250px-Mars_Viking_11h016.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mars_Viking_11h016.png)

_[Viking 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viking\_1 "Viking 1")_ landing site (click image for detailed description).

In 1976 two American [_Viking_ probes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viking_program "Viking program") entered orbit about Mars and each released a [lander module](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lander_(spacecraft) "Lander (spacecraft)") that made a successful [soft landing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soft_landing_(rocketry) "Soft landing (rocketry)") on the planet's surface. They subsequently had the first successful transmission of large volumes of data, including the first color pictures and extensive scientific information. Measured temperatures at the landing sites ranged from 150 to 250 K (−123 to −23°C; −190 to −10°F), with a variation over a given day of 35 to 50°C (95 to 122°F).[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_][[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-18) Seasonal dust storms, pressure changes, and movement of atmospheric gases between the polar caps were observed.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] A [biology experiment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viking_Biological_Experiments "Viking Biological Experiments") produced possible evidence of life, but it was not corroborated by other on-board experiments.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

While searching for a suitable landing spot for _[Viking 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viking\_2 "Viking 2")_'s lander, the _[Viking 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viking\_1 "Viking 1")_ orbiter photographed the landform that constitutes the so-called "[Face on Mars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Face_on_Mars "Face on Mars")" on 25 July 1976.

The Viking program was a descendant of the cancelled [Voyager program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voyager_program_(Mars) "Voyager program (Mars)"), whose name was later reused for a pair of outer solar system probes.

[![Image 9](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/33/PIA02405.jpg/250px-PIA02405.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PIA02405.jpg)

"Ares Vallis" as photographed by _Mars Pathfinder_

[NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA")'s _[Mars Pathfinder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars\_Pathfinder "Mars Pathfinder")_ spacecraft, with assistance from the _[Mars Global Surveyor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars\_Global\_Surveyor "Mars Global Surveyor")_ orbiter, landed on 4 July 1997. Its landing site was an ancient flood plain in Mars's northern hemisphere called [Ares Vallis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ares_Vallis "Ares Vallis"), which is among the rockiest parts of Mars. It carried a tiny remote-controlled rover called [_Sojourner_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sojourner_(rover) "Sojourner (rover)"), the first successful [Mars rover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_rover "Mars rover"), that traveled a few meters around the landing site, exploring the conditions and sampling rocks around it. Newspapers around the world carried images of the lander dispatching the rover to explore the surface of Mars in a way never achieved before.

Until the final data transmission on 27 September 1997, _Mars Pathfinder_ returned 16,500 images from the lander and 550 images from the rover, as well as more than 15 chemical analyses of rocks and soil and extensive data on winds and other weather factors. Findings from the investigations carried out by scientific instruments on both the lander and the rover suggest that in the past Mars has been warm and wet, with liquid water and a thicker atmosphere. The mission website was the most heavily trafficked up to that time.

_[Mars 96](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars\_96 "Mars 96")_, an orbiter launched on 16 November 1996 by Russia, failed when the planned second burn of the Block D-2 fourth stage did not occur. Following the success of Global Surveyor and Pathfinder, another spate of failures occurred in 1998 and 1999, with the Japanese [_Nozomi_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nozomi_(spacecraft) "Nozomi (spacecraft)") orbiter and NASA's _[Mars Climate Orbiter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars\_Climate\_Orbiter "Mars Climate Orbiter")_, _[Mars Polar Lander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars\_Polar\_Lander "Mars Polar Lander")_, and _[Deep Space 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep\_Space\_2 "Deep Space 2")_ penetrators all suffering various terminal errors. Mars Climate Orbiter is infamous for [Lockheed Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lockheed_Martin "Lockheed Martin") engineers mixing up the usage of [U.S. customary units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._customary_units "U.S. customary units") with [metric units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metric_system "Metric system"), causing the orbiter to burn up while entering Mars's atmosphere. Out of 5–6 NASA missions in the 1990s, only 2 worked: Mars Pathfinder and Mars Global Surveyor, making Mars Pathfinder and its rover the only successful Mars landing in the 1990s.

### Mars Express and _Beagle 2_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mars_landing&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Mars Express and Beagle 2")]

On 2 June 2003, the [European Space Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Space_Agency "European Space Agency")'s _[Mars Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars\_Express "Mars Express")_ set off from [Baikonur Cosmodrome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baikonur_Cosmodrome "Baikonur Cosmodrome") to Mars. The Mars Express craft consisted of the _[Mars Express Orbiter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars\_Express\_Orbiter "Mars Express Orbiter")_ and the lander _[Beagle 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beagle\_2 "Beagle 2")_. Although the landing probe was not designed to move, it carried a digging device and the least massive spectrometer created to date, as well as a range of other devices, on a robotic arm in order to accurately analyse soil beneath the dusty surface.

The orbiter entered Mars orbit on 25 December 2003, and _Beagle 2_ should have entered Mars's atmosphere the same day. However, attempts to contact the lander failed. Communications attempts continued throughout January, but _Beagle 2_ was declared lost in mid-February, and a joint inquiry was launched by the UK and ESA that blamed principal investigator [Colin Pillinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colin_Pillinger "Colin Pillinger")'s poor project management. Nevertheless, Mars Express Orbiter confirmed the presence of water ice and carbon dioxide ice at the planet's south pole. NASA had previously confirmed their presence at the north pole of Mars.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Signs of the _Beagle 2_ lander were found in 2013 by the [HiRISE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HiRISE "HiRISE") camera on NASA's _[Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars\_Reconnaissance\_Orbiter "Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter")_, and the _Beagle 2_'s presence was confirmed in January 2015, several months after Pillinger's death. The lander appears to have successfully landed but not deployed all of its power and communications panels.

### Mars Exploration Rovers

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mars_landing&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Mars Exploration Rovers")]

Shortly after the launch of Mars Express, NASA sent a pair of twin rovers toward the planet as part of the _[Mars Exploration Rover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars\_Exploration\_Rover "Mars Exploration Rover")_ mission. On 10 June 2003, NASA's _[MER-A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MER-A "MER-A")_ _(Spirit)_ Mars Exploration Rover was launched. It successfully landed in [Gusev Crater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gusev_(Mars_crater) "Gusev (Mars crater)") (believed once to have been a crater lake) on 3 January 2004. It examined rock and soil for evidence of the area's history of water. On 7 July 2003, a second rover, _[MER-B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MER-B "MER-B")_ _(Opportunity)_ was launched. It landed on 24 January 2004 in [Meridiani Planum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meridiani_Planum "Meridiani Planum") (where there are large deposits of [hematite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hematite "Hematite"), indicating the presence of past water) to carry out similar geological work.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Despite a temporary loss of communication with the _Spirit_ rover (caused by a file system anomaly[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-19)) delaying exploration for several days, both rovers eventually began exploring their landing sites. The rover _Opportunity_ landed in a particularly interesting spot, a crater with bedrock outcroppings. In fast succession, mission team members announced on 2 March that data returned from the rover showed that these rocks were once "drenched in water", and on 23 March that it was concluded that they were laid down underwater in a salty sea. This represented the first strong direct evidence for liquid water on Mars at some time in the past.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Towards the end of July 2005, it was reported by the _[Sunday Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sunday\_Times\_(UK) "The Sunday Times (UK)")_ that the rovers may have carried the [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria "Bacteria")_[Bacillus safensis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacillus\_safensis "Bacillus safensis")_ to Mars. According to one NASA microbiologist, this bacteria could survive both the trip and conditions on Mars. Despite efforts to sterilise both landers, neither could be assured to be completely sterile.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-20)

Having been designed for only three-month missions, both rovers lasted much longer than planned. _Spirit_ lost contact with Earth in March 2010, 74 months after commencing exploration. _Opportunity_, however, continued to carry out surveys of the planet, surpassing 45 km (28 mi) on its odometer by the time communication with it was lost in June 2018, 173 months after it began.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-21)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-22) These rovers have discovered many new things, including [Heat Shield Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heat_Shield_Rock "Heat Shield Rock"), the first [meteorite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meteorite "Meteorite") to be discovered on another planet.

[![Image 12](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2e/Phoenix_Lander_seen_from_MRO_during_EDL2.jpg/120px-Phoenix_Lander_seen_from_MRO_during_EDL2.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Phoenix_Lander_seen_from_MRO_during_EDL2.jpg)

Camera on [Mars orbiter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_Reconnaissance_Orbiter "Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter") snaps _Phoenix_ suspended from its parachute during descent through [Mars's atmosphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atmosphere_of_Mars "Atmosphere of Mars").

_[Phoenix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix\_(spacecraft) "Phoenix (spacecraft)")_ launched on 4 August 2007, and touched down on the northern polar region of Mars on 25 May 2008. It is famous for having been successfully photographed while landing, since this was the first time one spacecraft captured the landing of another spacecraft onto a planet.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-23)

### Mars Science Laboratory

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mars_landing&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Mars Science Laboratory")]

[![Image 13](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c7/HiRISE_image_of_MSL_during_EDL_%28refined%29.png/250px-HiRISE_image_of_MSL_during_EDL_%28refined%29.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:HiRISE_image_of_MSL_during_EDL_(refined).png)

[Mars Science Laboratory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_Science_Laboratory "Mars Science Laboratory") (and the [_Curiosity_ rover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curiosity_rover "Curiosity rover")) descending on Mars

The [Mars Science Laboratory (MSL)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_Science_Laboratory "Mars Science Laboratory") (and [Curiosity rover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curiosity_rover "Curiosity rover")), launched in November 2011, landed in a location that is now called "[Bradbury Landing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bradbury_Landing "Bradbury Landing")", on [Aeolis Palus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aeolis_Palus "Aeolis Palus"), between [Peace Vallis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peace_Vallis "Peace Vallis") and [Aeolis Mons ("Mount Sharp")](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aeolis_Mons "Aeolis Mons"), in [Gale Crater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gale_(crater) "Gale (crater)") on [Mars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars "Mars") on 6 August 2012, 05:17 UTC.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-Space-20120806-24)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-NASA-Curiosity-25) The landing site was in _Quad 51_ ("Yellowknife")[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-NASA-20120810-26)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-NASA-20120809-27)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-BBC-20120809-28)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-USA-20120809-29) of _Aeolis Palus_ near the base of _Aeolis Mons_. The landing site[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-NASA-20120822-30) was less than 2.4 km (1.5 mi) from the center of the rover's planned target site after a 563,000,000 km (350,000,000 mi) journey.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-autogenerated1-31)[NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA") named the landing site "[Bradbury Landing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bradbury_Landing "Bradbury Landing")", in honor of author [Ray Bradbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Bradbury "Ray Bradbury"), on 22 August 2012.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-NASA-20120822-30)

### ExoMars _Schiaparelli_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mars_landing&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: ExoMars Schiaparelli")]

[![Image 14](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/83/Schiaparelli_Lander_Model_at_ESOC.JPG/250px-Schiaparelli_Lander_Model_at_ESOC.JPG)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Schiaparelli_Lander_Model_at_ESOC.JPG)

Model of _Schiaparelli_ lander at [ESOC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESOC "ESOC")

The [_Schiaparelli_ lander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schiaparelli_EDM_lander "Schiaparelli EDM lander") was intended to test technology for future soft landings on the surface of Mars as part of the [ExoMars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ExoMars "ExoMars") project. It was built in [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy "Italy") by the [European Space Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Space_Agency "European Space Agency") (ESA) and [Roscosmos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roscosmos "Roscosmos"). It was launched together with the [ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ExoMars_Trace_Gas_Orbiter "ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter") (TGO) on 14 March 2016 and attempted a landing on 19 October 2016. Telemetry was lost about one minute before the scheduled landing time,[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-ESA-20161019-32) but confirmed that most elements of the landing plan, including heat shield operation, parachute deployment, and rocket activation, had been successful.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-SAR-2017-33) The [Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_Reconnaissance_Orbiter "Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter") later captured imagery showing what appears to be Schiaparelli's crash site.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-34)

[![Image 15](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6a/Phoenix_landing.jpg/250px-Phoenix_landing.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Phoenix_landing.jpg)

_Phoenix_ landing art, similar to _Insight_

NASA's _[InSight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/InSight "InSight")_ lander _,_ designed to study seismology and heat flow from the deep interior of Mars, was launched on 5 May 2018. It landed successfully in Mars's [Elysium Planitia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elysium_Planitia "Elysium Planitia") on 26 November 2018.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-35)

### Mars 2020 and _Tianwen-1_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mars_landing&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Mars 2020 and Tianwen-1")]

NASA's [Mars 2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_2020 "Mars 2020") and [CNSA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_National_Space_Administration "China National Space Administration")'s _[Tianwen-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tianwen-1 "Tianwen-1")_ were both launched in the July 2020 window. Mars 2020's rover [_Perseverance_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perseverance_(rover) "Perseverance (rover)") successfully landed, in a location that is now called "[Octavia E. Butler Landing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octavia_E._Butler_Landing "Octavia E. Butler Landing")", in [Jezero Crater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jezero_(crater) "Jezero (crater)") on 18 February 2021,[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-36)[_Ingenuity_ helicopter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingenuity_(helicopter) "Ingenuity (helicopter)") was deployed and took subsequent flights in April.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-37)_Tianwen_-1's lander and [_Zhurong_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tianwen-1#Zhurong_rover "Tianwen-1") rover landed in [Utopia Planitia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utopia_Planitia "Utopia Planitia") on 14 May 2021 with the rover being deployed on 22 May 2021 and dropping a remote selfie camera on 1 June 2021.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-38)

The [ESA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Space_Agency "European Space Agency")_[Rosalind Franklin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosalind\_Franklin\_(rover) "Rosalind Franklin (rover)")_ is planned for launch in the late 2020s and would obtain soil samples from up to 2 metres (6 ft 7 in) depth and make an extensive search for [biosignatures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biosignature "Biosignature") and [biomolecules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biomolecule "Biomolecule"). There is also a proposal for a [Mars Sample Return Mission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_Sample_Return_Mission "Mars Sample Return Mission") by ESA and NASA, which would launch in 2024 or later. This mission would be part of the European [Aurora Programme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora_Programme "Aurora Programme").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The [Indian Space Research Organisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Space_Research_Organisation "Indian Space Research Organisation") (ISRO) has proposed to include landing of a rover and Marsplane in its [Mars Lander Mission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_Lander_Mission "Mars Lander Mission") around 2030 near [Eridania basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eridania_Lake "Eridania Lake").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-roadmap22-39)

## Twinned locations to Mars landing sites on Earth

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mars_landing&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Twinned locations to Mars landing sites on Earth")]

In the run-up to NASA's Mars 2020 landing, former planetary scientist and film-maker [Christopher Riley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Riley "Christopher Riley") mapped the locations of all eight of NASA's successful [Mars landing sites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#List_of_Mars_landings) onto their equivalent spots on Earth, in terms of latitudes and longitudes; presenting pairs of photographs from each twinned interplanetary location on Earth and Mars to draw attention to climate change.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-41) Following the successful landing of NASA's [Perseverance Rover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perseverance_(rover) "Perseverance (rover)") on 18 February 2021, Riley called for volunteers to travel to and photograph its twinned Earth location in Andegaon Wadi, Sawali, in the central Indian state of [Maharashtra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maharashtra "Maharashtra") (18.445°N, 77.451°E).[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-42)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-thenakedscientists.com-43)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-44) Eventually [BBC World Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_World_Service "BBC World Service") radio programme [Digital Planet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Planet "Digital Planet") listener Gowri Abhiram, from [Hyderabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyderabad "Hyderabad") took up the challenge, and travelled there on 22 January 2022, becoming the first person to knowingly reach a spot on Earth that matches the latitude and longitude of a robotic presence on the surface of another world.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-45) China's Tianwen-1 landing site maps onto an area in Southern China, 40 kilometres Southwest of [Guilin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guilin "Guilin") and is yet to be photographed for the project.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_landing#cite_note-thenakedscientists.com-43)

The **Zodiac Killer** (also known by the [pseudonym](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pseudonym "Pseudonym")**The Zodiac**) is an unidentified [serial killer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serial_killer "Serial killer") who murdered at least five people in the [San Francisco Bay Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Bay_Area "San Francisco Bay Area") between December 1968 and October 1969. The Zodiac attacked three couples and a cab driver in [Benicia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benicia,_California "Benicia, California"), [Vallejo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vallejo,_California "Vallejo, California"), unincorporated [Napa County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napa_County "Napa County"), and the [city of San Francisco.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco") Two of the Zodiac's seven victims survived.

In a series of letters mailed to Bay Area newspapers, the Zodiac took credit for the murders, described details known only to police, threatened bombings and more murders if the newspapers did not print his letters, and included [cryptograms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptogram "Cryptogram") with his correspondence. Two of the Zodiac's four cryptograms were decrypted in 1969 and 2020, and the other two remain unsolved.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-2) The Zodiac's last letter was received by the [_San Francisco Chronicle_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Chronicle "San Francisco Chronicle") in 1974. In the letter, The Zodiac claimed to have killed 37 people.

Despite several theories about the Zodiac's true identity, the only suspect police named was [Arthur Leigh Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen "Arthur Leigh Allen"), a former elementary school teacher and convicted [sex offender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_offender "Sex offender") who died in 1992. The Zodiac's murders, cryptograms, and letters to newspapers have made the case one of the most famous unsolved cases in American history. The Zodiac has become a [fixture of popular culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_in_popular_culture "Zodiac Killer in popular culture"), and the search for his identity continues to be pursued by amateur detectives all over the world.

In 2004, the [San Francisco Police Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Police_Department "San Francisco Police Department") marked the case "inactive," but subsequently re-opened the case in 2006. The [California Department of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Department_of_Justice "California Department of Justice"), [the Federal Bureau of Investigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Bureau_of_Investigation "Federal Bureau of Investigation"), the city of Vallejo, and the Napa and [Solano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solano_County,_California "Solano County, California") county sheriffs maintain the case status as "open."

## Murders and correspondence

Police and investigators concur The Zodiac attacked seven people on four occasions in [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California"). Five victims died; two survived:[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-HISTORY-2023a-3)

1.   David Arthur Faraday (17) and Betty Lou Jensen (16) were shot and killed on December 20, 1968, on Lake Herman Road in [Benicia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benicia,_California "Benicia, California").
2.   Michael Renault Mageau (19) and Darlene Elizabeth Ferrin (22) were shot around midnight between July 4 and 5, 1969, in the parking lot of Blue Rock Springs Park in [Vallejo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vallejo,_California "Vallejo, California"). Mageau survived the attack; Ferrin died at [Kaiser Foundation Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaiser_Foundation_Hospital "Kaiser Foundation Hospital").
3.   Bryan Calvin Hartnell (20) and Cecelia Ann Shepard (22) were stabbed on September 27, 1969, at [Lake Berryessa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Berryessa "Lake Berryessa") in [Napa County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napa_County,_California "Napa County, California"). Hartnell survived; Shepard died from her injuries on September 29 at [Queen of the Valley Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_of_the_Valley_Medical_Center_(Napa,_California) "Queen of the Valley Medical Center (Napa, California)").
4.   Paul Lee Stine (29) was shot and killed on October 11, 1969, in the [Presidio Heights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidio_Heights,_San_Francisco,_California "Presidio Heights, San Francisco, California") neighborhood of [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco").

From 1969 to 1974, the Zodiac sent over twenty letters to newspapers, police, _Chronicle_ writer [Paul Avery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Avery "Paul Avery"), and attorney [Melvin Belli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melvin_Belli "Melvin Belli"). In the first sentence of the third letter, the writer identified himself as, "This is The Zodiac speaking," and signed all his letters with a symbol resembling the [crosshairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reticle "Reticle") of a [gunsight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sight_(device) "Sight (device)"): [![Image 7](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f4/Zodiac_Killer_symbol.svg/20px-Zodiac_Killer_symbol.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Zodiac_Killer_symbol.svg).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-4) Four of the mailings included [cryptograms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptogram "Cryptogram"); only two have been solved.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-5) The letters were postmarked in San Francisco and [Pleasanton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleasanton,_California "Pleasanton, California").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Read-6)

The Zodiac's confirmed correspondence with date, recipient, and [incipit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incipit "Incipit"):

[July 31st 1969](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_letter,_July_31st_1969 "s:Zodiac Killer letter, July 31st 1969"): _[San Francisco Chronicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San\_Francisco\_Chronicle "San Francisco Chronicle")_, _[San Francisco Examiner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San\_Francisco\_Examiner "San Francisco Examiner")_, and _[Vallejo Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vallejo\_Times\_Herald "Vallejo Times Herald")_. One-third of "Z408 cryptogram" enclosed with each letter. "I am the killer of the 2 teenagers last Christmass..."
2.   [August 4th 1969](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_letter,_August_4th_1969 "s:Zodiac Killer letter, August 4th 1969"): _Examiner_. "This is the Zodiac speaking."
3.   [October 13th 1969](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_letter,_October_13th_1969 "s:Zodiac Killer letter, October 13th 1969"): _Chronicle_. Swatch of Paul Stine's shirt. "I am the murderer of the taxi driver..."
4.   [November 8th 1969](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_letter,_November_8th_1969 "s:Zodiac Killer letter, November 8th 1969"): _Chronicle_. "Z340 cryptogram." The "Dripping Pen" card. "I though you would need a good laugh..."

6.   [December 20th 1969](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_letter,_December_20th_1969 "s:Zodiac Killer letter, December 20th 1969"): [Melvin Belli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melvin_Belli "Melvin Belli"). Swatch of Stine's shirt. "...happy Christmass."

11.   [July 26th 1970](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_letter,_July_26th_1970 "s:Zodiac Killer letter, July 26th 1970"): _Chronicle_. "Being that you will not wear some nice ⌖ buttons..."

### Lake Herman Road murders

[![Image 8](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/de/D.A.F.B.LJ.Lake_Herman_Road_1968_A.jpg/250px-D.A.F.B.LJ.Lake_Herman_Road_1968_A.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:D.A.F.B.LJ.Lake_Herman_Road_1968_A.jpg)

David Arthur Faraday and Betty Lou Jensen

The first murders retroactively attributed to the Zodiac were the shootings of high school students Betty Lou Jensen (16) and David Arthur Faraday (17) on December 20, 1968. Faraday was a student at [Vallejo High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vallejo_High_School "Vallejo High School"), while Jensen was a student at Hogan High School. At 8:30 p.m. Faraday picked up Jensen, and the couple visited one of Jensen's friends. Sometime after 9 p.m., they drove to the outskirts of Vallejo and parked at a [lover's lane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lovers%27_lane "Lovers' lane") on Lake Herman Road, (coordinates: 38.09491126839322, −122.14408650431645), just inside the [Benicia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benicia,_California "Benicia, California") city limits. Between 10:15 and 10:30 p.m., a passing motorist noticed the couple parked on a gravel runoff near the gate to a water pumping station. The couple was spotted again at 11 p.m.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Ripper-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-KN-8): 30–1

Between 11:05 and 11:10 p.m., Faraday and Jensen were attacked. Police determined that their assailant parked his vehicle about ten feet alongside the passenger side of Faraday's car. He fired several shots at Faraday's car as he walked around to the driver's side. None of the shots hit Faraday and Jensen. The couple scrambled to get out through the passenger door; Jensen succeeded. As Faraday was exiting, the killer shot him in the head with a [.22-caliber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/.22_caliber ".22 caliber") pistol. The assailant chased Jensen as she fled, firing six shots at her back. Only one missed. Police theorized the whole attack took two to three minutes.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-KN-8): 30–1 [[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Grey-9)

At 11:10 p.m., a motorist spotted the couple's bodies and alerted police. Jensen was dead. Faraday was still breathing. He died at the hospital. There were no witnesses and no usable tire or foot prints. The only motive the police could deduce was a "madman" wanting to kill. Despite an intense investigation in the following months, no viable suspects emerged.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-KN-8): 30–2  The murders were extensively covered by the media.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-KN-8): 37–8

### Blue Rock Springs murder

[![Image 9](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/14/Darlene_Ferrin_Zodiac_Killer_Ventura_County_Star_19_October_1969.jpg/250px-Darlene_Ferrin_Zodiac_Killer_Ventura_County_Star_19_October_1969.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Darlene_Ferrin_Zodiac_Killer_Ventura_County_Star_19_October_1969.jpg)

Darlene Ferrin

Darlene Ferrin (22) and Michael Mageau (19) were shot shortly after midnight on July 4, 1969. Ferrin was popular in Vallejo due to her job at a local restaurant, where she met Mageau. On July 4, they went on a date despite the fact that Ferrin was married. After 11:30 p.m., Ferrin received a phone call at her house. She arrived at Mageau's house around 11:50 p.m.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-KN-8): 32–5

Immediately after leaving Mageau's house, the couple noticed they were being followed by a man in a light-colored car. Ferrin drove out of Vallejo in the direction of Lake Herman Road. Shortly before midnight, she turned her car into an empty parking lot at Blue Rock Springs Park.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Fagan-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-LAMag-11) This was another lover's lane, located just two miles from Lake Herman Road. Ferrin either parked or stalled 70 feet from the lot entrance.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Grays-12): 26  Another vehicle parked about 80 feet to their left. The driver turned his headlights off and sat motionless. Mageau asked who the driver was. Ferrin told him not to worry. The stranger abruptly tore away from the parked couple.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-KN-8): 34

Five minutes later, the stranger returned, parked a few feet next to Mageau's side of the car and got out. He shone a flashlight into Ferrin's car as he approached. Assuming he was a police officer, the couple rolled down Mageau's window. Without speaking, the stranger fired a [9mm pistol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9_mm_caliber "9 mm caliber") into the car.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-DailyDem-13) One bullet hit Mageau in the right arm, and the other hit Ferrin in the neck. Mageau tried to leave the car, but his door handle was missing or removed. The assailant returned to his car, opened the door, and did something Mageau could not see. As Mageau struggled to exit the vehicle, the stranger shot him and Ferrin two more times each. The killer hurried into his car and drove off. A golf course caretaker heard the shots around 12:10 a.m.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-KN-8): 34–5  The perpetrator left no clues that could be traced back to him.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-KN-8): 38

Three teenagers drove into the parking lot, saw the wounded couple, and got help. Police arrived at 12:20 a.m. Twenty minutes later, Ferrin was pronounced dead at the hospital. Mageau survived and described the attacker as a heavyset white man, around 5'8" tall. He estimated the assailant's weight as 195–200 pounds, with a large face and curly light brown hair. The killer wore dark clothes and no glasses. These details were not enough to develop a suspect.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-KN-8): 35, 41  Moments after 12:40 a.m., the Vallejo Police Department (VPD) received a phone call from a [payphone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Payphone "Payphone") two blocks from headquarters. The man on the other end of the line said:

> "I want to report a double murder. If you go one mile east on Columbus Parkway to the public park you will find kids in a brown car. They were shot with a 9-millimeter [Luger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luger_pistol "Luger pistol"). I also killed those kids last year. Goodbye."[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-KN-8): 35, 39

Serial killers will commonly pause to reflect on their actions. Authors Michael Kelleher and David Van Nuys speculated that the seven months between the attacks on [Lake Herman Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#Lake_Herman_Road_Murders) and at Blue Rock Springs was a "cooling off period" for the Zodiac.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-KN-8): 37–8

#### Ferrin–Zodiac prior relationship theory

[![Image 10](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/b/ba/Ferrin_and_unknown_man%2C_1960s.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ferrin_and_unknown_man,_1960s.jpg)

A 1966 photo of Ferrin and a man who resembles the Zodiac composite sketch from the Stine murder.

Many have speculated that Darlene Ferrin knew her killer. Kelleher and Nuys credit the origin of the theory to [Robert Graysmith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Graysmith "Robert Graysmith")'s 1986 book _[Zodiac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac\_(true\_crime\_book) "Zodiac (true crime book)")_. He argued extensively for a connection based on interviews with Ferrin's friends.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Grays-12): 39ff  A definitive connection has not been proven.

Mageau gave conflicting accounts on whether Ferrin knew her killer. At the hospital, he stated he did not know the murderer. At another point, he said the assailant's name was "Richard". Ferrin's sister claimed one of Darlene's boyfriends was named Richard.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-14) In the Zodiac's later correspondence, he only ever refers to Ferrin as "girl".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-KN-8): 32, 35–6

In Graysmith's telling, Ferrin and Mageau were chased. They only stopped when their car hit a log and stalled. The detective on the scene noticed that the car was still on and in low gear.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Grays-12): 31  Kelleher and Nuys suggest that Ferrin would not tell Mageau to ignore the mystery driver, nor would they assume he was a police officer, if they had not stopped at the spot by choice.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-KN-8): 36–7

Ferrin did know Betty Lou Jensen and David Faraday. She lived less than two blocks from Jensen and attended Hogan High School. She was also familiar with Lake Herman Road's status as a lover's lane.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-KN-8): 32–3  There is a picture of Ferrin and an unknown man who closely resembles a [composite sketch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Composite_sketch "Composite sketch") of the Zodiac. In a 2011 episode of _[America's Most Wanted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America%27s\_Most\_Wanted "America's Most Wanted")_, police stated they believe the photo was taken in San Francisco in either 1966 or 1967.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-15)

### First letters from the Zodiac

[![Image 11: Wikisource logo](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4c/Wikisource-logo.svg/40px-Wikisource-logo.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Wikisource-logo.svg)

English [Wikisource](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikisource "Wikisource") has original text related to this article:

[![Image 12](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/67/Zodiac_Killer_letter%2C_San_Francisco_Chronicle%2C_July_31st_1969.pdf/page1-250px-Zodiac_Killer_letter%2C_San_Francisco_Chronicle%2C_July_31st_1969.pdf.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Zodiac_Killer_letter,_San_Francisco_Chronicle,_July_31st_1969.pdf)

[Zodiac letter](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_letter,_San_Francisco_Chronicle,_July_31,_1969 "s:Zodiac Killer letter, San Francisco Chronicle, July 31, 1969") to the _[San Francisco Chronicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San\_Francisco\_Chronicle "San Francisco Chronicle")_, August 1, 1969.

On August 1, 1969, the _[Vallejo Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vallejo\_Times\_Herald "Vallejo Times Herald")_, _[San Francisco Chronicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San\_Francisco\_Chronicle "San Francisco Chronicle")_ and _[San Francisco Examiner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San\_Francisco\_Examiner "San Francisco Examiner")_ all received letters written by someone taking credit for the attacks in Vallejo. [The three letters](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_letter,_San_Francisco_Chronicle,_July_31st_1969 "s:Zodiac Killer letter, San Francisco Chronicle, July 31st 1969") were nearly identical and began, "I am the killer of the 2 teenagers last Christmass at [Lake Herman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#Lake_Herman_Road_Murders)& the [girl last 4th of July](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#Blue_Rock_Springs_Murder)." The three letters were rife with misspellings and presented the first definitive link between the two separate attacks in Vallejo.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Zoellner-2000-17)

Enclosed in all three letters was a different [cryptogram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptogram "Cryptogram"). They combined to form a 408-symbol [cipher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cipher "Cipher") (**Z408**). The writer claimed, "In this cipher is my idenity. [_[sic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sic "Sic")_]" He demanded the codes be printed on each newspaper's front page. If they were not, he threatened to "cruise around all weekend killing lone people in the night then move on to kill again, until I end up with a dozen people over the weekend."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Grays-12): 49  The _Chronicle_ published its third of the cryptogram inside the August 2 edition. In the accompanying article, Vallejo Police Chief Jack E. Stiltz said, "We're not satisfied that the letter was written by the murderer". He requested the killer send more facts to prove his identity.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-18)

On August 4, the _Examiner_ received [a letter](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_letter,_August_4th_1969 "s:Zodiac Killer letter, August 4th 1969") with the salutation, "Dear Editor This is the Zodiac speaking." This letter marked the debut of the Zodiac persona.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-CB-19): 161  It was the first time the killer called himself by this nickname.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-20)

In this second letter to the media, the killer wrote at much greater length. He happily obliged Chief Stiltz's request for more information about both murders. He provided minute details about how he shot Michael Mageau. He described the golf course caretaker. Regarding the Lake Herman Road attack, he revealed that he had taped a flashlight to his gun in order to aim easily in the dark. The August 4 letter also referred investigators back to the Z408 cipher. The killer wrote, "when they do crack it they will have me".[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Grays-12): 55–57

[![Image 13](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ae/Zodiac_Killer_cipher_deciphered_by_Donald_and_Bettye_Harden.pdf/page1-250px-Zodiac_Killer_cipher_deciphered_by_Donald_and_Bettye_Harden.pdf.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Zodiac_Killer_cipher_deciphered_by_Donald_and_Bettye_Harden.pdf)

Part 1 of Z408 cipher and its decryption by Donald and Bettye Harden. ([Parts 2 & 3](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/ae/Zodiac_Killer_cipher_deciphered_by_Donald_and_Bettye_Harden.pdf))

The decoded message did not reveal the Zodiac's identity. Both the [Federal Bureau of Investigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Bureau_of_Investigation "Federal Bureau of Investigation") (FBI) and [Central Intelligence Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Intelligence_Agency "Central Intelligence Agency") (CIA) attempted to decrypt the Z408 cipher. On August 5, it was cracked by Donald and Bettye Harden, a couple in [Salinas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salinas,_California "Salinas, California"). Neither was a cryptologist. Bettye deployed a [crib](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Known-plaintext_attack "Known-plaintext attack") by correctly guessing the word "kill" would appear in the message.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-CB-19): 162ff

The message was rife with misspellings and referred to [Richard Connell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Connell "Richard Connell")'s 1924 short story "[The Most Dangerous Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Most_Dangerous_Game "The Most Dangerous Game")". The Zodiac explained killing was a way of collecting slaves for his [afterlife](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afterlife "Afterlife"). The full text of the decoded Z408 cipher reads:

> "I like killing people because it is so much fun it is more fun than killing wild game in the forrest because man is the most dangeroue anamal of all to kill something gives me the most thrilling experence it is even better than getting your rocks off with a girl the best part of it is thae when I die I will be reborn in paradice and all the I have killed will become my slaves I will not give you my name because you will try to sloi down or atop my collectiog of slaves for my afterlife ebeorietemethhpiti"[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Grays-12): 54–5

VPD asked a psychiatrist at the [California Medical Facility](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Medical_Facility "California Medical Facility") in [Vacaville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vacaville "Vacaville") to analyze the Zodiac's message. The doctor concluded the writer felt omnipotent based on his fantasy about collecting spiritual slaves. The analysis described the Zodiac as "someone you would expect to be brooding and [isolated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_isolation "Social isolation")". The psychiatrist speculated the killer's praise of murder over sex could be "an expression of inadequacy".[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Smith-21)

### Lake Berryessa murder

[![Image 14](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8d/Lake_Berryessa%2C_California%2C_looking_northeast_from_Oak_Shore.jpg/250px-Lake_Berryessa%2C_California%2C_looking_northeast_from_Oak_Shore.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Lake_Berryessa,_California,_looking_northeast_from_Oak_Shore.jpg)

[Lake Berryessa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Berryessa "Lake Berryessa")

At 4:00 p.m. on September 27, 1969, [Pacific Union College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Union_College "Pacific Union College") students Bryan Hartnell (20) and Cecelia Shepard (22) were picnicking at [Lake Berryessa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Berryessa "Lake Berryessa") on a small island connected by a sand spit to Twin Oak Ridge. Sometime later, Shepard noticed a man watching them. When he emerged from behind a tree, he put on a black [executioner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executioner "Executioner")'s hood with clip-on sunglasses.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Dorgan-22) He wore a [bib](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bib_(garment) "Bib (garment)") with a white 3x3" [![Image 15](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f4/Zodiac_Killer_symbol.svg/20px-Zodiac_Killer_symbol.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Zodiac_Killer_symbol.svg) symbol on it. He brandished a gun, which Hartnell believed was a [.45](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/.45_ACP ".45 ACP"). The Zodiac said he escaped from jail after killing a guard and needed their car and money to travel to Mexico.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Beck-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Flaherty-24): 20

Before tying up Shepard, the Zodiac made Shepard bind Hartnell with precut lengths of plastic clothesline. He tightened Hartnell's bonds because Shepard's knots were too loose. Hartnell still believed they were being robbed when the Zodiac drew a knife and stabbed them. Hartnell suffered six wounds and Shepard ten.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Smith-21)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-25)

[![Image 16](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Door_of_Bryan_Hartnell%27s_car.jpg/250px-Door_of_Bryan_Hartnell%27s_car.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Door_of_Bryan_Hartnell%27s_car.jpg)

Photo of Bryan Hartnell's car door, where the Zodiac tallied his crimes

The Zodiac hiked 500 yards to Knoxville Road, leaving several footprints for investigators to study. The killer drew the [![Image 17](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f4/Zodiac_Killer_symbol.svg/20px-Zodiac_Killer_symbol.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Zodiac_Killer_symbol.svg) symbol on Hartnell's car door with a black felt-tip pen and wrote beneath it:

> Vallejo
> 
>  12-20-68
> 
>  7-4-69
> 
>  Sept 27–69–6:30
> 
>  by knife[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Napa-26)

After hearing the victims' screams, a fisherman and his son sought help. Hartnell untied Shepard's ropes with his teeth, and she freed him.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Grays-12): 73  Two [park rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_ranger "Park ranger") arrived and tended to the stricken couple until the ambulance arrived. Napa County deputies Dave Collins and Ray Land responded to the report of the attack.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Dorgan-22) Shepard was conscious and gave a detailed description of their attacker. She and Hartnell were taken to a hospital in [Napa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napa,_California "Napa, California"). Shepard lapsed into a [coma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coma "Coma") during transport; she never regained consciousness and died two days later. Hartnell survived to recount his tale to the press.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-28)

[![Image 18](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/92/Lake_Berryessa_Sketch_of_the_Zodiac_Killer_as_described_by_3_coeds_sunbathing_that_day.jpg/250px-Lake_Berryessa_Sketch_of_the_Zodiac_Killer_as_described_by_3_coeds_sunbathing_that_day.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Lake_Berryessa_Sketch_of_the_Zodiac_Killer_as_described_by_3_coeds_sunbathing_that_day.jpg)

Witness sketch of man seen at Lake Berryessa shortly before the murder

Earlier that day, a suspicious man had been seen around Lake Berryessa by several people. A dentist and his son saw a heavyset man looking at them from a distance before he hurried off. Around 2:50 p.m., three women noticed a strange man as they stopped on their way to Lake Berryessa. After they had arrived to [sunbathe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunbathing "Sunbathing"), they noticed the man again.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Grays-12): 63f  Since they had potentially seen the Zodiac without his hood, the women worked with _[Napa Valley Register](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napa\_Valley\_Register "Napa Valley Register")_ photographer Robert McKenzie to create a composite sketch using an Identi-Kit [facial compositing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facial_composite "Facial composite") device. Police showed the image to other potential witnesses.

The suspect was described as being roughly 6' tall and weighing 200 pounds, which matched the descriptions by Shepard and Hartnell.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Napa-26)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Grays-12): 78  Graysmith also drew a sketch of the Zodiac's costume after Hartnell described it to him.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-29) Napa County detective Ken Narlow was assigned to the case from the outset and worked on solving the crime until his retirement in 1987.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-30)

The Zodiac drove 27 miles from the crime scene to a car wash in downtown [Napa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napa,_California "Napa, California"). He used a payphone to call the [Napa County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napa_County,_California "Napa County, California") Sheriff's Department at 7:40 p.m. He told the [dispatcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_dispatcher "Police dispatcher") he wished to "report a murder – no, a double murder" and confessed to the crime.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Napa-26) He did not hang up the phone.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Flaherty-24): 21 [KVON](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KVON "KVON") radio reporter Pat Stanley found the phone off the hook a few minutes later. The payphone was located a few blocks from the sheriff's office. Detectives lifted a wet [palm print](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_print "Palm print") from the phone but were never able to match it to any suspect.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Stanley-31)

### Presidio Heights murder

[![Image 19](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/Zodiac_Paul_Stine_Washington_and_Cherry_Presidio_Heights_October_11_1969.jpg/250px-Zodiac_Paul_Stine_Washington_and_Cherry_Presidio_Heights_October_11_1969.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Zodiac_Paul_Stine_Washington_and_Cherry_Presidio_Heights_October_11_1969.jpg)

Crime scene image at Washington and Cherry Street, October 11, 1969

The last confirmed Zodiac murder took place two weeks after the Lake Berryessa attacks. Around 9:40 p.m. on October 11 in [downtown San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_San_Francisco "Downtown San Francisco"), the Zodiac hailed a cab which was driven by a doctoral student named Paul Stine. The killer gave a destination in [Presidio Heights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neighborhoods_in_San_Francisco,_California#Presidio_Heights "Neighborhoods in San Francisco, California"). When the taxi arrived at Washington and Maple streets, the killer asked to be driven another block. At Washington and Cherry around 9:55 p.m., the Zodiac shot Stine in the head with a handgun and took his wallet and car keys.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Zoellner-2000-17)

Three teenagers witnessed the crime from a house directly across the street from Stine's cab. The Zodiac's face was clearly visible by streetlight.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Dowd-32) The teenagers watched as the Zodiac wiped down the vehicle and rifled through Stine's clothes. He left behind two partial [fingerprints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fingerprint "Fingerprint") from his right hand. While the Zodiac was tending to the cab, the kids called the [San Francisco Police Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Police_Department "San Francisco Police Department") (SFPD). They described the criminal as a "husky" white man in a "dark or black jacket". The [dispatcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_dispatcher "Police dispatcher") mistakenly alerted SFPD that the suspect was [Black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_people "Black people").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-KN-8): 76–7

Just two minutes after the call to SFPD, two nearby patrol officers responded to the radio dispatch. They encountered a white man in dark clothes walking north towards the [Presidio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidio_of_San_Francisco "Presidio of San Francisco") army base. They pulled alongside the man and asked if he had seen anything suspicious. The man confirmed he had seen someone waving a gun and heading east. The officers hurried away. The Zodiac later claimed he was the witness that spoke to the two officers. When police arrived at the scene, Stine was declared dead. SFPD canvassed the area, including the Presidio. The Zodiac had probably fled the area in a car by then.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-KN-8): 77–8

[![Image 20](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8e/Oct_1969_Zodiac_wanted_poster.png/330px-Oct_1969_Zodiac_wanted_poster.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Oct_1969_Zodiac_wanted_poster.png)

October 1969 SFPD poster featuring initial sketch made from the teenagers' description (_left_), and one based on the officers' description of the man they encountered (_right_).[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Dowd-32)

Police assumed the murder was a result of the robbery. However, the Zodiac mailed a bloody piece of Paul Stine's shirt to the _San Francisco Chronicle_ on October 13.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Flaherty-24): 27  He enclosed it in [a letter](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_letter,_October_13th_1969 "s:Zodiac Killer letter, October 13th 1969") where he boasted about the murder and claimed to have clandestinely watched SFPD search for him. The Zodiac also threatened to shoot a tire on a [school bus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/School_bus "School bus") and kill children as they exited.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Zoellner-2000-17)

The teenage witnesses helped a police artist make a [composite sketch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facial_composite "Facial composite") of the man they saw at Stine's cab. The two patrol officers who questioned the witness near the scene realized it may have been the Zodiac. They also helped develop a sketch of the suspect.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Dowd-32)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-KN-8): 78

SFPD detectives Bill Armstrong and [Dave Toschi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Toschi "Dave Toschi") were assigned to the case.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-KN-8): 78  Toschi ended up working on the case by himself and filled eight filing cabinets with potential suspects.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-33) In 1976, he told the [Associated Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_Press "Associated Press") that Zodiac's letters were an "ego game". He believed the killer lived in the [San Francisco Bay Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Bay_Area "San Francisco Bay Area"), "He's a weekend killer. Why can't he get away Monday through Thursday? Does his job keep him close to home? I would speculate he maybe has a menial job, is well thought of and blends into the crowd...I think he's quite intelligent and better educated than someone who misspells words as frequently as he does in his letters."[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Toschi76-34)

After working on the Zodiac case for seven years, Toschi started writing anonymous letters praising his own investigative work to _Chronicle_ columnist [Armistead Maupin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armistead_Maupin "Armistead Maupin"). Two years later in 1978, Toschi was removed from the case and demoted to [pawn shop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pawnbroker "Pawnbroker") detail. He expressed regret for the hoax. That same year, Maupin also received a purported Zodiac letter. SFPD investigated whether Toschi wrote it as well and concluded he did not.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-36)

### _A.M. San Francisco_ interview

On October 22, 1969, mental patient Eric Weill duped attorney [Melvin Belli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melvin_Belli "Melvin Belli") into a conversation on [KGO-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KGO-TV "KGO-TV")'s _A.M. San Francisco_. Investigators concluded Weill was not the Zodiac. He called the [Oakland Police Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakland_Police_Department "Oakland Police Department") and demanded to speak to Belli or [F. Lee Bailey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F._Lee_Bailey "F. Lee Bailey") on television. During the show, while using the name "Sam", Weill told Belli he would not reveal his identity for fear of being executed. He arranged a rendezvous with Belli on [Mission Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mission_Street "Mission Street") in [Daly City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daly_City "Daly City") and did not show.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-37)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Flaherty-24): 32

### November & December 1969 correspondence

[![Image 21](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e3/4abc_-_San_Francisco_Chronicle_Dripping_Pen_Card_November_8_1969_340_Cipher_COLOR.jpg/250px-4abc_-_San_Francisco_Chronicle_Dripping_Pen_Card_November_8_1969_340_Cipher_COLOR.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:4abc_-_San_Francisco_Chronicle_Dripping_Pen_Card_November_8_1969_340_Cipher_COLOR.jpg)

The Zodiac's Z340 cypher, November 8, 1969

On November 8, the Zodiac mailed [a card with a 340-character cryptogram](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_letter,_November_8th_1969 "s:Zodiac Killer letter, November 8th 1969") (**Z340**) to the _Chronicle_. He asked for his code to be printed on the front page. It remained unsolved for 51 years. One cryptologist ranked Zodiac's unsolved ciphers second only to the [Voynich manuscript](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voynich_manuscript "Voynich manuscript").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-38) Zodiac ciphers were [crowdsourced](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowdsourcing "Crowdsourcing") through a variety of websites, which led to gradual breakthroughs.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-JG-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-340z-40)

Z340 was deciphered by an international team of private citizens on December 5, 2020. The cryptology group included American [software engineer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_engineering "Software engineering") David Oranchak, Australian [mathematician](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematician "Mathematician") Sam Blake and Belgian programmer Jarl Van Eycke.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Canon-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Ong-42) Using a program made by Van Eycke called AZdecrypt, the team ran 650,000 possible solutions for the cipher until the program came up with the best possible [encryption key](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Key_(cryptography) "Key (cryptography)").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-NYT21-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-44)

In the decrypted message, the Zodiac denied being the "Sam" who spoke on _A.M. San Francisco_ and explained he was not afraid of the [gas chamber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gas_chamber "Gas chamber") "because it will send me to paradice all the sooner." The team submitted their findings to the FBI's Cryptographic and Racketeering Records Unit, which verified the decryption and concluded the decoded message gave no further clues to the Zodiac's identity.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Canon-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Ong-42)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-SFChron3.16.21-45) Subsequent analysis confirmed the Z340 decryption using [unicity distance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unicity_distance "Unicity distance") as a measure.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-JG-39)

The decoded Z340 cipher included the usual Zodiac respellings:

> "I hope you are having lots of fan in trying to catch me that wasn't me on the TV show which bringo up a point about me I am not afraid of the gas chamber becaase it will send me to paradlce all the sooher because e now have enough slaves to worv for me where every one else has nothing when they reach paradice so they are afraid of death I am not afraid because i vnow that my new life is life will be an easy one in paradice death"[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-SFChron3.16.21-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-46)

[![Image 22](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/44/Normal_5a_-_San_Francisco_Chronicle_letter_November_9_1969_Page_1.jpg/250px-Normal_5a_-_San_Francisco_Chronicle_letter_November_9_1969_Page_1.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Normal_5a_-_San_Francisco_Chronicle_letter_November_9_1969_Page_1.jpg)

### January 1974 letter

Zodiac remained silent for nearly three years. The _Chronicle_ received a [letter from the Zodiac](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_letter,_January_29th_1974 "s:Zodiac Killer letter, January 29th 1974"), postmarked January 29, 1974 from [San Mateo County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Mateo_County,_California "San Mateo County, California").
