### January 1974 letter

Zodiac remained silent for nearly three years. The _Chronicle_ received a [letter from the Zodiac](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_letter,_January_29th_1974 "s:Zodiac Killer letter, January 29th 1974"), postmarked January 29, 1974 from [San Mateo County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Mateo_County,_California "San Mateo County, California"). It praised _[The Exorcist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Exorcist "The Exorcist")_ (1973) as "the best [saterical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satire "Satire") comidy [_sic_] that I have ever seen." The letter included part of a verse from "Tit-willow Song" in _[The Mikado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Mikado "The Mikado")_ and an unusual symbol at the bottom that has remained unexplained. Zodiac concluded the letter with a new score, "Me = 37, SFPD = 0."[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Zoellner-2000-17)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Bee74-61)

Psychiatrist David Van Nuys theorized Zodiac stopped killing because he had [multiple personality disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiple_personality_disorder "Multiple personality disorder"). It may have lessened over time as it often can, which would also explain the reduced intensity of Zodiac's letters.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Taylor-62)

## Letters of suspicious authorship

Many more unconfirmed Zodiac letters were sent to the media. On August 1, 1973, a letter was mailed to the _[Albany Times Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albany\_Times\_Union "Albany Times Union")_ in [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_(state) "New York (state)"). The return address was the [![Image 35](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f4/Zodiac_Killer_symbol.svg/20px-Zodiac_Killer_symbol.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Zodiac_Killer_symbol.svg) symbol. The writer promised to kill again on August 10. A three-line code in the letter was supposed to reveal the name and location of the victim. FBI [cryptanalysts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptanalysis "Cryptanalysis") deciphered the code as "[redacted by the FBI] [Albany Medical Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albany_Medical_Center "Albany Medical Center"). This is only the beginning." No murder matched the details in the letter, and the handwriting was not a definitive match for Zodiac's.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-HISTORY-2023a-3)

The _Chronicle_ received a letter postmarked [February 14, 1974](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_letter,_Feb_14th_1974 "s:Zodiac Killer letter, Feb 14th 1974"), explaining that the [Symbionese Liberation Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symbionese_Liberation_Army "Symbionese Liberation Army")'s initials spelled out an [Old Norse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Norse "Old Norse") word meaning "kill." The SLA had recently kidnapped newspaper heiress [Patricia Hearst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patricia_Hearst "Patricia Hearst").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-HISTORY-2023a-3)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-63) The handwriting was not authenticated as the Zodiac's.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-64)

A [letter to the _Chronicle_](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_letter,_May_8th_1974 "s:Zodiac Killer letter, May 8th 1974") postmarked May 8, 1974, opined that _[Badlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badlands\_(film) "Badlands (film)")_ (1973) was "murder-glorification" and asked the paper to remove its advertisements. Signed by "A citizen", the handwriting, tone and sarcasm were similar to Zodiac's letters. The _Chronicle_ also received an anonymous letter [postmarked July 8, 1974](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_letter,_July_8th_1974 "s:Zodiac Killer letter, July 8th 1974"), complaining about [antifeminist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antifeminism "Antifeminism") columnist Marco Spinelli. The letter was signed, "the Red Phantom (red with rage)".[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Flaherty-24): 44

A letter arrived at the San Francisco Chronicle, postmarked May 6, 1986, with the author claiming to have killed 100+ people across California and Nevada.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-65) On October 27, 1987, the [Vallejo Times Herald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vallejo_Times_Herald "Vallejo Times Herald") received a correspondence, with the author saying they will be "out driving around on Halloween in my death machine looking for some kiddies to run over". The authorship of these two letters is debated.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-66)

In 2007, an [American Greetings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Greetings "American Greetings")[Christmas card](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_card "Christmas card") was discovered in the _Chronicle_'s photo files. Its postmark was from 1990 in [Eureka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eureka,_California "Eureka, California"). The card was handed over to the Vallejo police. A photocopy of two [United States Post Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Post_Office "United States Post Office") keys on a magnet key chain was enclosed. The handwriting on the envelope resembled Zodiac's; however, a forensic document examiner deemed it inauthentic. The discovery electrified Zodiac researchers. It suggested the killing spree may not have been stopped by death or imprisonment and that the Zodiac might be alive.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-67)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-68)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Harris-2007-69)

## Other possible victims

There is no consensus regarding the number of victims the Zodiac Killer killed or the length of his criminal spree. In 1976, SFPD detective [Dave Toschi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Toschi "Dave Toschi") said, "We know for sure he killed at least six", and the Zodiac had "a personal [boxscore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Box_score "Box score") of 37".[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Toschi76-34) Robert Graysmith estimated 49 Zodiac victims.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Grays-12): 308–11  Many murders and attacks in the 1960s and 1970s were seen as possible Zodiac crimes, but none have been confirmed.

### Raymond Davis

On April 9, 1962, a man called the police in [Oceanside](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oceanside,_California "Oceanside, California"), California, and said, "I am going to pull something here in Oceanside and you'll never be able to figure it out." At 11:10 p.m. on April 10, cab driver Raymond Davis (29) told his dispatcher he was taking a fare to South Oceanside. The next day, his body was found near the mayor's house in St. Malo, a [gated community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gated_community "Gated community") in Oceanside.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Harrison-70)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-71) Days later, the suspected killer called the police again, “Do you remember me calling you last week and telling you that I was going to pull a real baffling crime? I killed the cab driver and I am going to get me a bus driver next.” Following this call, the police began to place armed guards on buses.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-KGTV-72)

In 2019, the unsolved murder was connected to the Zodiac when Kristi Hawthorne, the Director of the Oceanside Historical Society, was researching St. Malo for another project. She stumbled upon a story about Davis' murder and further research dug up several parallels to the Zodiac killings. Davis' murder foreshadowed [Paul Stine's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#Presidio_Heights_murder) by 7 years. Both cabbie murders involved wealthy neighborhoods. Both victims were 29 years old. The ammunition was .22 caliber, which matches the Lake Herman Road attack. The taunting of police and the threat against buses also mirrored previous Zodiac behavior.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Lombardo-73)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Harrison-70)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-74) Hawthorne presented her findings to the Oceanside Police Department, which began an inquiry.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-KGTV-72)

### Robert Domingos and Linda Edwards

On June 2, 1963, on the beach at [Tajiguas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tajiguas,_California "Tajiguas, California") in [Santa Barbara County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Barbara_County,_California "Santa Barbara County, California"), California, an unidentified [sniper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sniper "Sniper") fired two shots from a .22 caliber gun at a group of teenagers. None of them were hit.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Lompoc-75) On June 4, on a beach within [Gaviota State Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaviota_State_Park "Gaviota State Park"), just west of Tajiguas, Robert George Domingos (18) and his fiancée Linda Faye Edwards (17) were shot dead by an unidentified person. They were at the beach while skipping school at [Lompoc High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lompoc_High_School "Lompoc High School") for [Senior Ditch Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senior_Skip_Day "Senior Skip Day").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Grey-9)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-BB-76) On June 5, when the couple had not returned home, their parents called the police. During a police search, several of the couple's belongings, like Edwards' purse, were inside Domingos' car.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Oakland-77)[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-LAT63-78)

Police believed that the assailant attempted to bind the couple with pre-cut rope. This was the same _[modus operandi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modus\_operandi "Modus operandi")_ as the [Lake Berryessa attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#Lake_Berryessa_murder).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Grey-9) It is likely that when the victims got loose and tried to flee, the killer shot them repeatedly in the back and chest. Domingos was shot 11 times and Edwards 8 times.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Oakland-77) The killer placed their bodies in a small shack nearby, and tried to burn it to the ground.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-BB-76) The firearm was probably a .22 caliber [semi-automatic rifle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semi-automatic_firearm "Semi-automatic firearm"), like the Tajiguas and [Lake Herman Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#Lake_Herman_Road_murders) incidents.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Minsky-79)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-BB-76) The [Winchester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winchester_Repeating_Arms_Company "Winchester Repeating Arms Company") Western Super X copper-coated bullets also matched the Zodiac's.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-BB-76) The [lot number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lot_number "Lot number") of the .22 ammunition was traced to an April purchase from a store in [Santa Barbara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Barbara,_California "Santa Barbara, California"). The only other place that lot number turned up was at [Vandenberg Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vandenberg_Space_Force_Base "Vandenberg Space Force Base") near [Lompoc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lompoc,_California "Lompoc, California"). Investigators looked into purchases of the ammunition at both locations.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Lompoc-75)

In a 1972 press conference, Santa Barbara County Sheriff John Carpenter stated "there now appears to be a high degree of probability" that the Zodiac committed the murders,[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-80) and "although the anticipated response to this statement would be one of skepticism, let me say that we do not make this assertion frivolously."[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-81)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Minsky-79) When SFPD detectives Bill Armstrong and Dave Toschi investigated the murders in 1972, Toschi said a connection is possible.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-82) A classmate of Domingos and Edwards, who later became a [clinical psychologist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinical_psychology "Clinical psychology") and police officer, said in 2011, "I believe the murders were the work of the Zodiac killer, but I can't prove it."[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-BB-76)

### Johnny Ray Swindle and Joyce Ann Swindle

On February 5, 1964, Johnny Ray Swindle and Joyce Ann Swindle (both 19), a newlywed couple from Alabama on their honeymoon, were shot while walking along [Ocean Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocean_Beach,_San_Diego "Ocean Beach, San Diego") in [San Diego](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego "San Diego"). A sniper with a .22 caliber [long rifle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_rifle "Long rifle") shot them five times from a nearby cliff. The killer then shot each of them once in the head at close range. Similar to the Zodiac murders, Johnny was shot behind the ear. Despite multiple bullet wounds, he remained alive for hours and died at the hospital. Joyce died almost instantly from shots to her back, left arm, and head. The killer took Joyce's necklace, as well as Johnny's wallet and [Timex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timex_Group_USA "Timex Group USA") watch—the same brand watch found at the Cheri Jo Bates crime scene, and assumed to belong to Bates' killer.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Grey-9)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Lombardo-73)

Johnny's mother said she could not think of him having any enemies.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-83) His sister theorized the Zodiac may have been the culprit. Police investigated a 51-year-old man living in a nearby beach shack, a teenager alleged by a priest to be violent, and a 19-year-old [Marine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Marine_Corps "United States Marine Corps") from San Diego who killed his parents and sister in Illinois. Police speculated that the Swindles were victims of a "[thrill killer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thrill_killing "Thrill killing")", and they also saw a parallel with the Domingos and Edwards murders.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Grey-9) In both the Santa Barbara and Ocean Beach killings, the victims were shot from a distance, then again at close range.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Both the Ocean Beach and Lake Herman Road murders used a .22 [Remington Arms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Remington_Arms "Remington Arms") Model 550-1 rifle, but the [ballistics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballistics "Ballistics") did not match between the [cartridges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartridge_(firearms) "Cartridge (firearms)") found at the two scenes. The _San Diego Reader_ noted that the murders at Lake Berryessa, Santa Barbara, and Ocean Beach were all near bodies of water.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Lombardo-73)

### Cheri Jo Bates

[![Image 36](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/73/Cheri_Jo_Bates_Crime_Scene_Terracina_Drive_October_31_1966.jpg/250px-Cheri_Jo_Bates_Crime_Scene_Terracina_Drive_October_31_1966.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cheri_Jo_Bates_Crime_Scene_Terracina_Drive_October_31_1966.jpg)

Officers from the [Riverside Police Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverside_Police_Department "Riverside Police Department") examining the Bates crime scene at Terracina Drive, Riverside, in 1966. Bates' body lies at the right of the gravel path.

On October 30, 1966, Cheri Jo Bates, an 18-year-old student at [Riverside City College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverside_City_College "Riverside City College") (RCC), spent the evening at the campus library annex until it closed at 9:00 p.m. Neighbors reported hearing a scream around 10:30. Her father reported her missing, and she was found dead the next morning at 6:30 a.m.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Grey-9) She was found a short distance from the library, between two abandoned houses slated to be demolished for campus renovations. She had been brutally beaten and stabbed to death. The wires in her [Volkswagen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volkswagen "Volkswagen")'s [distributor cap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distributor_cap "Distributor cap") had been pulled out. A man's paint-spattered Timex watch with a torn wristband was found nearby. The watch stopped at 12:24, but police believe that the attack had occurred much earlier.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-84)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Grays-12): 165–6

One month later, on November 29, nearly identical [typewritten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typewriter "Typewriter") letters were mailed to Riverside police and the _[Riverside Press-Enterprise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverside\_Press-Enterprise "Riverside Press-Enterprise")_, titled "The Confession." The author claimed responsibility for the Bates murder, providing details of the crime that were not released to the public. The author warned that Bates "is not the first and she will not be the last."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Grays-12): 168–9

[![Image 37](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9b/Zodiac-confession.jpg/250px-Zodiac-confession.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Zodiac-confession.jpg)

The typewritten confession received by the Riverside Police Department and _[The Press-Enterprise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Press-Enterprise "The Press-Enterprise")_ on November 29, 1966

[![Image 38](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/ZodiacsPoem.jpg/250px-ZodiacsPoem.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ZodiacsPoem.jpg)

In December 1966, a macabre poem was discovered carved into the bottom side of a desktop in the RCC library. Titled "Sick of living/unwilling to die," the poem's language and handwriting resembled that of the Zodiac's letters. It was signed with what were assumed to be a set of lowercase initials (_r h_) inscribed below. During the 1970 investigation, Sherwood Morrill, California's top "questioned documents" examiner, expressed his opinion that the poem was written by the Zodiac.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Grays-12): 170–2

In 1970, Paul Avery wrote an article connecting the Zodiac to Bates' murder. Five months later, on March 13, 1971, the Zodiac mailed a letter to the _Los Angeles Times_, credited the police, instead of Avery, for discovering his "Riverside activity, but they are only finding the easy ones, there are a hell of a lot more down there."[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-85) Zodiac's culpability in Bates' murder is unconfirmed.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-86)

### Enedine Molina and Fermin Rodriguez

On June 8, 1967, Enedine Molina (35) and Fermin Rodriguez (36) were parked on Vallecitos Road in [Alameda County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alameda_County,_California "Alameda County, California"). ### John Franklin Hood and Sandra Garcia

[![Image 39](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a4/East_Beach_%283391461890%29.jpg/250px-East_Beach_%283391461890%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:East_Beach_(3391461890).jpg)

Santa Barbara's [East Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Beach_(Santa_Barbara) "East Beach (Santa Barbara)")

On February 21, 1970, John Franklin Hood (24) and his fiancée, Sandra Garcia (20), visited [East Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Beach_(Santa_Barbara) "East Beach (Santa Barbara)") in Santa Barbara. The couple left their Santa Barbara home at 6 p.m. Early the following day, their fully-clothed bodies were discovered under their blanket. Hood was stabbed eleven times, mainly in the face and back. Garcia received the brunt of the vicious attack, leaving her almost unrecognizable. The bone-handled 4" fish knife used in their murder was partially buried in the sand beneath the blanket. There appeared to be no sexual interference, and robbery was ruled out. The double-murder was similar to the 1963 killing of Domingos and Edwards, thirty miles west. It also paralleled the 1969 [Lake Berryessa attack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#Lake_Berryessa_murder).[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-BB-76)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-88)

### Kathleen Johns

On the night of March 22, 1970, Kathleen Johns (22) was driving to [Petaluma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petaluma,_California "Petaluma, California") with her 10-month-old daughter. Johns was also seven months pregnant.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-89) She left [San Bernardino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Bernardino,_California "San Bernardino, California") at 4:30 p.m. At 11:30 p.m. on [Highway 132](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_State_Route_132 "California State Route 132") near [Patterson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patterson,_California "Patterson, California"), a vehicle behind her blinked its lights. A man pulled alongside and convinced her to pull over because her left rear wheel was loose. He fixed it, but when she pulled away it immediately fell off. Johns told Paul Avery that the man offered to drive her to a gas station that was in sight just up the road.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Avery11.70-90)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-91)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-SFExaminer70-92)

Johns asked the man if he always helped strangers this way. He replied, "By the time I get through with them, they won't need my help." He drove past the gas station and kept Johns captive for two hours. He told her repeatedly, "you know I'm going to kill you". When he abruptly stopped, Johns jumped out of the car with her infant and hid in an irrigation ditch. The man searched for her with a flashlight before leaving. A passing farmer drove Johns to a police station in Patterson. When she saw the Wanted poster from [Paul Stine's murder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#Presidio_Heights_murder), she exclaimed, "Oh my god...that's him".[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Avery11.70-90)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Adams-93): 268  Johns's car was found in flames on Highway 132.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-SFExaminer70-92)[A few months later](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#July_1970_letters), the Zodiac referenced this kidnapping in a [letter to the _Chronicle_](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_letter,_July_24th_1970 "s:Zodiac Killer letter, July 24th 1970").[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-94)

#### Astrological murders

The "Astrological Murders" were committed by a suspected serial killer who was also active in the same region of California and around the same time as the Zodiac. Police across multiple [jurisdictions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurisdiction "Jurisdiction") made a tentative connection between a single culprit and at least a dozen unsolved homicides that occurred between the late 1960s and early 1970s. All of the victims were female and were killed in a variety of ways, including [strangulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strangulation "Strangulation"), drowning, throat-cutting and bludgeoning, occasionally after being drugged. The killings were linked because victims were dumped in ravines and killed in conjunction with [astrological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astrology "Astrology") events, such as the [winter solstice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winter_solstice "Winter solstice"), [equinox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equinox "Equinox") and [Friday the 13th](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friday_the_13th "Friday the 13th").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Grays-12): 309, 311

#### Santa Rosa hitchhiker murders

The Zodiac was also suspected of being the perpetrator behind the "[Santa Rosa hitchhiker murders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_Hitchhiker_Murders "Santa Rosa Hitchhiker Murders")". Between 1972 and 1973, at least seven female hitchhikers were murdered in [Sonoma County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonoma_County,_California "Sonoma County, California") and [Santa Rosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa,_California "Santa Rosa, California").[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Grays2-101): 163  In the Zodiac's January 29, 1974 "Exorcist letter" to the _Chronicle_, he [claims thirty-seven victims](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#Final_Zodiac_letter). A symbol in that letter matched [Chinese characters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_characters "Chinese characters") on a soy barrel carried by one of the Santa Rosa victims. The Zodiac had warned he would vary his _modus operandi_ in [a previous letter](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_letter,_November_9th_1969 "s:Zodiac Killer letter, November 9th 1969"), "when I comitt [_sic_] my murders, they shall look like routine robberies, [killings of anger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_of_passion "Crime of passion"), + a few fake accidents, etc."[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-SFGateZL2-102)

One of the main Zodiac suspects, [Arthur Leigh Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_suspects#Arthur_Leigh_Allen "Zodiac Killer suspects"), was also suspected of being the Santa Rosa killer.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-103)

## 21st-century developments

In 2002, Cydne Holt of the SFPD crime lab developed a partial [DNA profile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_profile "DNA profile") from [saliva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saliva "Saliva") on stamps and envelopes of the Zodiac's letters – especially the stamp on the November 8, 1969, card – for the [ABC News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_News_(United_States) "ABC News (United States)") program _[Primetime Thursday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime\_Thursday "Primetime Thursday")_. The DNA of prime Zodiac suspect Arthur Leigh Allen was not a match; however, Zodiac researcher Tom Voigt claimed that the DNA material was obtained from the front of the stamp and could belong to someone else.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-104)

In April 2004, the SFPD cited caseload pressure and marked the Zodiac case "inactive."[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-105) By March 2007, they reactivated the case.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-106) The case remains open in Riverside and Napa County.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-107)[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-108)

In 2018, the Vallejo Police Department attempted to use [GEDmatch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GEDmatch "GEDmatch") to catch the Zodiac.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-109) They did not receive definitive results.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-110) The FBI's investigation was still ongoing as of 2021,[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-111)[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-112) although Voigt claims the case is no longer being investigated as of 2025.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-113)

## Suspects

In 2009, _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_ reported that the SFPD had investigated an estimated 2,500 Zodiac suspects, and only a half-dozen of them were seen as credible by the department.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Tunzelmann-114)[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-amw.com-115) Richard Grinell, who runs the website Zodiac Ciphers, stated in 2022 that "there are probably 50 or 100 suspects named every year."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-LAMag-11)

The only man ever named by the police as a suspect is [Arthur Leigh Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen "Arthur Leigh Allen"), a former elementary school teacher and convicted [sex offender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_offender "Sex offender") who died in 1992.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Ripper-7)[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-SFCCaseBreakers-116) Allen denied being the Zodiac.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-117) He was interviewed by police from the early days of the investigation, and was subject to several related [search warrants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Search_warrant "Search warrant") over a twenty-year period. In 2007, Robert Graysmith said that several detectives described Allen as the most likely suspect.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-118) In 2010, Dave Toschi stated that all the evidence against Allen ultimately "turned out to be negative."[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-119) Other suspects widely seen as viable by professional or amateur investigators include Earl Van Best Jr., Gary Francis Poste, Giuseppe Bevilacqua, Lawrence Kane, Paul Doerr, Richard Gaikowski, Richard Marshall, and Ross Sullivan.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-120)[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-121)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-LAMag-11)[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-122)

## Legacy

> This is the case that won't go away. The killer's catch-me-if-you-can taunting of police, the mind-puzzlers he sent to the press, the way he dropped off the face of the Earth in the early 1970s combined to give the Zodiac case a legendary status that in some ways outstripped the magnitude of the murders. – Michael Taylor[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Taylor-62)

In 2020, the _Chronicle_ called the Zodiac case "the most famous unsolved murder case in American history."[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-SFChron3.16.21-45) The unusual nature of the spree has sustained international interest for years.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-SFCAnother-123) A cottage industry of "Zodiologists" sprung up in the wake of the killings.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-124) They try to solve the case and have informal annual meetings.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-125)[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-126) Several websites collect information about the crimes and ciphers.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-127)

Dozens of books and documentaries have focused on the Zodiac.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Fagan-10)[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Anguiano-2022-128)[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-129) The original and most influential amateur book was Robert Graysmith's _Zodiac_ (1986). He was working at the _San Francisco Chronicle_ as a cartoonist while the Zodiac was corresponding with the paper. Graysmith compiled his research into an authoritative investigation that remains a touchstone for other researchers.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-CB-19): 193  John Bowman published the book _The Allen Files_, containing Arthur Leigh Allen's military records.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-130) That was followed with _Zodiac Killer: Fact Vs. Fiction_.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-131)

Theories about the Zodiac's identity are rampant. In _Zodiac_, Graysmith refers to Arthur Leigh Allen as "Robert Hall Starr" to protect his identity and avoid [litigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Litigation "Litigation"). In 2002, Graysmith wrote directly about Allen in _Zodiac Unmasked_.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-132) Attributing victims to the Zodiac is also a popular pastime. One Zodiologist has persistently claimed to also be a target of the killer.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-133) Since 2013, accusing [United States Senator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senator "United States Senator")[Ted Cruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Cruz "Ted Cruz") of being the Zodiac has been a [popular Internet meme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Cruz%E2%80%93Zodiac_Killer_meme "Ted Cruz–Zodiac Killer meme").[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-134)

The Zodiac inspired [copycat killers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copycat_killer "Copycat killer") like [Heriberto Seda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heriberto_Seda "Heriberto Seda") in New York City and [Shinichiro Azuma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kobe_child_murders "Kobe child murders") in Japan, both of whom called themselves "the Zodiac".[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-135)[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-136) In 2021, an anonymous author sent letters to media outlets in [Albany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albany,_New_York "Albany, New York") using a "Chinese Zodiac Killer" [sobriquet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sobriquet "Sobriquet").[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Stuti-137)

Brian Draper and Torey Adamcik, who perpetrated the 2006 [murder of Cassie Jo Stoddart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder_of_Cassie_Jo_Stoddart "Murder of Cassie Jo Stoddart"), cited the Zodiac as one of their inspirations in their homemade videos.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-138)

### Popular culture

[![Image 43](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0d/2017_Golden_Gate_Theatre.jpg/250px-2017_Golden_Gate_Theatre.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2017_Golden_Gate_Theatre.jpg)

The [Golden Gate Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Gate_Theatre "Golden Gate Theatre") in San Francisco

The first film about the Zodiac Killer was produced two years after his last confirmed murder during his letter-writing campaign. [Tom Hanson's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Hanson_(American_actor) "Tom Hanson (American actor)")[_The Zodiac Killer_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Zodiac_Killer_(film) "The Zodiac Killer (film)") was made as a scheme to capture the culprit. The film premiered on April 19, 1971, at the [Golden Gate Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Gate_Theatre "Golden Gate Theatre") in San Francisco. The audience were given a survey with the prompt, "I think the Zodiac kills because..." They were asked to complete the sentence and promised the best response would be rewarded with a [Kawasaki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kawasaki_motorcycles "Kawasaki motorcycles") motorcycle.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-139) The audience surveys were secretly compared to the Zodiac's handwriting. Hanson hoped the killer's supposed [egotism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egotism "Egotism") would lure him to the movie, and deployed volunteers to detain anyone whose handwriting matched the Zodiac's.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-140) The scheme lasted for several screenings, and in one, the volunteers actually confronted one potential suspect and held the suspect before releasing him due to lack of evidence.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-141)

The Zodiac has inspired villains in multiple movies, including Scorpio in _[Dirty Harry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirty\_Harry "Dirty Harry")_ (1971), the Gemini Killer in _[The Exorcist III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Exorcist\_III "The Exorcist III")_ (1990), John Doe in [_Seven_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven_(1995_film) "Seven (1995 film)") (1995), and the [Riddler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riddler "Riddler") in [_The Batman_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Batman_(film) "The Batman (film)") (2022).[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-142) The Zodiac case is also the subject of the film _[Zodiac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac\_(film) "Zodiac (film)")_ (2007), directed by [David Fincher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Fincher "David Fincher"), who also directed _Seven_. Fincher grew up in the Bay Area during the Zodiac killings. The film was an adaptation of Robert Graysmith's books,[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-143) focusing on Graysmith and Paul Avery's investigation over 23 years.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-144)[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Tunzelmann-114) The filmmakers extensively researched the case, conducting interviews with people involved in the case. The film posits Arthur Leigh Allen's culpability and led to more public interest in the Zodiac.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Minsky-79)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Harris-2007-69)

**Arthur Leigh Allen** (December 18, 1933 – August 26, 1992) was an American teacher, mechanic, cashier, and convicted child molester, who is best known for being the [prime suspect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_suspects "Zodiac Killer suspects") in the [Zodiac Killer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer "Zodiac Killer") case.

Allen was born in [Honolulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honolulu "Honolulu"), Hawaii, on December 18, 1933. He grew up in [Vallejo, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vallejo,_California "Vallejo, California"), and had a strained relationship with his mother.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-Nucleus-1) Allen entered the [U.S. Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy "United States Navy") on December 13, 1951, and served until his honorable discharge on December 12, 1959. During his time in the navy, he served mostly in the reserves but spent some time on active duty. He served on multiple submarines and earned the China Service Medal for his service in southeast Asia.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-2) On April 4, 1958, Allen faced a special court-martial at Treasure Island for bringing a loaded .45 pistol onto the naval base. He was found not guilty.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-3) Allen attended [California Polytechnic State College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Polytechnic_State_University,_San_Luis_Obispo "California Polytechnic State University, San Luis Obispo"), where he was the California collegiate trampoline champion in 1959.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-4)

In the early 1960s, Allen moved to [Atascadero, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atascadero,_California "Atascadero, California"), where he worked as a teacher and later as a mechanic.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-5) He was fired from his teaching job at an elementary school in March 1968 for molesting a student.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-6)

On October 6, 1969, Allen was interviewed by Detective John Lynch of the Vallejo Police Department. Allen had been reported in the vicinity of the [Lake Berryessa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Berryessa "Lake Berryessa") attack on September 27. He told Lynch that he was going to go to Lake Berryessa but changed his mind and went [scuba diving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuba_diving "Scuba diving") at [Salt Point State Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_Point_State_Park "Salt Point State Park") instead.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-zodiackiller.com-8)

In 1971, Allen's former friend, Donald L. Cheney, reported to [Manhattan Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan_Beach,_California "Manhattan Beach, California") police that Allen had spoken of his desire to kill people, used the name Zodiac, and secured a flashlight to a firearm for visibility at night. Cheney said this conversation occurred no later than January 1, 1969.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-Group-20052-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-10) Allen was interviewed again on August 4, 1971, this time by Detective Mulanax of the Vallejo Police Department and Inspectors Toschi and Bill Armstrong of SFPD.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-Zodiac_Killer_Errors2-11) Allen admitted to having possession of bloody knives the day of the Lake Berryessa attack, claiming he used the knives to “kill a chicken.” He also admitted to being in Riverside during the time of the [murder of Cheri Jo Bates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder_of_Cheri_Jo_Bates "Murder of Cheri Jo Bates"). Allen also talked about a book he enjoyed reading in high school called "[The Most Dangerous Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Most_Dangerous_Game "The Most Dangerous Game")", which is a phrase the Zodiac used in his first solved cipher.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-zodiackiller.com-8) Allen owned and wore a [Zodiac Watch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Watches "Zodiac Watches"), a brand that uses a logo similar to the killer's ![Image 2](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f4/Zodiac_Killer_symbol.svg/40px-Zodiac_Killer_symbol.svg.png) symbol.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-Group-20052-9)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-Beck5-12) Allen and the Zodiac also both had shoes sized 10.5.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-Group-20052-9)

In September 1972, the SFPD obtained a [search warrant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Search_warrant "Search warrant") for Allen's Santa Rosa trailer.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-13) Nothing incriminating was found. The SFPD took samples of Allen's handwriting, as well as obtaining his fingerprints; neither were a definitive match to the Zodiac.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-Group-20052-9)

In 1974, Allen was arrested for lewdness with a nine-year-old boy. After pleading guilty he was sent to [Atascadero State Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atascadero_State_Hospital "Atascadero State Hospital") for pre-sentence evaluation and treatment. On May 13, 1977, Allen was given a [suspended prison sentence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suspended_prison_sentence "Suspended prison sentence") and five years of felony [probation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Probation "Probation"). He completed probation successfully in 1982.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-14) Allen's arrest and sentencing could provide a potential reason for why the Zodiac's communications stopped in 1974.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-15) A possible Zodiac letter was received in 1978, after Allen was released.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-16)

[![Image 3](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a6/Vintage_Sea_Wolf_AdOld.jpg/250px-Vintage_Sea_Wolf_AdOld.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Vintage_Sea_Wolf_AdOld.jpg)

An advertisement for the [Zodiac Watch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Watches "Zodiac Watches"), Allen's watch, which has the same logo as the Zodiac Killer

After an old nemesis of Allen's named Ralph Spinelli told VPD that Allen admitted to him that he was the Zodiac,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-zodiackiller.com-8) the Vallejo Police Department served another search warrant at Allen's residence in February 1991 and seized some items.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-17) Despite its negative ramifications on his life, Allen continued to wear his Zodiac watch until it was seized during the execution of the search warrant. The letter sent to the Riverside Police Department from [Cheri Jo Bates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder_of_Cheri_Jo_Bates "Murder of Cheri Jo Bates")'s killer was printed with either [Elite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prestige_Elite "Prestige Elite") or Pica [typeface](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typeface "Typeface") on a [Royal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Typewriter_Company "Royal Typewriter Company") typewriter; during the 1991 search of Allen's residence, police seized a Royal typewriter with Elite type.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-amw.com3-18) The same type of ammunition used to kill the Lake Herman Road victims was also found, as well as a knife similar to the one Zodiac used at Lake Berryessa.

Department of Justice Agent Jim Silver had asked Zodiac victim Bryan Hartnell to observe Allen as he worked in a Vallejo hardware store. Hartnell watched Allen carefully and, at one time, spoke with him briefly. Hartnell reportedly stated, “I can’t say that that isn’t him.”[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-19)

[![Image 4](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c0/Arthur_Leigh_Allen_Driver%27s_License.jpg/250px-Arthur_Leigh_Allen_Driver%27s_License.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Arthur_Leigh_Allen_Driver%27s_License.jpg)

Allen's driver's license from 1967, showing his handwriting and appearance then

On August 16, 1991, Vallejo Police detective George Bawart showed Zodiac survivor Michael Mageau a [photo lineup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_lineup "Police lineup") of 1968 driver's licenses with Allen's picture among them; Mageau picked out Allen as the man who shot him in 1969, saying, "That's him! It's the man who shot me!".[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-20) However, by his own admission, Mageau never got a good look at the gunman and only saw the suspect briefly as he was shot.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-21) Following this identification, authorities were considering on charging Allen with the murders, as well as for possessing bomb-making materials that were found in his basement during the 1991 search of his home.

Shortly before his death, Allen wrote a letter to Rita Williams, a reporter from San Francisco station [KTVU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KTVU "KTVU") who had just interviewed him. The letter contained grammatical mistakes similar to those of the Zodiac letters.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-Nflix-22): Ep. 2  Williams firmly believes that Allen was the Zodiac. Allen died from a [heart attack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart_attack "Heart attack") on August 26, 1992.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-23) Two days after his death in 1992, the VPD served another warrant at Allen's house and seized more property from his residence.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-24)

In 2002, Cydne Holt of the SFPD crime lab developed a partial [DNA profile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_profile "DNA profile") from [saliva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saliva "Saliva") on stamps and envelopes of the Zodiac's letters – especially the stamp on the November 8, 1969, card – for the [ABC News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_News_(United_States) "ABC News (United States)") program _[Primetime Thursday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime\_Thursday "Primetime Thursday")_.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-:26-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-:27-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-:29-27) A partial DNA profile cannot "point to just one person", it "can only rule someone in as a possibility or exclude them if it isn't a match".[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-:31-28) The SFPD compared this partial profile to that of Allen and Cheney. Since neither test result indicated a match, the two were excluded as the contributors of the DNA.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-30)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-:29-27)

### 2007 film and documentary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arthur_Leigh_Allen&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2007 film and documentary")]

Allen was played by [John Carroll Lynch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carroll_Lynch "John Carroll Lynch") in the 2007 [David Fincher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Fincher "David Fincher") film _[Zodiac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac\_(film) "Zodiac (film)")_, which is based on [Robert Graysmith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Graysmith "Robert Graysmith")'s book.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-31) That same year, Graysmith noted that several policemen described Allen as the most likely suspect.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-Graysmith-2007-32)

Police officer Donald Fouke, who (with officer Eric Zelms) possibly saw the Zodiac fleeing the Paul Stine murder scene, said in the 2007 documentary _His Name was Arthur Leigh Allen_ that Allen weighed about 100 pounds more than the man Fouke saw, and that Allen's face was "too round".[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-Beck5-12)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-:28-33) Nancy Slover, the [police dispatcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_dispatcher "Police dispatcher") who received the call from the Zodiac after the Mageau–Ferrin shooting, said in the documentary that Allen did not sound like the man with whom she spoke.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-:28-33)

Retired police handwriting expert Lloyd Cunningham, who worked on the Zodiac case for decades, stated in 2009, "They gave me [banana boxes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banana_box "Banana box") full of Allen's writing, and none of his writing even came close to the Zodiac. Nor did DNA extracted from the envelopes [on the Zodiac letters] come close to Arthur Leigh Allen".[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-SFC:_Another-34) In 2010, [SFPD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Police_Department "San Francisco Police Department") investigator [Dave Toschi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Toschi "Dave Toschi") stated that all the evidence against Allen ultimately "turned out to be negative".[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-35)

In 2018, Tom Voigt, a veteran Zodiac internet sleuth and [9/11 conspiracy theorist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9/11_conspiracy_theories "9/11 conspiracy theories"), stated that the partial profile's efficacy from 2002 was dubious, as he had learned the DNA was "collected from the outside of the stamp" on the November 1969 card; "No genetic material was obtained from behind the stamp, or the seal of the envelope, or anywhere else that would have most certainly belonged to the Zodiac". Voigt claimed that this had been confirmed by Holt as well as an unnamed retired SFPD inspector, and that this discovery reaffirmed Allen's status as a viable suspect.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-:26-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-:27-26)

### _This Is the Zodiac Speaking_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arthur_Leigh_Allen&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: This Is the Zodiac Speaking")]

A three-episode documentary, _This Is the Zodiac Speaking_, aired on [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") in 2024. In the film, Allen's former students fondly recall his interest in [cryptology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptology "Cryptology"). They remembered him playing records like "[Tom Dooley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Dooley_(song) "Tom Dooley (song)")", about a woman's murder, and "I've got a little List" from _[The Mikado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Mikado "The Mikado")_. He also brought dead animals into the classroom. Numerous allegations are also made by former acquaintances, members of the Seawater family, that greatly inculpate Allen.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-:333-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-:342-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-:0-38) Zodiac researcher Michael Butterfield was skeptical of the documentary's allegations.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-:0-38)

In the 1960s, Allen was friends with Phyllis Seawater and often looked after her children. He took them on small trips, including one to Tajiguas Point in [Santa Barbara County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Barbara_County,_California "Santa Barbara County, California") on June 3, 1963. The day before, an unsolved shooting had occurred at that beach. According to their account, after Allen and the Seawater children arrived at Tajiguas Point, Allen left them in the car and went down to the beach alone. When he returned about an hour later, he appeared to have blood on his hands. He cleaned up and sped away with the children. The next day, the bodies of [Robert Domingos and Linda Edwards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#Robert_Domingos_and_Linda_Edwards "Zodiac Killer") were found on a nearby beach.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-:333-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-:342-37)

Three years later, on October 28, 1966, Allen took two of the older Seawater children, Connie and David, to [Riverside, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverside,_California "Riverside, California"). They stayed in a motel, and David slept through most of the trip. Cheri Jo Bates was killed near [Riverside City College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverside_City_College "Riverside City College") on October 30. The following morning, Allen hurried the children out of the motel, and Connie recalls him [molesting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Child_molestation "Child molestation") her in the car as they headed home.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-:333-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-:342-37) The Seawater children initially thought it was ludicrous that Allen could be the Zodiac. In 1991, Connie directly asked Allen if he was; he said if he told her, he would have to kill her. In 1992, David talked to Allen on the phone and thanked him for being so nice to them when they were young. Allen started sobbing and confessed to drugging them and molesting Connie. Alarmed, David asked Allen if he was the Zodiac, to which he allegedly responded, "It was me".[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-:0-38) The release of [David Fincher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Fincher "David Fincher")'s [film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_(film) "Zodiac (film)") about the Zodiac case in 2007 prodded the Seawater family to re-examine their memories of Allen.

A possible Zodiac cipher from 1973 was decoded for a 2017 [History Channel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_Channel "History Channel") show. On August 1, 1973, a letter was mailed to the _[Albany Times Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albany\_Times\_Union "Albany Times Union")_ in [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_(state) "New York (state)"). The return address was the [![Image 5](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f4/Zodiac_Killer_symbol.svg/20px-Zodiac_Killer_symbol.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Zodiac_Killer_symbol.svg) symbol. The writer promised to kill again on August 10. A three-line-code in the letter was supposed to reveal the name and location of the victim. FBI [cryptanalysts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptanalysis "Cryptanalysis") deciphered the code as "[redacted by the FBI] [Albany Medical Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albany_Medical_Center "Albany Medical Center"). This is only the beginning". No murder matched the details in the letter, and the handwriting was not a definitive match for Zodiac's.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-HISTORY-2023a-39) In the letter, the History Channel show revealed that Zodiac named his next victim as "Connie Henly" and her location in [Albany, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albany,_New_York "Albany, New York"), thus rendering the full deciphered code as "Connie Henly, [Albany Medical Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albany_Medical_Center "Albany Medical Center"). This is only the beginning". Phyllis Seawater's maiden-name was "Hensley", and at the time the letter had been sent, Connie was living in [New York State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_(state) "New York (state)"), just a few hours from Albany. Allen had previously fallen out with Connie for not leaving her family for him. The Seawaters also found a cache of Allen's letters to their mother, which include extensive discussions of the Zodiac.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen#cite_note-:0-38)

The **Zodiac Killer** (also known by the [pseudonym](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pseudonym "Pseudonym")**The Zodiac**) is an unidentified [serial killer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serial_killer "Serial killer") who murdered at least five people in the [San Francisco Bay Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Bay_Area "San Francisco Bay Area") between December 1968 and October 1969. The Zodiac attacked three couples and a cab driver in [Benicia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benicia,_California "Benicia, California"), [Vallejo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vallejo,_California "Vallejo, California"), unincorporated [Napa County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napa_County "Napa County"), and the [city of San Francisco.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco") Two of the Zodiac's seven victims survived.

In a series of letters mailed to Bay Area newspapers, the Zodiac took credit for the murders, described details known only to police, threatened bombings and more murders if the newspapers did not print his letters, and included [cryptograms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptogram "Cryptogram") with his correspondence. Two of the Zodiac's four cryptograms were decrypted in 1969 and 2020, and the other two remain unsolved.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-2) The Zodiac's last letter was received by the [_San Francisco Chronicle_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Chronicle "San Francisco Chronicle") in 1974. In the letter, The Zodiac claimed to have killed 37 people.

Despite several theories about the Zodiac's true identity, the only suspect police named was [Arthur Leigh Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Leigh_Allen "Arthur Leigh Allen"), a former elementary school teacher and convicted [sex offender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_offender "Sex offender") who died in 1992. The Zodiac's murders, cryptograms, and letters to newspapers have made the case one of the most famous unsolved cases in American history. The Zodiac has become a [fixture of popular culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_in_popular_culture "Zodiac Killer in popular culture"), and the search for his identity continues to be pursued by amateur detectives all over the world.

In 2004, the [San Francisco Police Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Police_Department "San Francisco Police Department") marked the case "inactive," but subsequently re-opened the case in 2006. The [California Department of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Department_of_Justice "California Department of Justice"), [the Federal Bureau of Investigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Bureau_of_Investigation "Federal Bureau of Investigation"), the city of Vallejo, and the Napa and [Solano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solano_County,_California "Solano County, California") county sheriffs maintain the case status as "open."

## Murders and correspondence

Police and investigators concur The Zodiac attacked seven people on four occasions in [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California"). Five victims died; two survived:[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-HISTORY-2023a-3)

1.   David Arthur Faraday (17) and Betty Lou Jensen (16) were shot and killed on December 20, 1968, on Lake Herman Road in [Benicia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benicia,_California "Benicia, California").
2.   Michael Renault Mageau (19) and Darlene Elizabeth Ferrin (22) were shot around midnight between July 4 and 5, 1969, in the parking lot of Blue Rock Springs Park in [Vallejo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vallejo,_California "Vallejo, California"). Mageau survived the attack; Ferrin died at [Kaiser Foundation Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaiser_Foundation_Hospital "Kaiser Foundation Hospital").
3.   Bryan Calvin Hartnell (20) and Cecelia Ann Shepard (22) were stabbed on September 27, 1969, at [Lake Berryessa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Berryessa "Lake Berryessa") in [Napa County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napa_County,_California "Napa County, California"). Hartnell survived; Shepard died from her injuries on September 29 at [Queen of the Valley Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_of_the_Valley_Medical_Center_(Napa,_California) "Queen of the Valley Medical Center (Napa, California)").
4.   Paul Lee Stine (29) was shot and killed on October 11, 1969, in the [Presidio Heights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidio_Heights,_San_Francisco,_California "Presidio Heights, San Francisco, California") neighborhood of [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco").

From 1969 to 1974, the Zodiac sent over twenty letters to newspapers, police, _Chronicle_ writer [Paul Avery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Avery "Paul Avery"), and attorney [Melvin Belli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melvin_Belli "Melvin Belli"). In the first sentence of the third letter, the writer identified himself as, "This is The Zodiac speaking," and signed all his letters with a symbol resembling the [crosshairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reticle "Reticle") of a [gunsight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sight_(device) "Sight (device)"): [![Image 7](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f4/Zodiac_Killer_symbol.svg/20px-Zodiac_Killer_symbol.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Zodiac_Killer_symbol.svg).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-4) Four of the mailings included [cryptograms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptogram "Cryptogram"); only two have been solved.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-5) The letters were postmarked in San Francisco and [Pleasanton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleasanton,_California "Pleasanton, California").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer#cite_note-Read-6)

The Zodiac's confirmed correspondence with date, recipient, and [incipit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incipit "Incipit"):

1.   [July 31st 1969](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_letter,_July_31st_1969 "s:Zodiac Killer letter, July 31st 1969"): _[San Francisco Chronicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San\_Francisco\_Chronicle "San Francisco Chronicle")_, _[San Francisco Examiner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San\_Francisco\_Examiner "San Francisco Examiner")_, and _[Vallejo Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vallejo\_Times\_Herald "Vallejo Times Herald")_. One-third of "Z408 cryptogram" enclosed with each letter. "I am the killer of the 2 teenagers last Christmass..."
2.   [August 4th 1969](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_letter,_August_4th_1969 "s:Zodiac Killer letter, August 4th 1969"): _Examiner_. "This is the Zodiac speaking."
3.   [October 13th 1969](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_letter,_October_13th_1969 "s:Zodiac Killer letter, October 13th 1969"): _Chronicle_. Swatch of Paul Stine's shirt. "I am the murderer of the taxi driver..."
4.   [November 8th 1969](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_letter,_November_8th_1969 "s:Zodiac Killer letter, November 8th 1969"): _Chronicle_. "Z340 cryptogram." The "Dripping Pen" card. "I though you would need a good laugh..."
5.   [November 9th 1969](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_letter,_November_9th_1969 "s:Zodiac Killer letter, November 9th 1969"): _Chronicle_. Bomb diagram. "...I have killed 7 people".
6.   [December 20th 1969](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_letter,_December_20th_1969 "s:Zodiac Killer letter, December 20th 1969"): [Melvin Belli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melvin_Belli "Melvin Belli"). Swatch of Stine's shirt. "...happy Christmass."
7.   [April 20th 1970](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_letter,_April_20th_1970 "s:Zodiac Killer letter, April 20th 1970"): _Chronicle_. "Z13 cryptogram." "My name is..."
8.   [April 28th 1970](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_letter,_April_28th_1970 "s:Zodiac Killer letter, April 28th 1970"): _Chronicle_. Greeting card. "I hope you enjoy yourselves..."
9.   [June 26th 1970](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_letter,_June_26th_1970 "s:Zodiac Killer letter, June 26th 1970"): _Chronicle_. "Z32 cryptogram." "I have become very upset..."
10.   [July 24th 1970](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_letter,_July_24th_1970 "s:Zodiac Killer letter, July 24th 1970"): _Chronicle_. "I am rather unhappy..."
11.   [July 26th 1970](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_letter,_July_26th_1970 "s:Zodiac Killer letter, July 26th 1970"): _Chronicle_. "Being that you will not wear some nice ⌖ buttons..."
12.   [October 5th 1970](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Zodiac_Killer_letter,_October_5th_1970 "s:Zodiac Killer letter, October 5th 1970"): _Chronicle_. Thirteen-hole punch card. "You'll hate me..."
