At the first [Game Developers Choice Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_Developers_Choice_Awards "Game Developers Choice Awards") in 2010, the game won four major awards: Best Online Technology, Game Design, New Online Game, and Visual Arts.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-119) At the 2011 [Golden Joystick Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Joystick_Awards "Golden Joystick Awards"), it won Best Free-to-Play Game.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-120) Music produced for the game won a [Shorty Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shorty_Award "Shorty Award"),[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-121) and was nominated at the [Hollywood Music in Media Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Music_in_Media_Awards "Hollywood Music in Media Awards").[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-122)

_League of Legends_ has received awards for its contribution to [esports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esports "Esports"). It was nominated for Best Esports Game at [The Game Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards "The Game Awards") in [2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2017 "The Game Awards 2017"),[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-123)[2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2018 "The Game Awards 2018"),[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-124) and [2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2025 "The Game Awards 2025");[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-125) then won in [2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2019 "The Game Awards 2019"), [2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2020 "The Game Awards 2020"), and [2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2021 "The Game Awards 2021").[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-TGA2019-126)[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-TGA2020-127)[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-TGA2021-128) Specific events organized by Riot for esports tournaments have been recognized by awards ceremonies. Also at The Game Awards, the Riot won Best Esports Event for the [2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_League_of_Legends_World_Championship "2019 League of Legends World Championship"), [2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_League_of_Legends_World_Championship "2020 League of Legends World Championship") and [2021 _League_ World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_League_of_Legends_World_Championship "2021 League of Legends World Championship").[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-TGA2019-126)[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-TGA2020-127)[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-TGA2021-128) At the 39th [Sports Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_Emmy_Award "Sports Emmy Award") in 2018, _League of Legends_ won Outstanding Live Graphic Design for the [2017 world championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_League_of_Legends_World_Championship "2017 League of Legends World Championship"); as part of the pre-competition proceedings, Riot used [augmented reality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Augmented_reality "Augmented reality") technology to have a [computer-generated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer-generated_imagery "Computer-generated imagery") dragon fly across the stage.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-129)[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-130)[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-131)

## Player behavior

_League of Legends_'s player base has a longstanding reputation for "toxicity"—rude and abusive in-game behavior,[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-132)[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-ReferenceA-133)[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-Alexander-134) with a survey by the [Anti-Defamation League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-Defamation_League "Anti-Defamation League") indicating that 76% of players have experienced in-game harassment.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-135) Riot Games has acknowledged the problem and responded that only a small portion of the game's players are consistently toxic. According to Jeffrey Lin, Riot's lead designer of social systems, most bad behavior is committed by players "occasionally acting out".[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-Webster-136) Several major systems have been implemented to tackle the issue. One is basic report functionality; players can report teammates or opponents who violate the game's code of ethics. The in-game chat is also monitored by algorithms that detect several types of abuse.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-Webster-136) An early system was the "Tribunal"—players who met certain requirements were able to review reports sent to Riot. If enough players determined that the messages were a violation, an automated system would punish them.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-137) Lin said that eliminating toxicity was an unrealistic goal, and the focus should be on rewarding good behavior.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-138) To that end, Riot reworked the "Honor system" in 2017, allowing players to award teammates virtual medals after games for one of three positive attributes. Acquiring these medals increases a player's "Honor level", rewarding them with free loot boxes over time.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-139)

of Legends: Wild Rift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League\_of\_Legends:\_Wild\_Rift "League of Legends: Wild Rift")_ is a version of the game for mobile operating systems Android and character models and environments were entirely rebuilt.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:20-163) A single-player, [turn-based role-playing game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Role-playing_video_game "Role-playing video game"), _[Ruined King: A League of Legends Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruined\_King:\_A\_League\_of\_Legends\_Story "Ruined King: A League of Legends Story")_, was released in 2021 for [PlayStation 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_4 "PlayStation 4"), [PlayStation 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_5 "PlayStation 5"), [Xbox One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_One "Xbox One"), [Xbox Series X/S](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_Series_X/S "Xbox Series X/S"), [Nintendo Switch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_Switch "Nintendo Switch"), and Windows.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:14-92) It was the first title released under Riot Games's publishing arm, [Riot Forge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riot_Forge "Riot Forge"), wherein non-Riot studios develop games using _League of Legends_ characters.[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-168) In December 2020, Greg Street, vice-president of IP and Entertainment at Riot Games, announced that a [massively multiplayer online role-playing game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massively_multiplayer_online_role-playing_game "Massively multiplayer online role-playing game") based on the game is in development.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-169)[_Song of Nunu: A League of Legends Story_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Song_of_Nunu "Song of Nunu"), a third-person adventure game revolving around the champion Nunu's search for his mother, with the help of the yeti Willump, was announced for a planned release in 2022. It is being developed by [Tequila Works](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tequila_Works "Tequila Works"), the creators of _[Rime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rime\_(video\_game) "Rime (video game)")_.[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-170) It was released on Windows and the Nintendo Switch on November 1, 2023.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-171)

### Music

Riot Games's first venture into music was in 2014 with the virtual [heavy metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavy_metal_music "Heavy metal music") band [Pentakill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentakill "Pentakill"), promoting a skin line of the same name.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-172)[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-lawson-173) Initially, Pentakill consisted of six champions: Kayle, Karthus, Mordekaiser, Olaf, Sona, and Yorick. In 2021, Viego was introduced to the group. Their music was primarily made by Riot Games's in-house music team but featured cameos by [Mötley Crüe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%B6tley_Cr%C3%BCe "Mötley Crüe") drummer [Tommy Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy_Lee "Tommy Lee") and [Danny Lohner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danny_Lohner "Danny Lohner"), a former member of industrial rock band [Nine Inch Nails](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nine_Inch_Nails "Nine Inch Nails"). Their second album, _Grasp of the Undying_, reached number one on the [iTunes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITunes "ITunes") metal charts in 2017.[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-lawson-173)

Pentakill was followed by [K/DA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K/DA "K/DA"), a [virtual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtual_band "Virtual band") K-pop [girl group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Girl_group "Girl group") composed of four champions, Ahri, Akali, Evelynn, and Kai'sa. As with Pentakill, K/DA is promotional material for a skin line by the same name.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-174) The group's debut single, "[Pop/Stars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop/Stars "Pop/Stars")", which premiered at the [2018 _League of Legends_ World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_League_of_Legends_World_Championship "2018 League of Legends World Championship"), garnered over 400 million views on YouTube and sparked widespread interest from people unfamiliar with _League of Legends_.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-175) In August 2020, Riot Games released "[The Baddest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Baddest_(K/DA_song) "The Baddest (K/DA song)")", the pre-release single for _[All Out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All\_Out\_(EP) "All Out (EP)")_, the five-track [EP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EP "EP") from K/DA which followed in November that year.[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-176)

In 2019, Riot created a virtual [hip hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip_hop "Hip hop") group called True Damage,[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-177) featuring the champions Akali, Yasuo, Qiyana, Senna, and Ekko.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-polygon1-178) The vocalists—[Keke Palmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keke_Palmer "Keke Palmer"), [Thutmose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thutmose_(musician) "Thutmose (musician)"), [Becky G](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Becky_G "Becky G"), [Duckwrth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duckwrth "Duckwrth"), and [Soyeon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soyeon "Soyeon")—performed a live version of the group's debut song, "Giants", during the opening ceremony of the [2019 _League of Legends_ World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_League_of_Legends_World_Championship "2019 League of Legends World Championship"), alongside holographic versions of their characters.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-polygon1-178) The in-game cosmetics promoted by the music video featured a collaboration with fashion house [Louis Vuitton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Vuitton "Louis Vuitton").[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-179)

In 2023, Riot formed Heartsteel, a virtual [boy band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_band "Boy band"), comprising the champions Aphelios, Ezreal, Kayn, K'Sante, Sett, and Yone. The vocalists are [Baekhyun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baekhyun "Baekhyun") from the K-pop groups [Exo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exo "Exo") and [SuperM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SuperM "SuperM"), Cal Scruby, [ØZI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%98ZI "ØZI"), and [Tobi Lou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tobi_Lou "Tobi Lou"). Heartsteel's debut single "Paranoia" was released in October of that year.[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-180)

### Comics

Riot announced a collaboration with [Marvel Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Comics "Marvel Comics") in 2018.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-Liao-91) Riot had previously experimented with releasing comics through its website.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-181)[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-182) Shannon Liao of _[The Verge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Verge "The Verge")_ noted that the comic books were "a rare opportunity for Riot to showcase its years of lore that has often appeared as an afterthought".[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-Liao-91) The first comic was _League of Legends: Ashe—Warmother_, which debuted in 2018, followed by _League of Legends: Lux_ that same year.[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-183) A print version of the latter was released in 2019.[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-184)

### _Arcane_

While celebrating _League of Legends_'s tenth anniversary, Riot announced an animated television series, _Arcane._[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-hollywoodreporter.com-185) It was the company's first production for television,[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:17-186) and a collaboration between Riot Games and animation studio [Fortiche Production](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortiche_Production "Fortiche Production").[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:17-186) The series is set in the technologically advanced city of Piltover and its oppressed, underground sister city of Zaun.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:17-186)[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-187)_Arcane_ explores adult themes and is not intended for children.[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-hollywoodreporter.com-185) It features multiple playable characters from _League of Legends_. [Hailee Steinfeld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hailee_Steinfeld "Hailee Steinfeld") stars as [Vi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vi_(League_of_Legends) "Vi (League of Legends)"), [Ella Purnell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ella_Purnell "Ella Purnell") as [Jinx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jinx_(League_of_Legends) "Jinx (League of Legends)"), [Kevin Alejandro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Alejandro "Kevin Alejandro") as Jayce, and [Katie Leung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katie_Leung "Katie Leung") as Caitlyn.[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-188)

After a delay caused by the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), the series premiered in November 2021 on [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") internationally and through [Tencent Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tencent_Video "Tencent Video") in China.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:17-186) The first season received critical acclaim, winning four [Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmy_Awards "Emmy Awards") and nine [Annie Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annie_Awards "Annie Awards").[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-Variety_Arcane-189) After the success of the first season, Riot hired former executives from [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix"), HBO Max, and [Paramount Television Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount_Television_Studios "Paramount Television Studios") to expand its entertainment division,[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-190) and CEO Nicolo Laurent pledged to create an "entertainment company for the 21st century".[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-191) Ahead of the premiere of the second and final season, [_Variety_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)") reported that production and marketing costs for _Arcane_'s 18 episodes exceeded $250 million, making it the most expensive animated series ever made.[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-Variety_Arcane-189)

_[Bloomberg News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloomberg\_News "Bloomberg News")_ reported that Riot paid Netflix around $3 million for each episode aired and that the studio failed to convert the series' success into in-game revenue. Riot had no plan to recoup the show's costs but said the second season was "on track to break even".[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-192) The second season premiered in November 2024 to similar acclaim, winning seven Annie Awards in all nominated categories.[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-auto-193)[GKIDS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GKIDS "GKIDS") produced home media releases of the first season in 2024, including a collector's edition DVD, a 4K UHD steelbook, and [Blu-ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blu-ray "Blu-ray") variants. The collector's edition, 4k UHD, and 4k Blu-ray variants for season 2 came out in 2025.[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-auto-193)

Title: Riot is rebuilding League of Legends targeting 2027 release

URL Source: https://www.gosugamers.net/lol/news/77750-riot-is-rebuilding-league-of-legends-targeting-2027-release

Published Time: 2025-12-19T06:04:00.0000000+00:00

Markdown Content:
### "We're often asked if we're going to make League of Legends 2 someday. And the answer to that has been, and remains, no."

Riot Games has confirmed it is working on a long-term overhaul of [League of Legends](https://www.gosugamers.net/lol) (LoL) after a report by Bloomberg detailed plans for what could be the biggest update in the game’s history, currently targeted for 2027. Following the report, Riot Games Head of League Studio Andrei “Meddler” Van Roon moved quickly to address speculation, sharing an early developer video on X.

“We were planning to share this video with you in early January as part of the bigger Season Start moment,” Meddler wrote, explaining that the studio decided to bring it forward as rumours gained traction. The video is part of a larger dev update planned after the holiday break and focuses on Riot’s long-term vision for League.

In the post, Meddler confirmed Riot is working on “a brand new around-game client that’s fully integrated with the in-game experience,” alongside a full visual overhaul of Summoner’s Rift, gameplay changes tied to that update, tweaks to Runes and pre-game systems, and a revamped new player experience. He added that Riot will share more details “sometime between MSI and Worlds,” including when in 2027 these updates are expected to land.

The confirmation follows [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-12-18/riot-has-a-secret-plan-to-remake-its-league-of-legends-game?accessToken=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzb3VyY2UiOiJTdWJzY3JpYmVyR2lmdGVkQXJ0aWNsZSIsImlhdCI6MTc2NjA5NjE4NCwiZXhwIjoxNzY2NzAwOTg0LCJhcnRpY2xlSWQiOiJUN0hLMzhLR1pBSzYwMCIsImJjb25uZWN0SWQiOiJGRUIzODlCNUI2ODI0RTY0QjY5MENEODE1RTBDREZGRCJ9.UPpzbjNqabzTLwz-1lVVBK4cfd1jmlT9gxz17gLhVrA&leadSource=reddit_wall)’s report, which states Riot is internally referring to the project as League Next and describes it as the largest update since League of Legends launched in 2009.

## **What Riot is working on behind the scenes**

The video shared by Meddler features him alongside Paul “Pabro” Bellezza, Executive Producer of League of Legends, and directly addresses long-standing community questions. “We’re often asked if we’re going to make League of Legends 2 someday,” Pabro says early on. “And the answer to that has been, and remains, no.” Instead, Riot is focused on continuing to evolve the existing game rather than replacing it.

Meddler explains that while League is usually updated incrementally, some improvements make more sense as part of a larger bundle. “There are some things that do make the most sense as part of a larger bundle of changes,” he says, confirming that the team has been working on bigger updates behind the scenes.

Although Riot is not yet ready to show footage, Pabro notes that “the majority of the League team are now working on” these long-term changes. He also confirms that Summoner’s Rift is being rebuilt with entirely new visuals and some gameplay updates, alongside changes to Runes and pre-game choices. On onboarding, Pabro adds that Riot is overhauling the new player experience so that “once we’re done, it should be the best time ever to get your friends into League.”

Riot has not yet shared exact dates or visuals for the update, with more information expected in future developer updates.

_**League of Legends**_ (_**LoL**_), commonly referred to as _**League**_, is a [multiplayer online battle arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiplayer_online_battle_arena "Multiplayer online battle arena") video game developed and published by [Riot Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riot_Games "Riot Games"). Inspired by _[Defense of the Ancients](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defense\_of\_the\_Ancients "Defense of the Ancients")_, a [custom map](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mod_(video_games) "Mod (video games)") for _[Warcraft III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warcraft\_III:\_Reign\_of\_Chaos "Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos")_, Riot's founders sought to develop a stand-alone game in the same genre. Since its release in October 2009, _League_ has been [free-to-play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free-to-play "Free-to-play") and is monetized through [purchasable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freemium "Freemium") character customization. The game is available for [Windows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows "Windows") and [macOS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MacOS "MacOS").

In the game's main mode, Summoner's Rift, two teams of five players battle in [player-versus-player](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Player-versus-player "Player-versus-player") combat. Each player controls a character, known as a "champion", with unique abilities and styles of play. During a match, champions become more powerful by collecting [experience points](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Experience_point "Experience point"), earning gold, and purchasing [items](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Item_(game_terminology) "Item (game terminology)") to defeat the opposing team. Teams defend their base and win by pushing toward the enemy base and destroying a large structure within it, the "Nexus".

_League of Legends_ has received generally favorable reviews, which have highlighted its accessibility, character designs, and production value. The game's long lifespan has resulted in a critical reappraisal, with reviews trending favorably; it is widely considered one of the [greatest video games ever made](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greatest_video_games_ever_made "Greatest video games ever made"). However, rude and abusive in-game player behavior, criticized since the game's early days, persists despite Riot's attempts to fix the problem. In 2019, _League_ regularly peaked at eight million concurrent players, and its popularity has led to tie-ins such as music, comic books, short stories, and the animated series _[Arcane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcane\_(TV\_series) "Arcane (TV series)")_. Its success has spawned several [spin-off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin-off_(media) "Spin-off (media)") video games, including a [mobile version](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends:_Wild_Rift "League of Legends: Wild Rift"), a [digital collectible card game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legends_of_Runeterra "Legends of Runeterra"), and a [turn-based role-playing game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruined_King "Ruined King"), among [others](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riot_Games#Games "Riot Games"). An [MMORPG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massively_multiplayer_online_role-playing_game "Massively multiplayer online role-playing game") based on the property is in development.

_League of Legends_ is the world's largest [esport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esport "Esport"), with an international [competitive scene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends_in_esports "League of Legends in esports") consisting of multiple regional leagues which culminates in an annual [_League of Legends_ World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends_World_Championship "League of Legends World Championship"). The [2019 event](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_League_of_Legends_World_Championship "2019 League of Legends World Championship") registered over 100 million unique viewers, peaking at a concurrent viewership of 44 million during the [finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_League_of_Legends_World_Championship_final "2019 League of Legends World Championship final"). Domestic and international events have been broadcast on [livestreaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Livestreaming "Livestreaming") websites such as [Twitch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitch_(service) "Twitch (service)"), [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube"), [Bilibili](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bilibili "Bilibili"), and the [cable television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cable_television_in_the_United_States "Cable television in the United States") sports channel [ESPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESPN "ESPN").

## Gameplay

[![Image 2: Screenshot of League of Legends, featuring four champions in the bottom lane of the game's primary map, surrounded by minions.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/c/ca/League_of_Legends_Screenshot_2018.png/330px-League_of_Legends_Screenshot_2018.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:League_of_Legends_Screenshot_2018.png)

Four champions in the bottom lane of Summoner's Rift, surrounded by minions. The red health bars indicate that they are opposing players.

_League of Legends_ is a [multiplayer online battle arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiplayer_online_battle_arena "Multiplayer online battle arena") (MOBA) game in which the player controls a character ("champion") with a set of unique abilities from an [isometric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isometric_video_game_graphics "Isometric video game graphics") perspective.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-July_2020-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-3) During a match, champions gain levels by accruing [experience points](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Experience_point "Experience point") (XP) through killing enemies.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:6-4) Items can be acquired to increase champions' strength,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:18-5) and are bought with gold, which players accrue passively over time and earn actively by defeating the opposing team's minions,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-July_2020-2) champions, or defensive structures.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:6-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:18-5) In the main game mode, Summoner's Rift, items are purchased through a shop menu available to players only when their champion is in the team's base.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-July_2020-2) Each match is discrete; levels and items do not transfer from one match to another.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-6)

### Summoner's Rift

[![Image 3: The game's main map. It is a square, with the team bases on the top right and bottom right corners. There are three pathways to each base: one diagonally across the center, and the others going up and turning at the top left and bottom right corners.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dc/Map_of_MOBA.svg/330px-Map_of_MOBA.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Map_of_MOBA.svg)

A simplified representation of Summoner's Rift. The yellow paths are the "lanes" down which minions march; blue and red dots represent turrets. The fountains are the dark areas within each base, and are beside each Nexus. The dotted black line indicates the river.

Summoner's Rift is the flagship game mode of _League of Legends_ and the most prominent in [professional-level play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends_in_esports "League of Legends in esports").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-9) The mode has a ranked competitive ladder; a matchmaking system determines a player's skill level and generates a starting rank from which they can climb. There are ten tiers; the least skilled are Iron, Bronze, and Silver, and the highest are Master, Grandmaster, and Challenger.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-10)[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-13)

Two teams of five players compete to destroy the opposing team's "Nexus", which is guarded by the enemy champions and defensive structures known as "turrets".[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-BBC_Sport-14) Each team's Nexus is in its base, where players start the game and reappear after death.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-BBC_Sport-14)[Non-player characters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-player_character "Non-player character") known as minions are generated from each team's Nexus and advance toward the enemy base along three lanes guarded by turrets: top, middle, and bottom.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-15) Each team's base contains three "inhibitors", one behind the third tower from the center of each lane. Destroying an enemy team's inhibitor causes stronger allied minions to [spawn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spawning_(video_games) "Spawning (video games)") in that lane and allows the attacking team to damage the enemy Nexus and the two turrets guarding it.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-16) The regions in between the lanes are known as the "jungle", which is inhabited by "monsters" that, like minions, respawn at regular intervals. Like minions, monsters provide gold and XP when killed.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-17) Another, more powerful class of monster resides within the river that separates each team's jungle.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-18) These monsters require multiple players to defeat and grant special abilities to their slayers' team. For example, teams can gain a powerful allied unit after killing the Rift Herald, permanent strength boosts by killing dragons, and stronger, more durable minions by killing Baron Nashor.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-19)

Summoner's Rift matches can last from 15 minutes to over an hour.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-20) The game does not dictate where players may go, but conventions have arisen: typically one player goes in the top lane, one in the middle lane, one in the jungle, and two in the bottom lane.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-July_2020-2)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:6-4)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-21) Players in a lane kill minions to accumulate gold and XP (termed "farming") and try to prevent their opponent from doing the same. A fifth champion, known as a "jungler", farms the jungle monsters and, when powerful enough, assists their teammates in a lane.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-22)

### Other modes

Besides Summoner's Rift, _League of Legends_ has two other permanent game modes. ARAM ("All Random, All Mid") is a five-versus-five mode like Summoner's Rift, but on a map called Howling Abyss with only one long lane, no jungle area, and champions randomly chosen for players.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:5-23)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-24)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-25) Given the small size of the map, players must be vigilant in avoiding enemy abilities.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-26)

_[Teamfight Tactics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teamfight\_Tactics "Teamfight Tactics")_ is an [auto battler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auto_battler "Auto battler") released in June 2019 and made a permanent game mode the next month.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:2-27)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-AutobattlerIGN-28) As with others in its genre, players build a team and battle to be the last one standing. Players do not directly affect combat but position their units on a board for them to fight automatically against opponents each round.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-29)_Teamfight Tactics_ is available for [iOS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IOS "IOS") and [Android](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Android_(operating_system) "Android (operating system)") and has [cross-platform play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross-platform_play "Cross-platform play") with the Windows and macOS clients.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:15-30)

Other game modes have been made available temporarily, typically aligning with in-game events.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-destructoidrotation2-31)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-patch117-32) Ultra Rapid Fire (URF) mode was available for two weeks as a 2014 [April Fools Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/April_Fools_Day "April Fools Day") prank. In the mode, champion abilities have no resource cost, significantly reduced cooldown timers, increased movement speed, reduced healing, and faster attacks.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-33)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-34) In April 2015, Riot disclosed that it had not brought the mode back because its unbalanced design resulted in player "burnout". Riot also said the costs associated with maintaining and balancing URF were too high.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-35) Other temporary modes include One for All and Nexus Blitz. One for All has players pick a champion for all members of their team to play.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-oneforall-36)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-oneforall2-37) In Nexus Blitz, players participated in a series of [mini-games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mini-games "Mini-games") on a compressed map.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-nexusblitz2-38)

## Development

### Pre-release

[![Image 4: A photograph of Riot Games's headquarters in West Los Angeles](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5a/Riot_Games_Headquarters_2023.jpg/250px-Riot_Games_Headquarters_2023.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Riot_Games_Headquarters_2023.jpg)

Riot Games's West Los Angeles headquarters

Riot Games's founders Brandon Beck and Marc Merill had an idea for a spiritual successor to _[Defense of the Ancients](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defense\_of\_the\_Ancients "Defense of the Ancients")_, known as _DotA_. A [mod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mod_(video_games) "Mod (video games)") for _[Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warcraft\_III:\_Reign\_of\_Chaos "Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos")_, _DotA_ required players to buy _Warcraft III_ and install custom software; _[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Washington\_Post "The Washington Post")_'s Brian Crecente said the mod "lacked a level of polish and was often hard to find and set up".[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:3-39) Phillip Kollar of _Polygon_ noted that [Blizzard Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blizzard_Entertainment "Blizzard Entertainment") supported _Warcraft III_ with an [expansion pack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expansion_pack "Expansion pack"), then shifted their focus to other projects while the game still had players. Beck and Merill sought to create a game that would be supported over a significantly longer period.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:7-40)

Beck and Merill held a _DotA_ tournament for students at the [University of Southern California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Southern_California "University of Southern California"), with an ulterior goal of recruitment. There they met Jeff Jew, later a producer on _League of Legends_. Jew was very familiar with _DotA_ and spent much of the tournament teaching others how to play. Beck and Merill invited him to an interview, and he joined Riot Games as an intern.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:3-39) Beck and Merill recruited two figures involved with _DotA:_ Steve Feak, one of its designers,_[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League\_of\_Legends#cite\_note-:3-39)_ and Steve Mescon, who ran a support website to assist players.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-41)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-42) Feak said early development was highly iterative, comparing it to designing _DotA_.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-43)

A demonstration of _League of Legends_ built in the _Warcraft III_ game engine was completed in four months and then shown at the 2007 [Game Developers Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_Developers_Conference "Game Developers Conference").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:7-40) There, Beck and Merill had little success with potential investors. Publishers were confused by the game's free-to-play business model and lack of a single-player mode. The free-to-play model was untested outside of Asian markets,[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:3-39) so publishers were primarily interested in a retail release, and the game's capacity for a [sequel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sequel "Sequel").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:7-40) In 2008, Riot reached an agreement with holding company [Tencent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tencent "Tencent") to oversee the game's launch in China.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:7-40)

_League of Legends_ was announced on October 7, 2008, for [Microsoft Windows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Windows "Microsoft Windows").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:11-44)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-45)[Closed beta-testing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Closed_beta "Closed beta") began in April 2009.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:11-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:0-46) Upon the launch of the beta, 17 champions were available.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-47) Riot initially aimed to ship the game with 20 champions but doubled the number before the game's full release in North America on October 27, 2009.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-Crecente-48)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-49) The game's full name was announced as _League of Legends: Clash of Fates_. Riot planned to use the subtitle to signal when future content was available, but decided it was silly and dropped it before launch._[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League\_of\_Legends#cite\_note-:7-40)_

### Post-release

_League of Legends_ receives regular updates in the form of [patches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patch_(computing) "Patch (computing)"). Although previous games had utilized patches to ensure no one strategy dominated, _League of Legends_' patches made keeping pace with the developer's changes a core part of the game. In 2014, Riot standardized its patch cadence to once approximately every two or three weeks.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-50) These updates change the effectiveness of strategies within the game, known as the [metagame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metagame "Metagame"); update content is determined by the developer using a combination of gameplay data and product goals.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-51)

The development team includes hundreds of game designers and artists. In 2016, the music team had four full-time composers and a team of producers creating audio for the game and its promotional materials.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:1-52) As of 2025, the game has 172 champions,[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-53) and Riot Games periodically overhauls the visuals and gameplay of the oldest in the roster.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-54) Although only available for Microsoft Windows at launch, a [Mac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MacOS "MacOS") version of the game was made available in 2013.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-55)

Since May 2023, the game uses Riot's custom always-online anti-cheat software, [Vanguard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riot_Vanguard "Riot Vanguard"), on Microsoft Windows devices.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:19-56) Originally developed by Riot for its tactical shooter _[Valorant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valorant "Valorant")_ (2020), Vanguard requires access to the device's [kernel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kernel_(operating_system) "Kernel (operating system)"), which some users saw as unnecessarily intrusive.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-57) Vanguard does not collect user data or send it to Riot Games.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-58) Following the anti-cheat's deployment, some players said Vanguard [bricked](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bricked "Bricked") their devices. The developer said this was caused by other problems, with only 0.03% of players reporting issues.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:19-56)

In December 2025, [Bloomberg News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloomberg_News "Bloomberg News") published a report stating Riot were planning a large-scale update to the game, internally titled "League Next".[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-59) The same day, the League of Legends team published a video responding to the report, and saying they intended to replace the game's client, improve onboarding for new users, and overhaul visuals. Both the report and video emphasised Riot's intention to make the game more beginner-friendly.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-60)

### Revenue model

_League of Legends_ uses a [free-to-play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free-to-play "Free-to-play") business model. Revenue is generated by selling cosmetic goods with no impact to gameplay. Several of these cosmetics—for example, "skins" that change the appearance of champions—can be redeemed after purchasing an [in-game currency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In-game_currency "In-game currency") called Riot Points (RP).[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:03-61) As virtual goods, they have high [profit margins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Profit_margins "Profit margins").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:1-52) An [Ubisoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ubisoft "Ubisoft") analyst estimated in 2014 that 4% of players were paying customers—significantly lower than the industry standard—and suggested that revenue optimization was likely not a priority because of the game's large player base.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:33-62) A 2016 analysis by [SuperData](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nielsen_Media_Research "Nielsen Media Research") estimated the game's monthly revenues at $150 million per month.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-63) At the 2024 [Summer Game Fest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Game_Fest "Summer Game Fest"), game director Pu Liu said that revenue is primarily generated by a "single-digit percentage" of players, colloquially known as whales.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-64)

Skins have five basic tiers, ranging in cost from $4 to $25.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:23-65) Riot Games added an additional skin tier to _League of Legends_ in 2024, describing them as a [luxury good](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luxury_good "Luxury good"). These skins cannot be purchased outright: instead, players buy attempts to win the skin via a [slot machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slot_machine "Slot machine").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-Exalted3-66) Some commentators identified this as a [gacha game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gacha_game "Gacha game") mechanic,[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-67)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-68) used by Riot since 2023 in _[Teamfight Tactics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teamfight\_Tactics "Teamfight Tactics")_.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-69) Players are guaranteed to acquire the skin after a predefined number of failed attempts.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:43-70) The cost can range from $200 to $430.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:43-70) Responses to early skins in this tier divided players.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-71) The first was criticized for being a recolored variant of an existing skin,[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-72) known as a "chroma".[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-73) The developer released several more of these,[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:12-74) with a [YouTube content creator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube_content_creator "YouTube content creator") known for showcasing upcoming skins for the company describing the tier as a "[scam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scam "Scam")".[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:12-74)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-75)

One day after revealing a $430 "Hall of Fame" skin to honor the career of professional gamer [Faker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faker_(gamer) "Faker (gamer)"),[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-76) Riot announced layoffs at the company, impacting Ben Rosado—the cosmetic's designer—and eliciting further negative responses from players.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:43-70)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-77) In early 2025, Riot announced a new skin in the tier that had been long requested by players. _[PC Gamer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PC\_Gamer "PC Gamer")_'s Rick Lane described the strategy as "whale chasing" and "psychological manipulation". He said that the skins had been selected to "subtly" entice players into "rolling the dice", at which point the [sunk-cost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunk_cost "Sunk cost") fallacy takes over. Lane described it as the latest in a series of monetization controversies for the developer.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-78)

In November 2024, the studio said they would streamline player rewards in an upcoming patch, describing the game's various progression tracks and currencies as "needlessly complex".[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-79) The announcement caused widespread outrage. A viral [Reddit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reddit "Reddit") post estimated that free-to-play players must play the game for over 800 hours to unlock a single champion.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-80) It was described by _[GamesRadar+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GamesRadar%2B "GamesRadar+")_ as the studio's "worst PR disaster in years".[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-81) In mid-January 2025, game director Andrei van Room said they had "screwed up", explaining that a designer forgot to include the "first win of the day" experience bonus in their calculations, causing unintended consequences.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-82) The developer partially reverted some of the changes, including halving the cost of purchasing a champion, and the return of "hextech chests"[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-83)—a [loot box](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loot_box "Loot box") system introduced in 2016. These are purchasable virtual "chests" that provide random cosmetics,[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-84) a practice that has been criticized as a form of gambling.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-85)

### Plot

See also: [_League of Legends_ §Spin-offs and other media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#Spin-offs_and_other_media)

Before 2014, players existed in-universe as political leaders, or "Summoners", commanding champions to fight on the Fields of Justice—for example, Summoner's Rift—to avert a catastrophic war.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-Rift_Herald,_Plot-86) Sociologist Matt Watson said the plot and setting were bereft of the political themes found in other [role-playing games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Role-playing_game "Role-playing game"), and presented in reductive "good versus evil" terms.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-87) In the game's early development, Riot did not hire writers, and designers wrote character biographies only a paragraph long.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:7-40)

In September 2014, Riot Games rebooted the game's [fictional setting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fictional_universe "Fictional universe"), removing summoners from the game's lore to avoid "creative stagnation".[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-Rift_Herald,_Plot-86)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-88) Luke Plunkett wrote for _[Kotaku](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kotaku "Kotaku")_ that, although the change would upset long-term fans, it was necessary as the game's player base grew in size.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-kotaku.com-89) Shortly after the reboot, Riot hired _[Warhammer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warhammer\_Fantasy\_(setting) "Warhammer Fantasy (setting)")_ writer [Graham McNeill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graham_McNeill "Graham McNeill").[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-90) Riot's storytellers and artists create [flavor text](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavor_text "Flavor text"), adding "richness" to the game, but very little of this is seen as a part of normal gameplay. Instead, that work supplies a foundation for the franchise's expansion into other media,[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:1-52) such as comic books and spin-off video games.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-Liao-91)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:14-92) The Fields of Justice were replaced by a new fictional setting—a planet called Runeterra. The setting has elements from several genres—from [Lovecraftian horror](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lovecraftian_horror "Lovecraftian horror") to traditional [sword and sorcery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sword_and_sorcery "Sword and sorcery") fantasy.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-93)

## Reception

_League of Legends_ received generally favorable reviews on its initial release, according to [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator") website [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic").[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-Metacritic-94) Many publications noted the game's high [replay value](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Replay_value "Replay value").[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-106)[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:9-107)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:10-108)_Kotaku_ reviewer Brian Crecente admired how items altered champion play styles.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:10-108) Quintin Smith of _[Eurogamer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurogamer "Eurogamer")_ concurred, praising the amount of experimentation offered by champions.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-Eurogamer-109) Comparing it to _Defense of the Ancients_, Rick McCormick of _[GamesRadar+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GamesRadar%2B "GamesRadar+")_ said that playing _League of Legends_ was "a vote for choice over refinement".[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-110)

Given the game's origins, other reviewers frequently compared aspects of it to _DotA._ According to _GamesRadar+_ and _[GameSpot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GameSpot "GameSpot")_, _League of Legends_ would feel familiar to those who had already played _DotA_.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-mccormick1-97)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-111) The game's inventive character design and lively colors distinguished the game from its competitors.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-IGN_Review_1-103) Smith concluded his review by noting that, although there was not "much room for negativity", Riot's goal of refining _DotA_ had not yet been realized.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-Eurogamer-109)

Although Crecente praised the game's free-to-play model,[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:10-108)_[GameSpy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GameSpy "GameSpy")_'s Ryan Scott was critical of the [grind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grinding_(video_games) "Grinding (video games)") required for non-paying players to unlock key gameplay elements, calling it unacceptable in a competitive game.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:16-112)[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-114) Many outlets said the game was underdeveloped.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:9-107)[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-IGN_Review_1-103) A physical version of the game was available for purchase from retailers; _GameSpot_'s Kevin VanOrd said it was an inadvisable purchase because the value included $10 of store credit for an unavailable store.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:9-107) German site _GameStar_ noted that none of the bonuses in that version were available until the launch period had ended and refused to carry out a full review.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-115)_[IGN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IGN "IGN")_'s Steve Butts compared the launch to the poor state of _[CrimeCraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CrimeCraft "CrimeCraft")_'s release earlier in 2009; he indicated that features available during _League of Legends_'s beta were removed for the release, even for those who purchased the retail version.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-IGN_Review_1-103) Matches took unnecessarily long to find for players, with long [queue times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matchmaking_(video_games) "Matchmaking (video games)"),[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:10-108)[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-IGN_Review_1-103)[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-116) and _GameRevolution_ mentioned frustrating bugs.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:4-117)

Some reviewers addressed toxicity in the game's early history. Crecente wrote that the community was "insular" and "whiny" when losing.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:10-108) Butts speculated that _League of Legends_ inherited many of _DotA_'s players, who had developed a reputation for being "notoriously hostile" to newcomers.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-IGN_Review_1-103)

### Reassessment

[![Image 5](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b2/Nidalee_%289844717146%29.jpg/250px-Nidalee_%289844717146%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nidalee_(9844717146).jpg)

Fan [cosplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosplay "Cosplay") of the _League of Legends_ champion Nidalee

Regular updates to the game have resulted in a reappraisal by some outlets; _IGN_'s second reviewer, Leah B. Jackson, explained that the website's original review had become "obsolete".[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-IGN_Review_2-104) Two publications increased their original scores: _GameSpot_ from 6 to 9,[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-vanord1900-99)[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-GameSpot_Review_2-100) and _IGN_ from 8 to 9.2.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-IGN_Review_1-103)[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-IGN_Review_2-104) The variety offered by the champion roster was described by Steven Strom of _PC Gamer_ as "fascinating";[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-PC_Gamer_review-105) Jackson pointed to "memorable" characters and abilities.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-IGN_Review_2-104) Although the items had originally been praised at release by other outlets such as _Kotaku_,[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:10-108) Jackson's reassessment criticized the lack of item diversity and viability, noting that the items recommended to the player by the in-game shop were essentially required because of their strength.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-IGN_Review_2-104)

While reviewers were pleased with the diverse array of play styles offered by champions and their abilities,[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-IGN_Review_2-104)[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-GameSpot_Review_2-100)[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-PC_Gamer_review-105) Strom thought that the female characters still resembled those in "horny _[Clash of Clans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clash\_of\_Clans "Clash of Clans")_ clones" in 2018.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-PC_Gamer_review-105) Two years before Strom's review, a champion designer responded to criticism by players that a young, female champion was not conventionally attractive. He argued that limiting female champions to one body type was constraining and said progress had been made in Riot's recent releases.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-118)

Comparisons persisted between the game and others in the genre. _GameSpot_'s Tyler Hicks wrote that new players would pick up _League of Legends_ quicker than _DotA_ and that the removal of randomness-based skills made the game more competitive.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-GameSpot_Review_2-100) Jackson called _League of Legends_'s rate of unlock for champions "a model of generosity", but less than _DotA_'s sequel, _[Dota 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dota\_2 "Dota 2")_ (2013), produced by [Valve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valve_Corporation "Valve Corporation"), wherein characters are unlocked by default.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-IGN_Review_2-104) Strom said the game was fast-paced compared to _Dota 2_'s "yawning" matches, but slower than those of Blizzard Entertainment's "intentionally accessible" MOBA _[Heroes of the Storm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heroes\_of\_the\_Storm "Heroes of the Storm")_ (2015).[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-PC_Gamer_review-105)

Also at The Game Awards, the Riot won Best Esports Event for the [2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_League_of_Legends_World_Championship "2019 League of Legends World Championship"), [2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_League_of_Legends_World_Championship "2020 League of Legends World Championship") and [2021 _League_ World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_League_of_Legends_World_Championship "2021 League of Legends World Championship").[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-TGA2019-126)[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-TGA2020-127)[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-TGA2021-128) At the 39th [Sports Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_Emmy_Award "Sports Emmy Award") in 2018, _League of Legends_ won Outstanding Live Graphic Design for the [2017 world championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_League_of_Legends_World_Championship "2017 League of Legends World Championship"); as part of the pre-competition proceedings, Riot used [augmented reality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Augmented_reality "Augmented reality") technology to have a [computer-generated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer-generated_imagery "Computer-generated imagery") dragon fly across the stage.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-129)[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-130)[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-131)

## Player behavior

_League of Legends_'s player base has a longstanding reputation for "toxicity"—rude and abusive in-game behavior,[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-132)[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-ReferenceA-133)[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-Alexander-134) with a survey by the [Anti-Defamation League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-Defamation_League "Anti-Defamation League") indicating that 76% of players have experienced in-game harassment.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-135) Riot Games has acknowledged the problem and responded that only a small portion of the game's players are consistently toxic. According to Jeffrey Lin, Riot's lead designer of social systems, most bad behavior is committed by players "occasionally acting out".[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-Webster-136) Several major systems have been implemented to tackle the issue. One is basic report functionality; players can report teammates or opponents who violate the game's code of ethics. The in-game chat is also monitored by algorithms that detect several types of abuse.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-Webster-136) An early system was the "Tribunal"—players who met certain requirements were able to review reports sent to Riot. If enough players determined that the messages were a violation, an automated system would punish them.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-137) Lin said that eliminating toxicity was an unrealistic goal, and the focus should be on rewarding good behavior.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-138) To that end, Riot reworked the "Honor system" in 2017, allowing players to award teammates virtual medals after games for one of three positive attributes. Acquiring these medals increases a player's "Honor level", rewarding them with free loot boxes over time.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-139)

### Music

Riot Games's first venture into music was in 2014 with the virtual [heavy metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavy_metal_music "Heavy metal music") band [Pentakill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentakill "Pentakill"), promoting a skin line of the same name.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-172)[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-lawson-173) Initially, Pentakill consisted of six champions: Kayle, Karthus, Mordekaiser, Olaf, Sona, and Yorick. In 2021, Viego was introduced to the group. Their music was primarily made by Riot Games's in-house music team but featured cameos by [Mötley Crüe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%B6tley_Cr%C3%BCe "Mötley Crüe") drummer [Tommy Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy_Lee "Tommy Lee") and [Danny Lohner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danny_Lohner "Danny Lohner"), a former member of industrial rock band [Nine Inch Nails](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nine_Inch_Nails "Nine Inch Nails"). Their second album, _Grasp of the Undying_, reached number one on the [iTunes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITunes "ITunes") metal charts in 2017.[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-lawson-173)

Pentakill was followed by [K/DA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K/DA "K/DA"), a [virtual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtual_band "Virtual band") K-pop [girl group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Girl_group "Girl group") composed of four champions, Ahri, Akali, Evelynn, and Kai'sa. As with Pentakill, K/DA is promotional material for a skin line by the same name.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-174) The group's debut single, "[Pop/Stars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop/Stars "Pop/Stars")", which premiered at the [2018 _League of Legends_ World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_League_of_Legends_World_Championship "2018 League of Legends World Championship"), garnered over 400 million views on YouTube and sparked widespread interest from people unfamiliar with _League of Legends_.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-175) In August 2020, Riot Games released "[The Baddest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Baddest_(K/DA_song) "The Baddest (K/DA song)")", the pre-release single for _[All Out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All\_Out\_(EP) "All Out (EP)")_, the five-track [EP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EP "EP") from K/DA which followed in November that year.[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-176)

In 2019, Riot created a virtual [hip hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip_hop "Hip hop") group called True Damage,[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-177) featuring the champions Akali, Yasuo, Qiyana, Senna, and Ekko.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-polygon1-178) The vocalists—[Keke Palmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keke_Palmer "Keke Palmer"), [Thutmose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thutmose_(musician) "Thutmose (musician)"), [Becky G](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Becky_G "Becky G"), [Duckwrth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duckwrth "Duckwrth"), and [Soyeon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soyeon "Soyeon")—performed a live version of the group's debut song, "Giants", during the opening ceremony of the [2019 _League of Legends_ World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_League_of_Legends_World_Championship "2019 League of Legends World Championship"), alongside holographic versions of their characters.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-polygon1-178) The in-game cosmetics promoted by the music video featured a collaboration with fashion house [Louis Vuitton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Vuitton "Louis Vuitton").[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-179)

In 2023, Riot formed Heartsteel, a virtual [boy band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_band "Boy band"), comprising the champions Aphelios, Ezreal, Kayn, K'Sante, Sett, and Yone. The vocalists are [Baekhyun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baekhyun "Baekhyun") from the K-pop groups [Exo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exo "Exo") and [SuperM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SuperM "SuperM"), Cal Scruby, [ØZI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%98ZI "ØZI"), and [Tobi Lou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tobi_Lou "Tobi Lou"). Heartsteel's debut single "Paranoia" was released in October of that year.[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-180)

### Comics

Riot announced a collaboration with [Marvel Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Comics "Marvel Comics") in 2018.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-Liao-91) Riot had previously experimented with releasing comics through its website.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-181)[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-182) Shannon Liao of _[The Verge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Verge "The Verge")_ noted that the comic books were "a rare opportunity for Riot to showcase its years of lore that has often appeared as an afterthought".[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-Liao-91) The first comic was _League of Legends: Ashe—Warmother_, which debuted in 2018, followed by _League of Legends: Lux_ that same year.[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-183) A print version of the latter was released in 2019.[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-184)

### _Arcane_

While celebrating _League of Legends_'s tenth anniversary, Riot announced an animated television series, _Arcane._[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-hollywoodreporter.com-185) It was the company's first production for television,[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:17-186) and a collaboration between Riot Games and animation studio [Fortiche Production](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortiche_Production "Fortiche Production").[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:17-186) The series is set in the technologically advanced city of Piltover and its oppressed, underground sister city of Zaun.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:17-186)[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-187)_Arcane_ explores adult themes and is not intended for children.[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-hollywoodreporter.com-185) It features multiple playable characters from _League of Legends_. [Hailee Steinfeld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hailee_Steinfeld "Hailee Steinfeld") stars as [Vi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vi_(League_of_Legends) "Vi (League of Legends)"), [Ella Purnell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ella_Purnell "Ella Purnell") as [Jinx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jinx_(League_of_Legends) "Jinx (League of Legends)"), [Kevin Alejandro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Alejandro "Kevin Alejandro") as Jayce, and [Katie Leung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katie_Leung "Katie Leung") as Caitlyn.[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-188)

After a delay caused by the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), the series premiered in November 2021 on [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") internationally and through [Tencent Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tencent_Video "Tencent Video") in China.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-:17-186) The first season received critical acclaim, winning four [Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmy_Awards "Emmy Awards") and nine [Annie Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annie_Awards "Annie Awards").[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-Variety_Arcane-189) After the success of the first season, Riot hired former executives from [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix"), HBO Max, and [Paramount Television Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount_Television_Studios "Paramount Television Studios") to expand its entertainment division,[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-190) and CEO Nicolo Laurent pledged to create an "entertainment company for the 21st century".[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-191) Ahead of the premiere of the second and final season, [_Variety_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)") reported that production and marketing costs for _Arcane_'s 18 episodes exceeded $250 million, making it the most expensive animated series ever made.[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-Variety_Arcane-189)

_[Bloomberg News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloomberg\_News "Bloomberg News")_ reported that Riot paid Netflix around $3 million for each episode aired and that the studio failed to convert the series' success into in-game revenue. Riot had no plan to recoup the show's costs but said the second season was "on track to break even".[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-192) The second season premiered in November 2024 to similar acclaim, winning seven Annie Awards in all nominated categories.[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-auto-193)[GKIDS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GKIDS "GKIDS") produced home media releases of the first season in 2024, including a collector's edition DVD, a 4K UHD steelbook, and [Blu-ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blu-ray "Blu-ray") variants. The collector's edition, 4k UHD, and 4k Blu-ray variants for season 2 came out in 2025.[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends#cite_note-auto-193)

**Christopher Hikaru Nakamura**[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hikaru_Nakamura#cite_note-fn-1) ([Japanese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_language "Japanese language"): 中村光; born December 9, 1987) is an American [chess grandmaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chess_grandmaster "Chess grandmaster"), [internet personality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet_personality "Internet personality"), five-time [U.S. Chess Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Chess_Champion "U.S. Chess Champion"), and the 2022 [World Fischer Random Chess Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIDE_World_Fischer_Random_Chess_Championship_2022 "FIDE World Fischer Random Chess Championship 2022"). A [chess prodigy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chess_prodigy "Chess prodigy"), he earned his grandmaster title at the age of 15, the youngest American at the time to do so. With a peak [rating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elo_rating_system "Elo rating system") of 2816, Nakamura is tied as the [tenth-highest-rated player in history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comparison_of_top_chess_players_throughout_history#Elo_system "Comparison of top chess players throughout history").

Nakamura has represented the United States at seven [Chess Olympiads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chess_Olympiad "Chess Olympiad") (2006, 2008, 2010, 2012, 2014, 2016, 2018), securing a team gold medal and two team bronze medals, and participated in three [Candidates Tournaments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candidates_Tournament "Candidates Tournament"), finishing second in the [2024 edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candidates_Tournament_2024 "Candidates Tournament 2024"), fourth in the [2022 edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candidates_Tournament_2022 "Candidates Tournament 2022"), and seventh in the [2016 edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candidates_Tournament_2016 "Candidates Tournament 2016"). In May 2014, when FIDE began publishing official [rapid and blitz chess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapid_and_blitz_chess "Rapid and blitz chess") ratings, Nakamura ranked No. 1 in the world on both lists.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hikaru_Nakamura#cite_note-chess-news.ru-2)

Since 2018, Nakamura has pursued a career as a [content creator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Content_creator "Content creator") and subsequently signed with an esports organization [TSM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TSM_(esports) "TSM (esports)"), later joining [Misfits Gaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_Gaming "Misfits Gaming") and then [Team Falcons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Falcons "Team Falcons"). Having popular channels on [Twitch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitch_(service) "Twitch (service)"), [Kick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kick_(service) "Kick (service)") and [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube"), Nakamura is one of the most popular chess streamers in the world, and is widely credited with contributing to the growth in popularity of [online chess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Online_chess "Online chess").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hikaru_Nakamura#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hikaru_Nakamura#cite_note-4)
