Neither element 119 nor element 120 was observed.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-search-81)

The team at the [Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_Berkeley_National_Laboratory "Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory") (LBNL) in [Berkeley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berkeley,_California "Berkeley, California"), [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California"), United States had made plans to use the 88-inch cyclotron to make new elements using 50 Ti projectiles.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-usprogram-65) (Such a plan had already been made before the [Russian invasion of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "Russian invasion of Ukraine") began in 2022, cutting off collaborations between the JINR and other institutes, in response to theoretical predictions that an attempt to produce element 120 would be feasible.)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-nelson-82) First, the 244 Pu+50 Ti reaction was tested, successfully creating two atoms of 290 Lv in 2024. Since this was successful, an attempt to make element 120 in the 249 Cf+50 Ti reaction was planned to begin in late 2025.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-83)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-84)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-85)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-86) The [Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_Livermore_National_Laboratory "Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory") (LLNL), which previously collaborated with the JINR, is collaborating with the LBNL on this project.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-nelson-82) By June 2025, updates were underway at the LBNL in preparation for the search for element 120,[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-87)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-88) and by September, the search had begun.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-89)

The JINR's plans to investigate the 249 Cf+50 Ti reaction in their new facility were disrupted by the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine, after which collaboration between the JINR and other institutes completely ceased due to sanctions. Thus, 249 Cf could no longer be used as a target, as it would have to be produced at the [Oak Ridge National Laboratory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak_Ridge_National_Laboratory "Oak Ridge National Laboratory") (ORNL) in the United States.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-90)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-91)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-ft-92) Instead, the 248 Cm+54 Cr reaction will be used.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-93) In 2023, the director of the JINR, [Grigory Trubnikov](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Grigory_Trubnikov&action=edit&redlink=1 "Grigory Trubnikov (page does not exist)"), stated that he hoped that the experiments to synthesise element 120 will begin in 2025.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-94) In preparation for this, the JINR reported success in the 238 U+54 Cr reaction in late 2023, making a new isotope of livermorium, [288 Lv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Livermorium-288 "Livermorium-288"). This was an unexpectedly good result; the aim had been to experimentally determine the cross-section of a reaction with 54 Cr projectiles and prepare for the synthesis of element 120. It is the first successful reaction producing a superheavy element using an actinide target and a projectile heavier than 48 Ca.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Lv288-95)

The team at the Heavy Ion Research Facility in [Lanzhou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lanzhou "Lanzhou"), which is operated by the [Institute of Modern Physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institute_of_Modern_Physics "Institute of Modern Physics") (IMP) of the [Chinese Academy of Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Academy_of_Sciences "Chinese Academy of Sciences"), also plans to synthesise elements 119 and 120. The reactions used will involve actinide targets (e.g. 243 Am, 248 Cm) and first-row transition metal projectiles (e.g. 50 Ti, 51 V, 54 Cr, 55 Mn).[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-96)

[Mendeleev's nomenclature for unnamed and undiscovered elements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mendeleev%27s_predicted_elements "Mendeleev's predicted elements") would call unbinilium _eka-[radium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radium "Radium")_.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-97) The 1979 IUPAC [recommendations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systematic_element_name "Systematic element name")[temporarily call it](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Placeholder_name "Placeholder name")_unbinilium_ (symbol _Ubn_) until it is discovered, the discovery is confirmed and a permanent name chosen.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-iupac-98) Although the IUPAC systematic names are widely used in the chemical community on all levels, from chemistry classrooms to advanced textbooks, scientists who work theoretically or experimentally on superheavy elements typically call it "element 120", with the symbol _E120_, _(120)_ or _120_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Haire-1)

## Predicted properties

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Unbinilium&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Predicted properties")]

### Nuclear stability and isotopes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Unbinilium&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Nuclear stability and isotopes")]

[![Image 5: A 2D graph with rectangular cells colored in black-and-white colors, spanning from the llc to the urc, with cells mostly becoming lighter closer to the latter](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/89/Island_of_Stability_derived_from_Zagrebaev.svg/960px-Island_of_Stability_derived_from_Zagrebaev.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Island_of_Stability_derived_from_Zagrebaev.svg)

A chart of nuclide stability as used by the Dubna team in 2010. Characterized isotopes are shown with borders. Beyond element 118 (oganesson, the last known element), the line of known nuclides is expected to rapidly enter a region of instability. The elliptical region encloses the predicted location of the island of stability, centered on element 112, [copernicium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copernicium "Copernicium").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-FOOTNOTEZagrebaevKarpovGreiner2013-66)

[![Image 6](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/70/Next_proton_shell.svg/330px-Next_proton_shell.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Next_proton_shell.svg)

Orbitals with high [azimuthal quantum number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Azimuthal_quantum_number "Azimuthal quantum number") are raised in energy, eliminating what would otherwise be a gap in orbital energy corresponding to a closed proton shell at element 114, as shown in the left diagram which does not take this effect into account. This raises the next proton shell to the region around element 120, as shown in the right diagram, potentially increasing the half-lives of element 119 and 120 isotopes.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Kratz-99)

The stability of nuclei decreases greatly with the increase in atomic number after [curium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curium "Curium"), element 96, whose half-life is four orders of magnitude longer than that of any currently known higher-numbered element. All isotopes with an atomic number above [101](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mendelevium "Mendelevium") undergo [radioactive decay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radioactive_decay "Radioactive decay") with half-lives of less than 30 hours. No elements with atomic numbers above 82 (after [lead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lead "Lead")) have stable isotopes.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-100) Nevertheless, because of reasons not yet well understood, there is a slight increase of nuclear stability around atomic numbers [110](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darmstadtium "Darmstadtium")–[114](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flerovium "Flerovium"), which leads to the appearance of what is known in nuclear physics as the "[island of stability](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Island_of_stability "Island of stability")". This concept, proposed by [University of California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Berkeley "University of California, Berkeley") professor [Glenn Seaborg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Seaborg "Glenn Seaborg"), explains why superheavy elements last longer than predicted.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-101)

Isotopes of unbinilium are predicted to have alpha decay half-lives of the order of [microseconds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsecond "Microsecond").[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-prc08ADNDT08-102)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-sciencedirect1-103) In a [quantum tunneling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_tunneling "Quantum tunneling") model with mass estimates from a macroscopic-microscopic model, the [alpha-decay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alpha_decay "Alpha decay") half-lives of several unbinilium [isotopes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isotope "Isotope") (292–304 Ubn) have been predicted to be around 1–20 microseconds.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-prc08ADNDT08-102)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-half-lifesall-104)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-105)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-sciencedirect1-103) Some heavier isotopes may be more stable; Fricke and Waber predicted 320 Ubn to be the most stable unbinilium isotope in 1971.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Fricke1971-3) Since unbinilium is expected to decay via a cascade of alpha decays leading to [spontaneous fission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spontaneous_fission "Spontaneous fission") around [copernicium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copernicium "Copernicium"), the total half-lives of unbinilium isotopes are also predicted to be measured in microseconds.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Haire-1)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Hofmann-67) This has consequences for the synthesis of unbinilium, as isotopes with half-lives below one microsecond would decay before reaching the detector.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Haire-1)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Hofmann-67) Nevertheless, new theoretical models show that the expected gap in energy between the [proton orbitals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_shell_model "Nuclear shell model") 2f 7/2 (filled at element 114) and 2f 5/2 (filled at element 120) is smaller than expected, so that element 114 no longer appears to be a stable spherical closed nuclear shell, and this energy gap may increase the stability of elements 119 and 120. The next [doubly magic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doubly_magic "Doubly magic") nucleus is now expected to be around the spherical 306 Ubb (element 122), but the expected low half-life and low production [cross section](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross_section_(physics) "Cross section (physics)") of this nuclide makes its synthesis challenging.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Kratz-99)

Given that element 120 fills the 2f 5/2 proton orbital, much attention has been given to the compound nucleus 302 Ubn* and its properties. Several experiments have been performed between 2000 and 2008 at the Flerov Laboratory of Nuclear Reactions in Dubna studying the fission characteristics of the compound nucleus 302 Ubn*. Two nuclear reactions have been used, namely 244 Pu+58 Fe and 238 U+64 Ni. The results have revealed how nuclei such as this fission predominantly by expelling closed shell nuclei such as 132[Sn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tin "Tin") (_[Z](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic\_number "Atomic number")_=50, _[N](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neutron\_number "Neutron number")_=82). It was also found that the yield for the fusion-fission pathway was similar between 48 Ca and 58 Fe projectiles, suggesting a possible future use of 58 Fe projectiles in superheavy element formation.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-106)

In 2008, the team at [GANIL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Acc%C3%A9l%C3%A9rateur_National_d%27Ions_Lourds "Grand Accélérateur National d'Ions Lourds"), France, described the results from a new technique which attempts to measure the fission [half-life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-life "Half-life") of a compound nucleus at high excitation energy, since the yields are significantly higher than from neutron evaporation channels. It is also a useful method for probing the effects of shell closures on the survivability of compound nuclei in the super-heavy region, which can indicate the exact position of the next proton shell (_Z_=114, 120, 124, or 126). The team studied the nuclear fusion reaction between uranium ions and a target of natural nickel:[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Natowitz-107)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Morjean-108)

238

92 U + nat

28 Ni → 296,298,299,300,302

120 Ubn* → fission
The results indicated that nuclei of unbinilium were produced at high (≈70 MeV) excitation energy which underwent fission with measurable half-lives just over 10−18 s.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Natowitz-107)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Morjean-108) Although very short (indeed insufficient for the element to be considered by [IUPAC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IUPAC "IUPAC") to exist, because a compound nucleus has no internal structure and its nucleons have not been arranged into shells until it has survived for 10−14 s, when it forms an electronic cloud),[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-109) the ability to measure such a process indicates a strong shell effect at _Z_=120. At lower excitation energy (see neutron evaporation), the effect of the shell will be enhanced and ground-state nuclei can be expected to have relatively long half-lives. This result could partially explain the relatively long half-life of 294 Og measured in experiments at Dubna. Similar experiments have indicated a similar phenomenon at [element 124](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbiquadium "Unbiquadium") but not for [flerovium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flerovium "Flerovium"), suggesting that the next proton shell does in fact lie beyond element 120.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Natowitz-107)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Morjean-108) In September 2007, the team at RIKEN began a program utilizing 248 Cm targets and have indicated future experiments to probe the possibility of 120 being the next proton magic number (and 184 being the next neutron magic number) using the aforementioned nuclear reactions to form 302 Ubn*, as well as 248 Cm+54 Cr. They also planned to further chart the region by investigating the nearby compound nuclei 296 Og*, 298 Og*, 306 Ubb*, and 308 Ubb*.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-110)

The most likely isotopes of unbinilium to be synthesised in the near future are 295 Ubn through 299 Ubn, because they can be produced in the 3n and 4n channels of the 249–251 Cf+50 Ti, 245 Cm+54 Cr, and 248 Cm+54 Cr reactions.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-jinr2024-111)

### Atomic and physical

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Unbinilium&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Atomic and physical")]

Being the second [period 8 element](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Period_8_element "Period 8 element"), unbinilium is predicted to be an alkaline earth metal, below [beryllium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beryllium "Beryllium"), [magnesium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnesium "Magnesium"), [calcium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcium "Calcium"), [strontium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strontium "Strontium"), [barium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barium "Barium"), and [radium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radium "Radium"). Each of these elements has two [valence electrons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valence_electron "Valence electron") in the outermost s-orbital (valence electron configuration _n_ s 2), which is easily lost in chemical reactions to form the +2 [oxidation state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxidation_state "Oxidation state"): thus the alkaline earth metals are rather [reactive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reactivity_(chemistry) "Reactivity (chemistry)") elements, with the exception of beryllium due to its small size. Unbinilium is predicted to continue the trend and have a valence electron configuration of 8s 2. It is therefore expected to behave much like its lighter [congeners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congener_(chemistry) "Congener (chemistry)"); however, it is also predicted to differ from the lighter alkaline earth metals in some properties.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Haire-1)

The main reason for the predicted differences between unbinilium and the other alkaline earth metals is the [spin–orbit (SO) interaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin%E2%80%93orbit_interaction "Spin–orbit interaction")—the mutual interaction between the electrons' motion and [spin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin_(physics) "Spin (physics)"). The SO interaction is especially strong for the superheavy elements because their electrons move faster—at velocities comparable to the [speed of light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speed_of_light "Speed of light")—than those in lighter atoms.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Thayer-4) In unbinilium atoms, it lowers the 7p and 8s electron energy levels, stabilizing the corresponding electrons, but two of the 7p electron energy levels are more stabilized than the other four.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Faegri-112) The effect is called subshell splitting, as it splits the 7p subshell into more-stabilized and the less-stabilized parts. Computational chemists understand the split as a change of the second ([azimuthal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Azimuthal_quantum_number "Azimuthal quantum number")) [quantum number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_number "Quantum number")_l_ from 1 to 1/2 and 3/2 for the more-stabilized and less-stabilized parts of the 7p subshell, respectively.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Thayer-4)[[l]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-113) Thus, the outer 8s electrons of unbinilium are stabilized and become harder to remove than expected, while the 7p 3/2 electrons are correspondingly destabilized, perhaps allowing them to participate in chemical reactions.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Haire-1) This stabilization of the outermost s-orbital (already significant in radium) is the key factor affecting unbinilium's chemistry, and causes all the trends for atomic and molecular properties of alkaline earth metals to reverse direction after barium.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Pershina-114)

Due to the stabilization of its outer 8s electrons, unbinilium's first [ionization energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ionization_energy "Ionization energy")—the energy required to remove an electron from a neutral atom—is predicted to be 6.0 eV, comparable to that of calcium.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Haire-1) The electron of the [hydrogen-like](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrogen-like_atom "Hydrogen-like atom") unbinilium atom—oxidized so it has only one electron, Ubn 119+—is predicted to move so quickly that its mass is 2.05 times that of a non-moving electron, a feature coming from the [relativistic effects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Relativistic_quantum_chemistry "Relativistic quantum chemistry"). For comparison, the figure for hydrogen-like radium is 1.30 and the figure for hydrogen-like barium is 1.095.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Thayer-4) According to simple extrapolations of relativity laws, that indirectly indicates the contraction of the [atomic radius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_radius "Atomic radius")[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Thayer-4) to around 200[pm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Picometer "Picometer"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Haire-1) very close to that of strontium (215 pm); the [ionic radius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ionic_radius "Ionic radius") of the Ubn 2+ ion is also correspondingly lowered to 160 pm.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Haire-1) The trend in electron affinity is also expected to reverse direction similarly at radium and unbinilium.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Pershina-114)

Unbinilium should be a [solid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solid "Solid") at room temperature, with melting point 680°C:[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-BFricke-116) this continues the downward trend down the group, being lower than the value 700°C for radium.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-117) The boiling point of unbinilium is expected to be around 1700°C, which is lower than that of all the previous elements in the group (in particular, radium boils at 1737°C), following the downward periodic trend.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Fricke1971-3) The density of unbinilium has been predicted to be 7 g/cm 3, continuing the trend of increasing density down the group: the value for radium is 5.5 g/cm 3.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Fricke1971-3)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-B&K-2)

| --- | --- | --- |
| Ca 2 | 4.277 | 0.14 |

The chemistry of unbinilium is predicted to be similar to that of the alkaline earth metals,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Haire-1) but it would probably behave more like calcium or strontium[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Haire-1) than barium or radium. Like strontium, unbinilium should react vigorously with air to form an oxide (UbnO) and with water to form the hydroxide (Ubn(OH)2), which would be a strong [base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Base_(chemistry) "Base (chemistry)"), and releasing [hydrogen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrogen "Hydrogen") gas. It should also react with the [halogens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halogen "Halogen") to form salts such as UbnCl 2.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-emsley-118) While these reactions would be expected from [periodic trends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Periodic_trends "Periodic trends"), their lowered intensity is somewhat unusual, as ignoring relativistic effects, periodic trends would predict unbinilium to be even more reactive than barium or radium. This lowered [reactivity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reactivity_(chemistry) "Reactivity (chemistry)") is due to the relativistic stabilization of unbinilium's valence electron, increasing unbinilium's first ionization energy and decreasing the [metallic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metallic_radius "Metallic radius") and [ionic radii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ionic_radius "Ionic radius");[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-EB-119) this effect is already seen for radium.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Haire-1) On the other hand, the ionic radius of the Ubn 2+ ion is predicted to be larger than that of Sr 2+, because the 7p orbitals are destabilized and are thus larger than the p-orbitals of the lower shells.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Thayer-4)

Unbinilium may also show the +4 [oxidation state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxidation_state "Oxidation state"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Haire-1) which is not seen in any other alkaline earth metal,[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Greenwood&Earnshaw-120) in addition to the +2 oxidation state that is characteristic of the other alkaline earth metals and is also the main oxidation state of all the known alkaline earth metals: this is because of the destabilization and expansion of the 7p 3/2 spinor, causing its outermost electrons to have a lower ionization energy than what would otherwise be expected.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Haire-1)[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Greenwood&Earnshaw-120) The +6 state involving all the 7p 3/2 electrons has been suggested in a [hexafluoride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hexafluoride "Hexafluoride"), UbnF 6.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Cao2-121) The +1 state may also be isolable.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Thayer-4) Many unbinilium compounds are expected to have a large [covalent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Covalent "Covalent") character, due to the involvement of the 7p 3/2 electrons in the bonding: this effect is also seen to a lesser extent in radium, which shows some 6s and 6p 3/2 contribution to the bonding in [radium fluoride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radium_fluoride "Radium fluoride") (RaF 2) and astatide (RaAt 2), resulting in these compounds having more covalent character.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Thayer-4) The [standard reduction potential](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_reduction_potential "Standard reduction potential") of the Ubn 2+/Ubn couple is predicted to be −2.9 V, which is almost exactly the same as that for the Sr 2+/Sr couple of strontium (−2.899 V).[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-BFricke-116)

In the gas phase, the alkaline earth metals do not usually form covalently bonded diatomic molecules like the alkali metals do, since such molecules would have the same number of electrons in the bonding and antibonding orbitals and would have very low [dissociation energies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dissociation_energy "Dissociation energy").[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Be2-122) Thus, the M–M bonding in these molecules is predominantly through [van der Waals forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Van_der_Waals_force "Van der Waals force").[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Pershina-114) The metal–metal [bond lengths](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bond_length "Bond length") in these M 2 molecules increase down the group from Ca 2 to Ubn 2. On the other hand, their metal–metal [bond-dissociation energies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bond-dissociation_energy "Bond-dissociation energy") generally increase from Ca 2 to Ba 2 and then drop to Ubn 2, which should be the most weakly bound of all the group 2 homodiatomic molecules. The cause of this trend is the increasing participation of the p 3/2 and d electrons as well as the relativistically contracted s orbital.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Pershina-114) From these M 2 dissociation energies, the [enthalpy of sublimation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enthalpy_of_sublimation "Enthalpy of sublimation") (Δ _H_ sub) of unbinilium is predicted to be 150 kJ/mol.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Pershina-114)

The Ubn–[Au](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold "Gold") bond should be the weakest of all bonds between gold and an alkaline earth metal, but should still be stable. This gives extrapolated medium-sized adsorption enthalpies (−Δ _H_ ads) of 172 kJ/mol on gold (the radium value should be 237 kJ/mol) and 50 kJ/mol on [silver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver "Silver"), the smallest of all the alkaline earth metals, that demonstrate that it would be feasible to study the [chromatographic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromatography "Chromatography")[adsorption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adsorption "Adsorption") of unbinilium onto surfaces made of [noble metals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noble_metal "Noble metal").[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Pershina-114) The Δ _H_ sub and −Δ _H_ ads values are correlated for the alkaline earth metals.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unbinilium#cite_note-Pershina-114)

**James Trevor Oliver**[MBE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire "Member of the Order of the British Empire")[OSI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_Star_of_Italy "Order of the Star of Italy") (born 27 May 1975) is an English [celebrity chef](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_chef "Celebrity chef"), restaurateur and cookbook author.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-1) He is known for his casual approach to cuisine, and he has fronted many television shows and opened numerous restaurants.

Oliver reached the public eye when his [BBC Two](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Two "BBC Two") series _[The Naked Chef](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Naked\_Chef "The Naked Chef")_ premiered in 1999. In 2005, he started a campaign, [Feed Me Better](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie%27s_School_Dinners "Jamie's School Dinners"), to introduce schoolchildren to healthier foods, which was later backed by the government. He was the owner of a restaurant chain, Jamie Oliver Restaurant Group, which opened its first restaurant, Jamie's Italian, in 2008. The chain went into [administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Administration_(law) "Administration (law)") in May 2019.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-2)

Oliver is a best-selling British non-fiction author. As of February 2019, Oliver had sold more than 14.55 million books. His [TED Talk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TED_(conference) "TED (conference)") won him the 2010 [TED Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TED_Prize "TED Prize"). In June 2003, Oliver was made a [Member of the Order of the British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire "Member of the Order of the British Empire") for "services to the hospitality industry".

Jamie Trevor Oliver[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-hello-3) was born and raised in [Clavering, Essex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clavering,_Essex "Clavering, Essex").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-5) His parents, Trevor and Sally ([née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name") Palmer) Oliver, ran a pub and restaurant, the Cricketers, where he practised cooking in the kitchen with his parents.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-Hello-6) He has a sister, and was educated at [Newport Free Grammar School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newport_Free_Grammar_School "Newport Free Grammar School"), in [Newport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newport,_Essex "Newport, Essex").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-7) A surprise revelation from 2009 suggested he had a sixth-generation [Sudanese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan "Sudan") ancestor through his grandfather's side.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-8)

He left school at the age of 16 with two [GCSE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Certificate_of_Secondary_Education "General Certificate of Secondary Education") qualifications in art and geology[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-9) and went on to attend Westminster Technical College (now [Westminster Kingsway College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westminster_Kingsway_College "Westminster Kingsway College")).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-Hello-6) He earned a [City & Guilds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_%26_Guilds "City & Guilds")[National Vocational Qualification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Vocational_Qualification "National Vocational Qualification") (NVQ) in [home economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_economics "Home economics").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-10)

[![Image 2](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8a/Jamie_Oliver_cooking.jpg/250px-Jamie_Oliver_cooking.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jamie_Oliver_cooking.jpg)

Oliver cooking at one of the [Scandic Hotels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scandic_Hotels "Scandic Hotels") in 2014

Oliver's first job was a [pastry chef](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pastry_chef "Pastry chef") at [Antonio Carluccio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Carluccio "Antonio Carluccio")'s Neal Street restaurant, where he first gained experience at preparing [Italian cuisine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_cuisine "Italian cuisine"), and developed a relationship with his mentor [Gennaro Contaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gennaro_Contaldo "Gennaro Contaldo"); later in his career Oliver employed Contaldo to help run his chain of high street restaurants, Jamie's Italian.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-11) Oliver moved to the [River Cafe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_River_Cafe_(London) "The River Cafe (London)") in Fulham, as a [sous-chef](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sous-chef "Sous-chef"). He was noticed there by the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") in 1997, after making an unscripted appearance in the documentary _Christmas at the River Cafe_.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-The_Guardian-12)

In 1999, Oliver's [BBC Two](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Two "BBC Two") show _[The Naked Chef](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Naked\_Chef "The Naked Chef")_ debuted, and his cookbook became a bestseller in the United Kingdom.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-nytimes.com-13) That same year, he was invited to prepare lunch for Prime Minister [Tony Blair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Blair "Tony Blair") at [10 Downing Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10_Downing_Street "10 Downing Street").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-nytimes.com-13) After three series of _Naked Chef_ programmes (_The Naked Chef_, _Return of the Naked Chef_ and _Happy Days with The Naked Chef_) for the BBC, Oliver moved to [Channel 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channel_4 "Channel 4") in 2002,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-14) following BBC Two's decision not to renew his contract with the network, after Oliver had appeared in similarly-themed TV cookery advertisements for [Sainsbury's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sainsbury%27s "Sainsbury's") supermarket.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-15)

His first Channel 4 series was a documentary, _[Jamie's Kitchen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie%27s\_Kitchen "Jamie's Kitchen")_, which began in November 2002, and followed the setting up of Fifteen restaurant in London.

Oliver's [holding company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holding_company "Holding company"), Jamie Oliver Holdings Ltd., earned enough for Oliver to be listed on _[The Sunday Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sunday\_Times "The Sunday Times")_ list of richest Britons under 30 in 2005.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-17) Oliver's net worth was estimated in 2014 at £240 million.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-DT-18) A decade later, his net worth was estimated at £173 million.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-19) Oliver was chosen by [Disney Pixar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney_Pixar "Disney Pixar") to provide the voice of the health inspector in the UK version of _[Ratatouille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ratatouille\_(film) "Ratatouille (film)")_.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-20) In December 2009, Oliver received the 2010 [TED Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TED_Prize "TED Prize").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-Time-21) He hosted _[Jamie's 15 Minute Meals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie%27s\_15\_Minute\_Meals "Jamie's 15 Minute Meals")_ on [Channel 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channel_4 "Channel 4"), which aired for 40 episodes in 2012.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-22)

[![Image 3](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d9/Burgers_at_Jamie%27s_italian.jpg/250px-Burgers_at_Jamie%27s_italian.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Burgers_at_Jamie%27s_italian.jpg)

Burgers at Jamie's Italian at Oxford

Oliver's restaurant Fifteen, in Westland Place, London continued to train young adults who have a disadvantaged background for careers in the restaurant business until its closure on 21 May 2019.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-24)

The Fifteen Foundation opened further restaurants in [Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam "Amsterdam"), [Cornwall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornwall "Cornwall") (May 2006) and [Fifteen Melbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteen_Melbourne "Fifteen Melbourne"), Australia (September 2006). The Melbourne restaurant cut ties with Oliver in 2011. The London, Amsterdam and Cornwall restaurants closed in 2019 when his restaurant group went into administration.

In June 2008, Oliver launched a restaurant, Jamie's Italian, his first high street business venture, in [Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford "Oxford"), England.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-25) At its peak, there were 42 Jamie's Italian restaurants in the UK. The brand was franchised via the Jamie Oliver Restaurant Group (JORG), and included branches in Australia (which Oliver part-bought back in November 2016 after its founders went bankrupt),[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-26) Canada, Cyprus, Hong Kong, Iceland, Ireland, Qatar, Russia, Taiwan, Turkey, the UAE and Singapore.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-:0-27)

In 2011, Oliver, an advocate of cooking meals from scratch and using local produce, caused controversy after it turned out the sauces used in Jamie's Italian in Glasgow were from an industrial park almost 400 miles (640 km) away in [Bicester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicester "Bicester").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-28) That same year, he came under fire for lack of food safety protections in his restaurants and illnesses associated with under-cooking mincemeat that may have been contaminated with _E. coli_.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-29)

In 2011, Oliver set up Barbecoa, a barbecued meat-based restaurant with his friend, American barbecue expert Adam Perry Lang. There were two outlets, both in London, one in Piccadilly and a second in [St Pauls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_London "City of London"). In 2014 the Piccadilly outlet voluntarily closed for 24 hours after hygiene inspectors gave it the second-lowest rating. _[The Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Times "The Times")_ reported they had found mouse droppings, mouldy carcasses and out-of-date meat.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-30) In February 2018, JORG confirmed that they had "instructed a firm of [real estate agents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_estate_agent "Real estate agent") to ascertain the potential value and market suitability of two of our sites".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-31) On 19 February 2018, Barbecoa Ltd went into administration, with Oliver immediately buying back the St Paul's site in a pre-packed agreement via a new subsidiary.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-32)

In 2014, he partnered with [Toronto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto "Toronto") restaurateur King Street Co. and executive chef Rob Gentile to open 10 planned branches of Jamie's Italian, including a location in [Yorkdale Shopping Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yorkdale_Shopping_Centre "Yorkdale Shopping Centre"). The business collapsed in 2020.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-33)

In January 2017, chief executive Simon Blagden announced the closure of six restaurants in the UK affecting 120 jobs, at sites in [Aberdeen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aberdeen "Aberdeen"), [Cheltenham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheltenham "Cheltenham"), [Exeter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exeter "Exeter"), [Royal Tunbridge Wells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Tunbridge_Wells "Royal Tunbridge Wells"), and in London at [Ludgate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludgate "Ludgate") and [Richmond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richmond,_London "Richmond, London").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-:0-27)

In January 2018, as part of an agreement with creditors to secure £71.5M of debt, JORG proposed to enter the UK company Jamie's Italian Ltd into a [company voluntary arrangement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Company_voluntary_arrangement "Company voluntary arrangement"), seeking rent reductions on eight outlets and closing a further 12 in [Bath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bath,_Somerset "Bath, Somerset"), [Bristol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bristol "Bristol"), [Bluewater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bluewater_(shopping_centre) "Bluewater (shopping centre)"), [Chelmsford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelmsford "Chelmsford"), [Harrogate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrogate "Harrogate"), [Kingston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingston_upon_Thames "Kingston upon Thames"), [Milton Keynes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milton_Keynes "Milton Keynes"), [Reading](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reading,_Berkshire "Reading, Berkshire"), and [St Albans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Albans "St Albans"), and [Greenwich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenwich "Greenwich"), [Piccadilly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piccadilly "Piccadilly") and [Threadneedle Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Threadneedle_Street "Threadneedle Street") in London. As part of the agreement, court papers revealed that Jamie's Italian had debts of £71.5m, including £2.3 million in wages owed to staff; £30.2 million of overdrafts and loans; £41.3 million owed to landlords, [HM Revenue and Customs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HM_Revenue_and_Customs "HM Revenue and Customs"), suppliers and other creditors; with £47 million of the debts covered by loans from [HSBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HSBC "HSBC") Bank and Oliver's other companies.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-36)

The group went into [administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Administration_(law) "Administration (law)") on 21 May 2019 with 22 of 25 restaurants closed and 1,000 jobs lost.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-37) Jamie's Italian restaurants and Jamie Oliver's Diner at [Gatwick Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gatwick_Airport "Gatwick Airport") continued operations until they were sold to catering company [SSP Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SSP_Group "SSP Group"). Jamie Oliver's Fifteen Cornwall at Watergate Bay, as well as 61 overseas locations and the catering services operated by [Aramark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aramark "Aramark") in the U.S., are all operated by franchisees so they were unaffected.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-38) In January 2020, [KPMG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KPMG "KPMG"), the firm administrators, said that most of the £80 million the chain owed after its collapse will not be recovered. Hundreds of suppliers, as well as some town councils, will bear the brunt of the losses.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-39) In 2020, an [employment tribunal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Employment_tribunal "Employment tribunal") ruled that Oliver's restaurants had broken labour laws by failing to consult employees prior to making them redundant.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-41)

In November 2023, Oliver opened a new restaurant, Jamie Oliver Catherine Street, in London, his first since the collapse of Jamie's Italian. It was launched in partnership with [Andrew Lloyd Webber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Lloyd_Webber "Andrew Lloyd Webber")'s [LW Theatres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LW_Theatres "LW Theatres") at the [Theatre Royal, Drury Lane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theatre_Royal,_Drury_Lane "Theatre Royal, Drury Lane").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-42) In March 2024, Oliver opened a restaurant in [Serbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serbia "Serbia"), Jamie's Italian Belgrade, in the [Belgrade Waterfront](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgrade_Waterfront "Belgrade Waterfront") quarter.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-43) In March 2026, Oliver reopened Jamie's Italian in London, backed by the investors of the Italian chain [Prezzo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prezzo_(restaurant) "Prezzo (restaurant)").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-44)

### Other media appearances

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jamie_Oliver&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Other media appearances")]

Oliver has twice guest-hosted Channel 4's _[The Friday Night Project](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Friday\_Night\_Project "The Friday Night Project")_ and has appeared twice in the "Star in a Reasonably-Priced Car" segment of [BBC Two](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Two "BBC Two")'s _[Top Gear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top\_Gear\_(2002\_TV\_series) "Top Gear (2002 TV series)")_. In his first appearance he attempted to make a green salad in the back of his [Volkswagen Microbus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volkswagen_Microbus "Volkswagen Microbus"), which was fitted with a [Porsche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porsche "Porsche") engine, while [the Stig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Stig "The Stig") drove it around the [_Top Gear_ test track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top_Gear_test_track "Top Gear test track").[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-100)

Oliver is the second British celebrity chef (after [Robert Irvine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Irvine "Robert Irvine")) to appear as a challenger on _[Iron Chef America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron\_Chef\_America "Iron Chef America"),_ taking on Iron Chef [Mario Batali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Batali "Mario Batali") in 2008 in a losing battle with [cobia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cobia "Cobia") as the theme ingredient.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-101)

Oliver was one of the judges in the _[Oprah's Big Give](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oprah%27s\_Big\_Give "Oprah's Big Give")_ hosted by [Oprah Winfrey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oprah_Winfrey "Oprah Winfrey") in the United States in 2008.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-102)

Oliver had an Australian tour in 2006, when he performed in Sydney and Melbourne. Following the entertaining format of his first live show, the 2006 Australian tour featured special guests including mentor [Gennaro Contaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gennaro_Contaldo "Gennaro Contaldo"), and students from Fifteen London. He performed a new song written by Leigh Haggerwood called _Fish Stew_ which Oliver cooked to and also drummed along to at the end of the show. The shows were featured in a one-off TV documentary called _Jamie Oliver: Australian Diary_.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-103)

On 27 December 2022, Oliver was the guest editor on the [_Today_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Today_(BBC_Radio_4) "Today (BBC Radio 4)") Programme on [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") Radio 4.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-104)

Oliver appeared as himself in the music video for Irish singer [CMAT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CMAT "CMAT")’s single "The Jamie Oliver Petrol Station", which was released on 14 March 2026.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-105)

From June 2000, Oliver became the public face of the [Sainsbury's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sainsbury%27s "Sainsbury's") supermarket chain in the UK, appearing on television and radio advertisements and in-store promotional material. The deal earned him an estimated £1.2 million every year.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-nytimes.com-13)[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-106)

He was criticised by [Sainsbury's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sainsbury%27s "Sainsbury's") CEO [Justin King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_King_(businessman) "Justin King (businessman)") after Oliver criticised the "junk" sold by supermarkets that ends up in the lunchboxes of millions of children. King reportedly hit back, saying: "Dictating to people—or unleashing an expletive-filled tirade—is not the way to get engagement."[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-107) In July 2011, after eleven years, the partnership between Oliver and Sainsbury's ended. The final television advertisement was for Christmas 2011.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-108)

Oliver also promotes a range of non-stick pans and cookware for [Tefal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tefal "Tefal") and has appeared in Australian television commercials for [Yalumba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yalumba "Yalumba") wines, using [Del Boy's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Only_Fools_and_Horses "Only Fools and Horses") catchphrase of "Lovely Jubbly".[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-109)

In August 2013, Oliver and Canadian supermarket chain [Sobeys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sobeys "Sobeys") announced a partnership in improving nationwide nutrition and advertising campaigns.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-110)

In October 2013, he began a partnership with the Australian supermarket chain [Woolworths](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woolworths_(Australia) "Woolworths (Australia)") on a series of better nutrition initiatives and advertising campaigns.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-111) In 2014, Oliver became the culinary face of Woolworths.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-112) Oliver came under strong criticism over the funding of the advertising surrounding his relationship with the supermarket.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-113)

In January 2016, Oliver and [HelloFresh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HelloFresh "HelloFresh"), an international meal kit subscription service, announced a partnership to incorporate his recipes to the weekly subscription deliveries. Customers receive one recipe written by Oliver with all the exact ingredients and steps for the dish.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-114)

In September 2018, Oliver created a series of recipes and tips for [Tesco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesco "Tesco") and participated in the promotion of the company's food products.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-115)

In 2019, Oliver partnered with [Royal Dutch Shell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Dutch_Shell "Royal Dutch Shell") to offer a Jamie Oliver Deli by Shell branded range at 500 Shell petrol stations in the UK for £5 million. The deal was criticised as a way to improve their image due to Shell's lack of action on climate change, corruption and bribery allegations and damaged Oliver's image of working in the interests of children and for action on climate change.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-116)[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-117)[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-118)[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-119)[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-120)[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-121)

## Charity work and campaigning

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jamie_Oliver&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Charity work and campaigning")]

Oliver conceived and established the [Fifteen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteen_(restaurant) "Fifteen (restaurant)") charity restaurant, where he trained disadvantaged young people to work in the hospitality industry. Following the success of the original restaurant in London, more Fifteens have opened around the globe: Fifteen Amsterdam opened in December 2004, Fifteen [Cornwall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornwall "Cornwall") in Newquay in May 2006 and [Fifteen Melbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteen_Melbourne "Fifteen Melbourne") in September 2006 with an Australian friend and fellow chef [Tobie Puttock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tobie_Puttock "Tobie Puttock").[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-Kids_in_the_kitchen-122) Fifteen Melbourne has since closed, as has Fifteen Cornwall.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-123)[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-124)

In 2005, Oliver initiated a campaign originally called "Feed Me Better" to move British schoolchildren towards eating healthy foods and cutting out [junk food](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junk_food "Junk food"). As a result, the British government also pledged to address the issue. His public campaign for changes in nutrition resulted in people voting him as the "Most Inspiring Political Figure of 2005", according to a [Channel 4 News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channel_4_News "Channel 4 News") annual viewer poll.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-nytimes.com-13) His emphasis on cooking fresh, nutritious food continued as he created _Jamie's Ministry of Food_, a television series where Oliver travelled to inspire everyday people in [Rotherham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotherham "Rotherham"), [Yorkshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yorkshire "Yorkshire"), to cook healthy meals. Another television series is _[Jamie Oliver's Food Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie\_Oliver%27s\_Food\_Revolution "Jamie Oliver's Food Revolution")_ (2010–11), where he travelled first to [Huntington, West Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntington,_West_Virginia "Huntington, West Virginia") and then to [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") to change the way Americans eat, and address their dependence on fast food.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-nytimes.com-13)

Oliver began a formal campaign to ban unhealthy food in British schools and to get children eating nutritious food instead. Oliver's efforts to bring radical change to the school meals system, chronicled in the series _Jamie's School Dinners_, challenged the junk-food culture by showing schools they could serve healthy, cost-efficient meals that kids enjoyed eating.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-125) His efforts brought the subject of school dinners to the political forefront and changed the types of food served in schools.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-126)

In December 2009, Oliver was awarded the 2010 TED Prize for his campaigns to "create change on both the individual and governmental levels" to "bring attention to the changes that the English, and now Americans, need to make in their lifestyles and diet".[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-Time-21) In 2010, he joined several other celebrity chefs on the series _The Big Fish Fight_, in which Oliver and fellow chefs [Hugh Fearnley-Whittingstall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugh_Fearnley-Whittingstall "Hugh Fearnley-Whittingstall") and [Gordon Ramsay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gordon_Ramsay "Gordon Ramsay") made a variety of programmes [_[clarification needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Please\_clarify "Wikipedia:Please clarify")_] to raise awareness about the discarding of hundreds of thousands of saltwater fish because the fishermen are prohibited from keeping any fish other than the stated target of the trawl.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-127) He is a patron of environmental charity [Trees for Cities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trees_for_Cities "Trees for Cities").[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-128)

In April 2022, he co-organized together with Ukrainian chef [Yurii Kovryzhenko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yurii_Kovryzhenko "Yurii Kovryzhenko") a charity dinner in London within an initiative #CookForUkraine to raise money for Ukrainians who suffered from Russian invasion of Ukraine.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-129)

Oliver and Gordon Ramsay are spokespeople for the "Big Fish Fight", which campaigns for sustainable seafood, but were criticised for their use of endangered fish.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-130)[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-131)

Oliver has been criticised for underestimating the cost of supposedly cheap food he encouraged poor people to prepare for themselves, as well as for an unrealistic view of poverty in [Britain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_in_the_United_Kingdom "Poverty in the United Kingdom") and [round the Mediterranean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Mediterranean "Northern Mediterranean").[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-132)[Cookery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cooking "Cooking") writer and poverty campaigner [Jack Monroe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Monroe "Jack Monroe") stated that Oliver's comments "support damaging myths that poor people are only poor because they spend their money on the wrong things, rather than being constrained by time, equipment, knowledge or practicalities".[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-133)

## Views and criticism

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jamie_Oliver&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Views and criticism")]

Oliver has spoken out against [Marco Pierre White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Pierre_White "Marco Pierre White"), who has been critical of Oliver in the past, and at the profanity with which chef [Gordon Ramsay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gordon_Ramsay "Gordon Ramsay") speaks to his staff.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-134)

In February 2017, Oliver criticised the [Red Tractor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Tractor "Red Tractor") scheme, earning the ire of farming leaders, such as [Minette Batters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minette_Batters "Minette Batters"), the president of the NFU. Oliver said: "Chickens are bred to grow fast with a high ratio of meat to bone, but this makes them heavy so they can struggle to walk...I think people would be shocked by the reality of what we are buying...I personally wouldn't feed it to my kids."[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-135) Batters responded: "There are a lot of people on tight budgets and they must not be disadvantaged in all of this. It is about making sure we can provide quality affordable, safe, traceable food to everybody regardless of budgets, regardless of background."[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-136)

In 2005, Oliver was widely criticised by animal rights groups for slaughtering a lamb on his TV show without first stunning it, with [PETA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PETA "PETA") stating that it showed to the public problems with the methods used within slaughterhouses. PETA spokesman Sean Gifford said that it was hoped the footage "could turn the more die-hard carnivore into a vegetarian". TV regulator [Ofcom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ofcom "Ofcom") reported seven complaints from the public.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-137)

On 13 May 2001, Oliver's series _The Naked Chef_ won the BAFTA award for _Best Feature_ at the prestigious [2001 British Academy Television Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_British_Academy_Television_Awards "2001 British Academy Television Awards"), held at the [Grosvenor House Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grosvenor_House_Hotel "Grosvenor House Hotel") in [Park Lane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Lane "Park Lane"), [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London").[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-138)

In June 2003, Oliver was awarded the MBE in the [Queen's Birthday Honours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen%27s_Birthday_Honours "Queen's Birthday Honours").[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-139)

On 21 August 2010, Oliver won an Emmy for _[Jamie Oliver's Food Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie\_Oliver%27s\_Food\_Revolution "Jamie Oliver's Food Revolution")_ at the [62nd Primetime Creative Arts Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/62nd_Primetime_Creative_Arts_Emmy_Awards "62nd Primetime Creative Arts Emmy Awards"). The series tackled the problem of childhood obesity in America.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-140)

In 2013, Oliver was awarded an Honorary Fellowship by the [Royal College of General Practitioners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_College_of_General_Practitioners "Royal College of General Practitioners") for his work in tackling [childhood obesity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Childhood_obesity "Childhood obesity") by improving the nutritional value of school dinners.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-141)

In 2019, Oliver was awarded the [Order of the Star of Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_Star_of_Italy "Order of the Star of Italy") with the rank of Knight.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-142) The investiture took place at the Italian embassy in 2021.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-143)

In July 2000, Oliver married the former model and writer Juliette Norton, usually known as "Jools".[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-144) They have five children.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-145)[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-146) Oliver has severe [dyslexia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dyslexia "Dyslexia"), and read his first novel, _[Catching Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catching\_Fire "Catching Fire")_, by American novelist [Suzanne Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suzanne_Collins "Suzanne Collins") (the second book in the three-book _[The Hunger Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hunger\_Games "The Hunger Games")_ series) in 2013, at the age of 38.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-147)

During the summer of 2019, Oliver and his family moved into [Spains Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spains_Hall "Spains Hall"), the 16th-century mansion in [Finchingfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finchingfield "Finchingfield"), [Essex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Essex "Essex"). The property is located on a 70-acre (28 ha) estate and includes a six-bedroom farmhouse, three-bedroom lodge, swimming pool, tennis court and converted stables.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Oliver#cite_note-148)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

This is a **list of international presidential trips made by Joe Biden**, the [46th](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_the_United_States "List of presidents of the United States") president of the United States. [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden") made 21 international trips to 28 countries (in addition to visiting the [West Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bank "West Bank")) during [his presidency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Joe_Biden "Presidency of Joe Biden"), which began on [January 20, 2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inauguration_of_Joe_Biden "Inauguration of Joe Biden") and ended on [January 20, 2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_inauguration_of_Donald_Trump "Second inauguration of Donald Trump"). Due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), Biden did not make any international trips between January and June 2021.

The number of visits per country where President Biden traveled are:

*   **One**: [Angola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angola "Angola"), [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil "Brazil"), [Cambodia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambodia "Cambodia"), [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada "Canada"), [Cape Verde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Verde "Cape Verde"), [Egypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt "Egypt"), [Finland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finland "Finland"), [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France "France"), [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India"), [Indonesia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesia "Indonesia"), [Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ireland "Ireland"), [Lithuania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithuania "Lithuania"), [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico "Mexico"), [Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peru "Peru"), [Saudi Arabia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabia "Saudi Arabia"), [South Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korea "South Korea"), [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain "Spain"), [Switzerland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland "Switzerland"), [Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukraine "Ukraine"), [Vatican City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vatican_City "Vatican City"), [Vietnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam "Vietnam") and the [West Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bank "West Bank")
*   **Two**: [Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium "Belgium"), [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany "Germany"), [Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel "Israel"), [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy "Italy"), [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan "Japan") and [Poland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poland "Poland")
*   **Six**: The [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom")

[![Image 1](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4d/President_Joe_Biden%27s_international_trips.png/960px-President_Joe_Biden%27s_international_trips.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:President_Joe_Biden%27s_international_trips.png)

| **1** | ![Image 2: United Kingdom](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a5/Flag_of_the_United_Kingdom_%281-2%29.svg/40px-Flag_of_the_United_Kingdom_%281-2%29.svg.png)United Kingdom | [Mildenhall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mildenhall,_Suffolk "Mildenhall, Suffolk"), [St Ives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Ives,_Cornwall "St Ives, Cornwall"), [Bodelva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bodelva "Bodelva"), [Windsor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windsor,_Berkshire "Windsor, Berkshire") | June 9–13 | Attended the [47th G7 summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/47th_G7_summit "47th G7 summit") at the [Carbis Bay Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbis_Bay_Hotel "Carbis Bay Hotel"). Met with [Queen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monarchy_of_the_United_Kingdom "Monarchy of the United Kingdom")[Elizabeth II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_II "Elizabeth II") at [Windsor Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windsor_Castle "Windsor Castle") and Prime Minister [Boris Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Johnson "Boris Johnson"). Both Biden and Johnson issued a revision of the [Atlantic Charter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Atlantic_Charter "New Atlantic Charter") which had previously been issued by their predecessors, [Franklin Roosevelt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin_Roosevelt "Franklin Roosevelt") and [Winston Churchill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill "Winston Churchill") respectively, eighty years prior.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_presidential_trips_made_by_Joe_Biden#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_presidential_trips_made_by_Joe_Biden#cite_note-2) Participated in a meeting with the [G7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Group_of_Seven "Group of Seven") leaders and other members of the [Royal Family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_royal_family "British royal family") at [Eden Project](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eden_Project "Eden Project") in Bodelva. Also met with [US Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Air_Force "United States Air Force") personnel at [RAF Mildenhall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RAF_Mildenhall "RAF Mildenhall"). Stayed at [Tregenna Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tregenna_Castle "Tregenna Castle").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_presidential_trips_made_by_Joe_Biden#cite_note-foreign_trip_13-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_presidential_trips_made_by_Joe_Biden#cite_note-4) | [![Image 3](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/Family_photo_of_the_G7_leaders_at_Carbis_Bay_%281%29.jpg/250px-Family_photo_of_the_G7_leaders_at_Carbis_Bay_%281%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Family_photo_of_the_G7_leaders_at_Carbis_Bay_(1).jpg) |
| ![Image 4: Belgium](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/92/Flag_of_Belgium_%28civil%29.svg/40px-Flag_of_Belgium_%28civil%29.svg.png)Belgium | [Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels "Brussels") | June 13–15 | Attended the [31st NATO summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Brussels_NATO_summit "2021 Brussels NATO summit"). Met with [King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monarchy_of_Belgium "Monarchy of Belgium")[Philippe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippe_of_Belgium "Philippe of Belgium") and Prime Minister [Alexander De Croo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_De_Croo "Alexander De Croo") at the [Royal Palace of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Palace_of_Brussels "Royal Palace of Brussels"). Held multilateral meetings with the leaders of the [Baltic states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltic_states "Baltic states"), [Secretary General of NATO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary_General_of_NATO "Secretary General of NATO")[Jens Stoltenberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jens_Stoltenberg "Jens Stoltenberg"), and Turkish President [Recep Erdoğan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recep_Tayyip_Erdo%C4%9Fan "Recep Tayyip Erdoğan").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_presidential_trips_made_by_Joe_Biden#cite_note-foreign_trip_122-5) Also participated in an EU–US summit with European Council president [Charles Michel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Michel "Charles Michel") and European Commission president [Ursula von der Leyen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ursula_von_der_Leyen "Ursula von der Leyen") at the [Europa building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europa_building "Europa building"). Stayed at the [US Embassy in Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium%E2%80%93United_States_relations#Resident_diplomatic_missions "Belgium–United States relations").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_presidential_trips_made_by_Joe_Biden#cite_note-6) | [![Image 5](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ac/P20210615AS-0600_%2851267682502%29.jpg/250px-P20210615AS-0600_%2851267682502%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:P20210615AS-0600_(51267682502).jpg) |
| ![Image 6: Switzerland](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/08/Flag_of_Switzerland_%28Pantone%29.svg/20px-Flag_of_Switzerland_%28Pantone%29.svg.png)Switzerland | [Geneva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geneva "Geneva") | June 15–16 | Attended the [summit meeting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Russia%E2%80%93United_States_Summit "2021 Russia–United States Summit") with Russian President [Vladimir Putin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Putin "Vladimir Putin") at [Villa La Grange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parc_La_Grange "Parc La Grange"). Held a bilateral meeting with Swiss President [Guy Parmelin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guy_Parmelin "Guy Parmelin") and Swiss Foreign Minister [Ignazio Cassis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ignazio_Cassis "Ignazio Cassis") at the [InterContinental Geneva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/InterContinental_Geneva "InterContinental Geneva"), where he stayed.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_presidential_trips_made_by_Joe_Biden#cite_note-7) | [![Image 7](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/32/Putin_in_Switzerland_2021_10.jpg/250px-Putin_in_Switzerland_2021_10.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Putin_in_Switzerland_2021_10.jpg) |

Also held bilateral meeting with [Cardinal Secretary of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Secretary_of_State "Cardinal Secretary of State")[Pietro Parolin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pietro_Parolin "Pietro Parolin").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_presidential_trips_made_by_Joe_Biden#cite_note-8) | [![Image 9](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/72/Joe_Biden_met_with_Pope_Francis_again_at_the_Vatican_-_2021.jpg/250px-Joe_Biden_met_with_Pope_Francis_again_at_the_Vatican_-_2021.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Joe_Biden_met_with_Pope_Francis_again_at_the_Vatican_-_2021.jpg) |
