His first two successful singles as an artist were released by the next year, including "[Willingly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willingly "Willingly")" (a duet with his soon-to-be second wife, [Shirley Collie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shirley_Collie_Nelson "Shirley Collie Nelson"), which became his first charting single and first Top Ten at No.10) and "[Touch Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Touch_Me_(Willie_Nelson_song) "Touch Me (Willie Nelson song)")" (his second Top Ten, stalling at No.7).[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEdwardsCallahan2001-38) Nelson's tenure at Liberty yielded his first album entitled _[...And Then I Wrote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/...And\_Then\_I\_Wrote "...And Then I Wrote")_, released in September 1962.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBushMitchell200779-39) In 1963 Collie and Nelson were married in [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas "Las Vegas"). He then worked on the west coast offices of Pamper Records, in [Pico Rivera, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pico_Rivera,_California "Pico Rivera, California"). Since the job did not allow him the time to play music of his own, he left it and bought a ranch in [Ridgetop, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ridgetop,_Tennessee "Ridgetop, Tennessee"), outside of Nashville.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMyers19695-29)[Fred Foster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_Foster "Fred Foster") of [Monument Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monument_Records "Monument Records") signed Nelson in early 1964, but only one single was released: "I Never Cared For You".[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEScobey1982190-40)

By the fall of 1964, Nelson had moved to [RCA Victor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RCA_Victor "RCA Victor") at the behest of [Chet Atkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chet_Atkins "Chet Atkins"), signing a contract for $10,000 per year.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEReid2004[httpsbooksgooglecombooksid224pgPA224_224]-41)_[Country Willie – His Own Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country\_Willie\_%E2%80%93\_His\_Own\_Songs "Country Willie – His Own Songs")_ became Nelson's first RCA Victor album, recorded in April 1965. That same year he joined the [Grand Ole Opry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Ole_Opry "Grand Ole Opry"),[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPatoski2008Nashville,_1960-42) and he met and became friends with [Waylon Jennings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waylon_Jennings "Waylon Jennings") after watching one of his shows in [Phoenix, Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix,_Arizona "Phoenix, Arizona").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTENelsonShrakeShrake2000158-43) In 1967, he formed his backing band "The Record Men", featuring Johnny Bush, [Jimmy Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Day "Jimmy Day"), [Paul English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_English_(drummer) "Paul English (drummer)") and David Zettner.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBushMitchell2007137%E2%80%93138-44) During his first few years on RCA Victor, Nelson had no significant hits, but from November 1966 through March 1969, his singles reached the Top 25 in a consistent manner. "One in a Row" (#19, 1966), "The Party's Over" (#24 during a 16-week chart run in 1967), and his cover of [Morecambe & Wise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morecambe_%26_Wise "Morecambe & Wise")'s "Bring Me Sunshine" (#13, March 1969) were Nelson's best-selling records during his time with RCA.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDicair2007[httpsbooksgooglecombooksidMYMQl9dsKJECpgPA246_246]-26)

By 1970, most of Nelson's songwriting royalties were invested in tours that did not produce significant profits. In addition to the problems in his career, Nelson divorced Shirley Collie in 1970. In December, his ranch in Ridgetop, Tennessee, burned down. He interpreted the incident as a signal for a change. He moved to a ranch near [Bandera, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandera,_Texas "Bandera, Texas"), and married Connie Koepke. In early 1971 his single "I'm a Memory" reached the top 30.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKienzle2003[httpsbooksgooglecombooksidGq2TTa6TStkCpgPA248_248]-45) After he recorded his final RCA single, "Mountain Dew" (backed with "Phases, Stages, Circles, Cycles and Scenes"), in late April 1972, RCA requested that Nelson renew his contract ahead of schedule, with the implication that RCA would not release his latest recordings if he did not.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEReid2004[httpsbooksgooglecombooksidqCDF5fFuBT8CpgPA223_223]-46) Due to the failure of his albums, and particularly frustrated by the reception of _[Yesterday's Wine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yesterday%27s\_Wine "Yesterday's Wine")_, although his contract was not over, Nelson decided to retire from music.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTENelsonShrakeShrake2000167-47)

### Outlaw country and success (1972–1989)

Nelson moved to [Austin, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin,_Texas "Austin, Texas"), where the burgeoning hippie music scene (see [Armadillo World Headquarters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armadillo_World_Headquarters "Armadillo World Headquarters")) rejuvenated the singer. His popularity in Austin soared as he played his own brand of country music marked by country, folk and jazz influences.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEReidSahm2010[httpsbooksgooglecombooksid1gry61absiECpgPA79_79]-48) In March, he performed on the final day of the _Dripping Springs Reunion_, a three-day country music festival aimed by its producers to be an annual event. Despite the failure to reach the expected attendance, the concept of the festival inspired Nelson to create the _[Fourth of July Picnic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie\_Nelson%27s\_Fourth\_of\_July\_Picnic "Willie Nelson's Fourth of July Picnic")_, his own annual event, starting the following year.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEThomas2012-49)

Nelson decided to return to the recording business; he signed Neil Reshen as his manager to negotiate with RCA, who got the label to agree to end his contract upon repayment of $14,000.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEReid2004[httpsbooksgooglecombooksidqCDF5fFuBT8CpgPA223_223]-46) Reshen eventually signed Nelson to [Atlantic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Records "Atlantic Records") for $25,000 per year, where he became the label's first country artist.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEReid2004[httpsbooksgooglecombooksid224pgPA224-50) He formed his backing band, [the Family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_(Willie_Nelson%27s_band) "Family (Willie Nelson's band)"),[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMilner1998[httpsbooksgooglecombooksidzeslYkOZIvUCpgPA183_183],_[httpsbooksgooglecombooksid184pgPA184_184]-51) and, by February 1973, he was recording his acclaimed _[Shotgun Willie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shotgun\_Willie "Shotgun Willie")_ at Atlantic Studios in New York City.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHardenHoekstraMcCallMorris1996169-52)

![Image 9](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cb/Gnome-mime-audio-openclipart.svg/60px-Gnome-mime-audio-openclipart.svg.png)

Introduction of the song "Shotgun Willie", opening track of the album _[Shotgun Willie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shotgun\_Willie "Shotgun Willie")_, that marked a change of style from Nelson's earlier recordings.

_Shotgun Willie_, released in May 1973, earned excellent reviews but did not sell well. The album led Nelson to a new style, later stating that _Shotgun Willie_ had "cleared his throat".[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTETichi1998341-53) His next release, _[Phases and Stages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phases\_and\_Stages "Phases and Stages")_, released in 1974, was a concept album about a couple's divorce, inspired by his own experience. Side one of the record is from the viewpoint of the woman, and side two is from the viewpoint of the man.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEErlewine2007-54) The album included the hit single "[Bloody Mary Morning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloody_Mary_Morning "Bloody Mary Morning")".[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDicair2007[httpsbooksgooglecombooksidMYMQl9dsKJECpgPA247_247]-55) The same year, he produced and starred in the pilot episode of [PBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PBS "PBS")' _[Austin City Limits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin\_City\_Limits "Austin City Limits")_.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTERichmond200075-56)

Nelson then moved to [Columbia Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Records "Columbia Records"), where he signed a contract that gave him complete creative control, made possible by the critical and commercial success of his previous albums.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDicair2007[httpsbooksgooglecombooksid247pgPA247_247]-57) The result was the critically acclaimed and massively popular 1975 concept album _[Red Headed Stranger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red\_Headed\_Stranger "Red Headed Stranger")_. Although Columbia was reluctant to release an album with primarily a guitar and piano for accompaniment, Nelson and Waylon Jennings insisted. The album included a cover of [Fred Rose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_Rose_(songwriter) "Fred Rose (songwriter)")'s 1945 song "[Blue Eyes Crying in the Rain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Eyes_Crying_in_the_Rain "Blue Eyes Crying in the Rain")", that had been released as a single previous to the album, and became Nelson's first number one hit as a singer.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWolffDuane2000[httpsbooksgooglecombooksid3Jorozp1yp4CpgPA367_367]-58) Throughout his 1975 tour, Nelson raised funds for PBS-affiliated stations across the south promoting _Austin City Limits_. The pilot was aired first on those stations, later being released nationwide. The positive reception of the show prompted PBS to order ten episodes for 1976, formally launching the show.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTERichmond200076-59)

[![Image 10: Three men. From left to right, the first man has brown hair and beard. He wears a blue T-shirt and a white jacket and is looking at the man in the middle. The man in the middle wears a green cap and shades, and long red hair. He wears a brown T-shirt. The man at the right has brown hair, he looks at the man at the middle. He wears a white shirt and a black letter jacket.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/29/Kris_Willie_Waylon.jpg/250px-Kris_Willie_Waylon.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kris_Willie_Waylon.jpg)

L–R: [Kris Kristofferson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson "Kris Kristofferson"), Nelson, and [Waylon Jennings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waylon_Jennings "Waylon Jennings") at the 1972 _[Dripping Springs Reunion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dripping\_Springs\_Reunion "Dripping Springs Reunion")_

As Jennings was also achieving success in country music in the early 1970s, the pair were combined into a genre called [outlaw country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outlaw_country "Outlaw country"), since it did not conform to Nashville standards.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHartman2008[httpsbooksgooglecombooksid174pgPA174_174]-60) The album _[Wanted! The Outlaws](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wanted!\_The\_Outlaws "Wanted! The Outlaws")_ in 1976 with [Jessi Colter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessi_Colter "Jessi Colter") and [Tompall Glaser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tompall_Glaser "Tompall Glaser") cemented the pair's outlaw image and became country music's first [platinum album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_recording_certification "Music recording certification").[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHartman2008[httpsbooksgooglecombooksid175pgPA175_175]-61) Later that year Nelson released _[The Sound in Your Mind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sound\_in\_Your\_Mind "The Sound in Your Mind")_ (certified gold in 1978 and platinum in 2001)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTERIAA_staff2010-62) and his first gospel album _[Troublemaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Troublemaker\_(album) "The Troublemaker (album)")_[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEErlewine2008-63) (certified gold in 1986).[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTERIAA_staff_22010-64)

In the summer of 1977, Nelson discovered that Reshen had been filing tax extensions and not paying the [Internal Revenue Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internal_Revenue_Service "Internal Revenue Service") (IRS) since he took over as his manager.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTENelsonRitz2015263-65) In June, a package containing cocaine was sent from Reshen's office in New York to Jennings in Nashville.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTENelsonRitz2015262-66) The package was followed by the [DEA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drug_Enforcement_Administration "Drug Enforcement Administration"), and Jennings was arrested. The charges were later dropped, since Reshen's assistant, Mark Rothbaum, stepped in and took the charges. Rothbaum was sentenced to serve time in jail. Impressed by his attitude, Nelson fired Reshen and hired Rothbaum as his manager.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTENelsonRitz2015263-65) In 1978, Nelson released two more platinum albums. One, _[Waylon & Willie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waylon\_%26\_Willie "Waylon & Willie")_, was a collaboration with Jennings that included "[Mammas Don't Let Your Babies Grow Up to Be Cowboys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammas_Don%27t_Let_Your_Babies_Grow_Up_to_Be_Cowboys "Mammas Don't Let Your Babies Grow Up to Be Cowboys")", a hit single written and performed by [Ed Bruce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Bruce "Ed Bruce").[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJenningsKaye199610-67) Though observers predicted that _[Stardust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stardust\_(Willie\_Nelson\_album) "Stardust (Willie Nelson album)")_ would ruin his career, it went platinum the same year.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTERIAA_staff_32010-68) Nelson continued to top the charts with hit songs during the late 1970s, including "[Good Hearted Woman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_Hearted_Woman_(song) "Good Hearted Woman (song)")", "Remember Me",[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBillboard1976-69) "[If You've Got the Money I've Got the Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_You%27ve_Got_the_Money_I%27ve_Got_the_Time "If You've Got the Money I've Got the Time")", and "[Uncloudy Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncloudy_Day "Uncloudy Day")".[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTETribe2006188-70)

![Image 11](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cb/Gnome-mime-audio-openclipart.svg/60px-Gnome-mime-audio-openclipart.svg.png)

From the album _Honeysuckle Rose_, "On the Road Again" peaked at number one on the [Hot Country Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Country_Songs "Hot Country Songs") chart in 1980.

During the 1980s, Nelson recorded a series of hit singles including "[Midnight Rider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midnight_Rider "Midnight Rider")", a 1980 cover of the [Allman Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allman_Brothers "Allman Brothers") song which Nelson recorded for _[The Electric Horseman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Electric\_Horseman "The Electric Horseman")_,[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHarrison,_Thomas201196-71) the soundtrack "[On the Road Again](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On_the_Road_Again_(Willie_Nelson_song) "On the Road Again (Willie Nelson song)")" from the movie _[Honeysuckle Rose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeysuckle\_Rose\_(film) "Honeysuckle Rose (film)")_, and a duet with [Julio Iglesias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julio_Iglesias "Julio Iglesias") titled "[To All the Girls I've Loved Before](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/To_All_the_Girls_I%27ve_Loved_Before "To All the Girls I've Loved Before")".[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJurek2008-72)

[![Image 12](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1d/President_Jimmy_Carter_with_Willie_Nelson_and_his_guests.jpg/250px-President_Jimmy_Carter_with_Willie_Nelson_and_his_guests.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:President_Jimmy_Carter_with_Willie_Nelson_and_his_guests.jpg)

Nelson and guests with President [Jimmy Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Carter "Jimmy Carter") in 1978

In 1982, _[Pancho & Lefty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pancho\_%26\_Lefty\_(album) "Pancho & Lefty (album)")_, a duet album with [Merle Haggard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merle_Haggard "Merle Haggard") produced by [Chips Moman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chips_Moman "Chips Moman"), was released.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMonkman2008-73) During the recording sessions of _Pancho & Lefty_, Johnny Christopher, a session guitarist and the co-writer of "[Always on My Mind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Always_on_My_Mind "Always on My Mind")", tried to pitch the song to an uninterested Haggard. Nelson, who was unaware of [Elvis Presley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elvis_Presley "Elvis Presley")'s version of the song, asked him to record it. Produced by Moman, the single of the song was released, as well as the album [_Always on My Mind_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Always_on_My_Mind_(Willie_Nelson_album) "Always on My Mind (Willie Nelson album)"). The single topped _Billboard_'s Hot Country Singles, while it reached number five on the _Billboard_ Hot 100. The release won three awards during the [25th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/25th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "25th Annual Grammy Awards"): [Song of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Song_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Song of the Year"), [Best Country Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Country_Song "Grammy Award for Best Country Song") and [Best Male Country Vocal Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Male_Country_Vocal_Performance "Grammy Award for Best Male Country Vocal Performance"). The single was certified platinum, while the album was certified quadruple-platinum and later inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame in 2008.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPoe2012147-74)

Meanwhile, two collaborations with Waylon Jennings were released: _[WWII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWII\_(album) "WWII (album)")_ in 1982,[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEErlewine2005-75) and _[Take it to the Limit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Take\_It\_to\_the\_Limit\_(Willie\_Nelson\_album) "Take It to the Limit (Willie Nelson album)")_ in 1983. In the mid-1980s, Nelson, Jennings, Kristofferson, and [Johnny Cash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Cash "Johnny Cash") formed [The Highwaymen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Highwaymen_(country_supergroup) "The Highwaymen (country supergroup)"), a supergroup who achieved platinum record sales and toured the world.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPatoski2008383-76) Meanwhile, Nelson became more involved with charity work, such as singing on "[We Are the World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Are_the_World "We Are the World")" in 1984.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEdwards2015-77) In 1985, Nelson had another success with _[Half Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half\_Nelson\_(Willie\_Nelson\_album) "Half Nelson (Willie Nelson album)")_, a compilation album of duets with a range of artists such as [Ray Charles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Charles "Ray Charles") and [Neil Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Young "Neil Young").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPatoski2008368-78) In 1980, Nelson performed on the south lawn of the [White House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House "White House"). The concert of September 13 featured First Lady [Rosalynn Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosalynn_Carter "Rosalynn Carter") and Nelson in a duet of [Ray Wylie Hubbard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Wylie_Hubbard "Ray Wylie Hubbard")'s "Up Against the Wall Redneck Mother". Nelson frequently visited the White House, where, according to the biography by Joe Nick Patoski, _Willie Nelson: An Epic Life_, he smoked marijuana on the White House roof.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPatoski2008342-79)

### Later career (1990s–2000s)

In 1996, Nelson re-recorded the tracks "[Hello Walls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hello_Walls "Hello Walls")" with the band [the Reverend Horton Heat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reverend_Horton_Heat "The Reverend Horton Heat"), and "[Bloody Mary Morning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloody_Mary_Morning "Bloody Mary Morning")" with the [Supersuckers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supersuckers "Supersuckers"), for _Twisted Willie_, a tribute album featuring rock versions of Nelson's songs performed by artists such as [Johnny Cash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Cash "Johnny Cash"), [Kris Kristofferson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson "Kris Kristofferson"), [Jerry Cantrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Cantrell "Jerry Cantrell"), [Mark Lanegan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Lanegan "Mark Lanegan"), [L7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L7_(band) "L7 (band)"), [the Presidents of the United States of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Presidents_of_the_United_States_of_America_(band) "The Presidents of the United States of America (band)"), and [Jello Biafra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jello_Biafra "Jello Biafra"), among others.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHochman1996-80) Proceeds from the sale of the record went to Nelson's Farm Aid.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-81)

[![Image 13](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4b/President_Clinton_greets_Willie_Nelson_-_DPLA_-_1537c83498c3b09d10fcf1931b9e30df.jpg/250px-President_Clinton_greets_Willie_Nelson_-_DPLA_-_1537c83498c3b09d10fcf1931b9e30df.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:President_Clinton_greets_Willie_Nelson_-_DPLA_-_1537c83498c3b09d10fcf1931b9e30df.jpg)

Nelson with President [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton") in 1993

During the 1990s and 2000s, Nelson toured continuously, recording several albums including 1998's critically acclaimed _[Teatro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teatro\_(Willie\_Nelson\_album) "Teatro (Willie Nelson album)")_,[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPatoski2008430-82) and performed and recorded with other acts including [Phish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phish "Phish"),[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFarm_Aid_Staff2011-83) Johnny Cash,[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEErlewine2000-84) and [Toby Keith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toby_Keith "Toby Keith"). His duet with Keith, "[Beer for My Horses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beer_for_My_Horses "Beer for My Horses")", was released as a single and topped the _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard\_magazine "Billboard magazine")_ Hot Country Songs charts for six consecutive weeks in 2003,[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBMI_staff2003-85) while the accompanying video won an award for "Best Video" at the 2004 [Academy of Country Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Country_Music "Academy of Country Music") Awards.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBiography_staff2011-86) A [USA Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA_Network "USA Network") television special celebrated Nelson's 70th birthday,[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPareles2003-87) and Nelson released _[The Essential Willie Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Essential\_Willie\_Nelson "The Essential Willie Nelson")_ as part of the celebration. Nelson also appeared on [Ringo Starr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ringo_Starr "Ringo Starr")'s 2003 album, _[Ringo Rama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ringo\_Rama "Ringo Rama")_, as a guest vocal on "Write One for Me".[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEntertainment_One_staff2003-88)

Nelson was featured on the album [_True Love_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/True_Love_(Toots_%26_the_Maytals_album) "True Love (Toots & the Maytals album)") by [Toots and the Maytals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toots_and_the_Maytals "Toots and the Maytals"), which won the [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award") in 2004 for Best Reggae Album, and showcased many notable musicians including [Eric Clapton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Clapton "Eric Clapton"), [Jeff Beck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Beck "Jeff Beck"), [Trey Anastasio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trey_Anastasio "Trey Anastasio"), [Gwen Stefani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani "Gwen Stefani"), and [Keith Richards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Richards "Keith Richards").[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEToots_and_the_Maytals2016-89) In the following year of 2005, Nelson released a [reggae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggae "Reggae") album entitled _[Countryman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Countryman\_(album) "Countryman (album)")_ which featured [Toots Hibbert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toots_Hibbert "Toots Hibbert") of [Toots and the Maytals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toots_and_the_Maytals "Toots and the Maytals") on the song "I'm a Worried Man".[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDeusner2005-90)

Nelson headlined the 2005 Tsunami Relief Austin to Asia concert to benefit the victims of the [2004 Indian Ocean earthquake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Indian_Ocean_earthquake "2004 Indian Ocean earthquake"), which raised an estimated $75,000 for UNICEF.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBBC_News_staff2005-91) Also in 2005, a live performance of the Johnny Cash song "[Busted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Busted_(Johnny_Cash_song) "Busted (Johnny Cash song)")" with Ray Charles was released on Charles' duets album _[Genius & Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genius\_%26\_Friends "Genius & Friends")_. Nelson's 2007 performance with jazz trumpeter [Wynton Marsalis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wynton_Marsalis "Wynton Marsalis") at the [Lincoln Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln_Center "Lincoln Center"), was released as the live album _[Two Men with the Blues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two\_Men\_with\_the\_Blues "Two Men with the Blues")_ in 2008; reaching number one in _Billboard_'s Top Jazz Albums and number twenty on the _Billboard_ 200.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTENelsonRitz2015360-92) The same year, Nelson recorded his first album with [Buddy Cannon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddy_Cannon "Buddy Cannon") as the producer, _[Moment of Forever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moment\_of\_Forever "Moment of Forever")_. Cannon acquainted Nelson earlier, during the production of his collaboration with [Kenny Chesney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Chesney "Kenny Chesney") on the duet "[That Lucky Old Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/That_Lucky_Old_Sun "That Lucky Old Sun")", for Chesney's album _[Lucky Old Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucky\_Old\_Sun "Lucky Old Sun")_.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTECooper2014-93) In 2009 Nelson and Marsalis joined with Norah Jones in a tribute concert to Ray Charles, which resulted in the _[Here We Go Again: Celebrating the Genius of Ray Charles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Here\_We\_Go\_Again:\_Celebrating\_the\_Genius\_of\_Ray\_Charles "Here We Go Again: Celebrating the Genius of Ray Charles")_ album, released in 2011.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWillie_Nelson.com_staff2011-94)

### 2010s

In 2010, Nelson released _[Country Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country\_Music\_(Willie\_Nelson\_album) "Country Music (Willie Nelson album)")_, a compilation of standards produced by [T-Bone Burnett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T-Bone_Burnett "T-Bone Burnett").[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEvans-Price2010-95) The album peaked at number four in _Billboard_'s Top Country Albums, and twenty on the _Billboard_ 200.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEErlewine2010-96) It was nominated for Best Americana Album at the [2011 Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/53rd_Annual_Grammy_Awards "53rd Annual Grammy Awards").[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTECBS_Music_staff2011-97) In 2011 Nelson participated in the concert _Kokua For Japan_, a fund raising event for the victims of the [2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_T%C5%8Dhoku_earthquake_and_tsunami "2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami") in Japan which raised $1.6 million.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTESugimoto2011-98)

In February 2012, [Legacy Recordings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legacy_Recordings "Legacy Recordings") signed a deal with Nelson that included the release of new material, as well as past releases that would be selected and complemented with outtakes and other material selected by him.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWillie_Nelson.com_staff2012-99) With the new deal, Buddy Cannon returned to produce the recordings of Nelson. After selecting the material and the sound of the tunes with the singer, Cannon's work method consisted in the recording of the tracks with studio musicians, with the takes later completed on a separate session by Nelson with his guitar. Cannon's association to Nelson also extended to songwriting, with singer and producer composing the lyrics by exchanging text messages.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTECooper2014-93)

Nelson's first release for the Legacy Recordings was _[Heroes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heroes\_(Willie\_Nelson\_album) "Heroes (Willie Nelson album)")_, that included guest appearances by his sons [Lukas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lukas_Nelson_%26_Promise_of_the_Real "Lukas Nelson & Promise of the Real") and Micah of the band [Insects vs Robots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insects_vs_Robots "Insects vs Robots"), Ray Price, Merle Haggard, [Snoop Dogg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snoop_Dogg "Snoop Dogg"), Kris Kristofferson, [Jamey Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamey_Johnson "Jamey Johnson"), [Billy Joe Shaver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Joe_Shaver "Billy Joe Shaver") and [Sheryl Crow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheryl_Crow "Sheryl Crow"). The album reached number four on _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard\_(magazine) "Billboard (magazine)")_'s [Top Country Albums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_charts "Billboard charts").[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBillboard_staff2012-100) His 2013 release _[To All the Girls...](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/To\_All\_the\_Girls... "To All the Girls...")_, a collection of duets with all female partners, featured among others [Dolly Parton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolly_Parton "Dolly Parton"), [Loretta Lynn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loretta_Lynn "Loretta Lynn"), [Rosanne Cash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosanne_Cash "Rosanne Cash"), Sheryl Crow, [Mavis Staples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mavis_Staples "Mavis Staples"), Norah Jones, [Emmylou Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmylou_Harris "Emmylou Harris"), [Carrie Underwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrie_Underwood "Carrie Underwood") and [Miranda Lambert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert "Miranda Lambert").[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEVinson2013-101) The album entered _Billboard_'s Top Country Albums at number two, marking his highest position on the chart since the release of his 1989 _A Horse Called Music_, and extending his record to a total of forty-six top ten albums on the country charts. Nelson scored as well his second top ten album on the [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200"), with the release entering at number nine.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJessen2013-102)

[![Image 14](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/09/Willie_Nelson%2C_Fort_Wayne%2C_Indiana_%28June_27%2C_2018%29_-_Pamela_Smith_06.jpg/250px-Willie_Nelson%2C_Fort_Wayne%2C_Indiana_%28June_27%2C_2018%29_-_Pamela_Smith_06.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Willie_Nelson,_Fort_Wayne,_Indiana_(June_27,_2018)_-_Pamela_Smith_06.jpg)

Nelson performing in Fort Wayne, Indiana, in 2018

Nelson's following release was _[Band of Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Band\_of\_Brothers\_(Willie\_Nelson\_album) "Band of Brothers (Willie Nelson album)")_, in 2014, the first Nelson album to feature the most newly self-penned songs since 1996's _[Spirit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spirit\_(Willie\_Nelson\_album) "Spirit (Willie Nelson album)")_. Upon its release, it topped _Billboard_'s Top Country albums chart, the first time since 1986's _[The Promiseland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Promiseland "The Promiseland")_, the last Nelson album to top it. The release reached number five on the _Billboard_ 200, Nelson's highest position on the chart since 1982's _Always on My Mind_.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTELeahey2014-103) In December 2014, a duet with [Rhonda Vincent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhonda_Vincent "Rhonda Vincent"), "Only Me", topped _[Bluegrass Unlimited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bluegrass\_Unlimited "Bluegrass Unlimited")'s_ National Airplay chart.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHolden2014-104) In June 2015, his collaboration with Haggard _[Django and Jimmie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Django\_and\_Jimmie "Django and Jimmie")_ topped _Billboard_'s Top Country albums chart and reached number seven on the _Billboard_ 200.

In 2017, Nelson released _[God's Problem Child](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God%27s\_Problem\_Child "God's Problem Child")_. The release, consisting mostly of Nelson originals co-written with Cannon, entered the Top country albums at number one, while it reached number ten on the _Billboard_ 200.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAsker2017-105)

In 2018, Nelson sang a song written by [Daniel Lanois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Lanois "Daniel Lanois") called "Cruel World" for the [soundtrack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_of_Red_Dead_Redemption_2 "Music of Red Dead Redemption 2") of [Rockstar Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockstar_Games "Rockstar Games")'s action-adventure video game _[Red Dead Redemption 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red\_Dead\_Redemption\_2 "Red Dead Redemption 2")_.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDaly2018-106) Lanois wrote the song especially for Nelson. When a hurricane prevented Nelson from recording the song, the production team sent the track to [Josh Homme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Homme "Josh Homme") in the hopes that he could record it in time for the game's release. Nelson was ultimately able to record the song in time in Los Angeles;[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShanley2019-107) the team considered combining the two versions into a duet, but ultimately included both versions in the game.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTELanois2019-108) Also in 2018, Nelson was one of several artists on _[Restoration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revamp\_%26\_Restoration "Revamp & Restoration")_, a cover album containing various country renditions of songs originally by [Elton John](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John "Elton John"), on which he performed "[Border Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Border_Song "Border Song")".[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrickey2018-109) His 2019 release _[Ride Me Back Home](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ride\_Me\_Back\_Home "Ride Me Back Home")_ charted at number two on the _Billboard_ Top Country Albums chart.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAsker2019-110) For the title-track, Nelson received the [Grammy Award for Best Country Solo Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Country_Solo_Performance "Grammy Award for Best Country Solo Performance").[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKroll2020-111)

### 2020s

Following the [U.S. coronavirus pandemic lockdowns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_coronavirus_pandemic_in_the_United_States#Lockdowns "2020 coronavirus pandemic in the United States") that began in March 2020, Nelson [livestreamed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Livestreaming "Livestreaming") a series of [benefit concerts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benefit_concert "Benefit concert"). The first two raised $700,000 for people who had suffered financial loss due to effects on the U.S. economy.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMargolis2020-112) The third, which was held on April 20, 2020, was a variety show titled _[Come and Toke It](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come\_and\_Toke\_It "Come and Toke It")_.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFrance2020-113) Some of the content was [cannabis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cannabis_(drug) "Cannabis (drug)")-themed, and some of the proceeds will be used to support The Last Prisoner Project, a [restorative justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Restorative_justice "Restorative justice") program relating to persons convicted of cannabis-related crimes.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTERosenthal2020-114)[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWillman2020-115)[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKreps2020-116) The same year, Nelson was approached by [Karen O](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karen_O "Karen O") of [The Yeah Yeah Yeahs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Yeah_Yeah_Yeahs "The Yeah Yeah Yeahs") to collaborate. They chose to perform [David Bowie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Bowie "David Bowie") and [Queen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_(band) "Queen (band)")'s "[Under Pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Under_Pressure "Under Pressure")."[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-117)

For his releases of _[The Willie Nelson Family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Willie\_Nelson\_Family "The Willie Nelson Family")_ (2021) and _[A Beautiful Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Beautiful\_Time "A Beautiful Time")_ (2022), Nelson received four nominations for the [65th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/65th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "65th Annual Grammy Awards"), winning in two categories: Best Country Solo Performance and Best Country Album.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTECummings,_Tommy2022-118)[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFarias,_Robbie2023-119) In December 2022, Mark Rothbaum announced a five-part documentary entitled _Willie Nelson and Family_; it was released at the 2023 [Sundance Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sundance_Film_Festival "Sundance Film Festival").[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTECummings,_Tommy2022-118) In 2023, Nelson performed at two concerts at the [Hollywood Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Bowl "Hollywood Bowl") celebrating his 90th birthday[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-120) and was inducted into the [Rock and Roll Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame "Rock and Roll Hall of Fame").[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTERockHall2023-121)

In 2024, Nelson was featured in the "Smoke Hour ★ Willie Nelson" and "Smoke Hour II" interludes of [Beyoncé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyonc%C3%A9 "Beyoncé")'s _[Cowboy Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy\_Carter "Cowboy Carter")_ album, the second album in her [trilogy project](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyonc%C3%A9_discography "Beyoncé discography").[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-122) With the death of [Kris Kristofferson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson "Kris Kristofferson") in September 2024, Nelson became the last surviving member of [The Highwaymen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Highwaymen_(country_supergroup) "The Highwaymen (country supergroup)").

## Other ventures

Nelson's acting debut was in the 1979 film _The Electric Horseman_, followed by appearances in _[Honeysuckle Rose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeysuckle\_Rose\_(film) "Honeysuckle Rose (film)")_, _[Thief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thief\_(film) "Thief (film)")_, and _[Barbarosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbarosa "Barbarosa")_. He played the role of Red Loon in _[Coming Out of the Ice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coming\_Out\_of\_the\_Ice "Coming Out of the Ice")_ in 1982 and starred in _Songwriter_ two years later. He portrayed the lead role in the 1986 film version of his album _Red Headed Stranger_.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAllmovie_staff2011-123) Other movies that Nelson acted in include _[Wag the Dog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wag\_the\_Dog "Wag the Dog")_, _[Gone Fishin'](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gone\_Fishin%27\_(film) "Gone Fishin' (film)")_ (as Billy 'Catch' Pooler), the 1986 television movie _[Stagecoach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stagecoach\_(TV\_film) "Stagecoach (TV film)")_ (with Johnny Cash, Waylon Jennings, and Kris Kristofferson), _[Half Baked](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half\_Baked "Half Baked")_, _[Beerfest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beerfest "Beerfest")_, _[The Dukes of Hazzard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Dukes\_of\_Hazzard\_(film) "The Dukes of Hazzard (film)")_, _[Surfer, Dude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surfer,\_Dude "Surfer, Dude")_ and _[Swing Vote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swing\_Vote\_(2008\_film) "Swing Vote (2008 film)")_. He has also made guest appearances on _[Miami Vice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami\_Vice "Miami Vice")_ (1986's "El Viejo" episode); _[Delta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delta\_(American\_TV\_series) "Delta (American TV series)")_; _[Nash Bridges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nash\_Bridges "Nash Bridges")_; _[The Simpsons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Simpsons "The Simpsons")_; _[Monk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monk\_(TV\_series) "Monk (TV series)")_; _[Adventures in Wonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adventures\_in\_Wonderland\_(1992\_TV\_series) "Adventures in Wonderland (1992 TV series)")_; _[Dr. Quinn, Medicine Woman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr.\_Quinn,\_Medicine\_Woman "Dr. Quinn, Medicine Woman")_; _[King of the Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King\_of\_the\_Hill\_(TV\_series) "King of the Hill (TV series)")_; _[The Colbert Report](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Colbert\_Report "The Colbert Report")_; _[Swing Vote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swing\_Vote "Swing Vote")_; and _[Space Ghost Coast to Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space\_Ghost\_Coast\_to\_Coast "Space Ghost Coast to Coast")_.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEYahoo!_Movies_staff2011-124)

[![Image 15: A store with a sign that reads "Willie's Place". The apostrophe is replaced in the sign by a bullet hole. The structure of the store is constructed in wooden with three columns. There are four windows and there are a red and a grey car in the parking lot.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/82/Willie%27s_Place_near_Hillsboro%2C_TX_IMG_4050.JPG/250px-Willie%27s_Place_near_Hillsboro%2C_TX_IMG_4050.JPG)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Willie%27s_Place_near_Hillsboro,_TX_IMG_4050.JPG)

In 2008, Nelson reopened the truck stop [Willie's Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie%27s_Place "Willie's Place") near [Hillsboro, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillsboro,_Texas "Hillsboro, Texas")

In 1988 his first book, _[Willie: An Autobiography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie:\_An\_Autobiography "Willie: An Autobiography")_, was published.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTENelsonShrakeShrake2000-125)_[The Facts of Life: And Other Dirty Jokes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Facts\_of\_Life:\_And\_Other\_Dirty\_Jokes "The Facts of Life: And Other Dirty Jokes")_, a personal recollection of tour and musical stories from his career, combined with song lyrics, followed in 2002. In 2005 he co-authored _Farm Aid: A Song for America_, a commemorative book about the twentieth anniversary of the foundation of Farm Aid.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGeorge-WarrenHoekstra2005-126) His third book, co-authored with long-time friend [Turk Pipkin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turk_Pipkin "Turk Pipkin"), _The Tao of Willie: A Guide to the Happiness in Your Heart_, was published in 2006.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTENPR_staff2010-127) In 2007 a book advocating the use of bio-diesel and the reduction of gas emissions, _On the Clean Road Again: Biodiesel and the Future of the Family Farm_, was published.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTENelson2007a29-4) His next book, _A Tale Out of Luck_, published in 2008 and co-authored by Mike Blakely, was Nelson's first fictional book.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTENelson2008-128) In 2012, a new autobiography by Nelson, _[Roll Me Up and Smoke Me When I Die: Musings from the Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roll\_Me\_Up\_and\_Smoke\_Me\_When\_I\_Die:\_Musings\_from\_the\_Road "Roll Me Up and Smoke Me When I Die: Musings from the Road")_, was announced. Released on November 13, it was named after the song from his album _Heroes_. The book contained further biographical details, as well as family pictures and stories about Nelson's political views, as well as his marijuana advocacy. The artwork of the book was designed by Nelson's son, Micah, and the foreword written by Kinky Friedman.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWhitaker2012-129) A second Nelson autobiography, _[It's a Long Story: My Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It%27s\_a\_Long\_Story:\_My\_Life "It's a Long Story: My Life")_ co-authored with [David Ritz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Ritz "David Ritz"), was published on May 5, 2015.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHachette_staff2015-130)_[Pretty Paper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pretty\_Paper\_(book) "Pretty Paper (book)")_, another collaboration with Ritz, was published the following year.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTENelsonRitz2016-131)

In 2002, Nelson became the official spokesman of the [Texas Roadhouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Roadhouse "Texas Roadhouse"), a chain of steakhouses. Nelson heavily promoted the chain and appeared on a special on [Food Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_Network "Food Network"). The chain installed _Willie's Corner_, a section dedicated to him and decked out with Willie memorabilia, at several locations.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTECarey2003-132) In 2004, Nelson and his wife Annie became partners with Bob and Kelly King in the building of two Pacific bio-diesel plants, one in [Salem, Oregon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salem,_Oregon "Salem, Oregon"), and the other at Carl's Corner, Texas (the Texas plant was founded by Carl Cornelius, a longtime Nelson friend and the eponym for Carl's Corner). In 2005, Nelson and several other business partners formed [Willie Nelson Biodiesel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson_Biodiesel "Willie Nelson Biodiesel") ("Bio-Willie"), a company that markets biodiesel bio-fuel to truck stops.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTESmithTaylor2008173-133) The fuel is made from vegetable oil (mainly soybean oil) and can be burned without modification in [diesel engines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diesel_engine "Diesel engine").[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAssociated_Press_staff2005-134) Nelson registered his company with Earth Biofuels and he became a board member. In 2007, Nelson forfeited six million shares of the company as he left the board.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrick,_Michael2014-135) By 2008, he reopened [Willie's Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie%27s_Place "Willie's Place"), a truck stop in [Carl's Corner, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl%27s_Corner,_Texas "Carl's Corner, Texas"). The [U.S. Bankruptcy Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Bankruptcy_Court "U.S. Bankruptcy Court") allowed Nelson to invest in it. The establishment had about 80 employees,[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDunn2011-136) and was used as a concert hall with a bar and a 1,000 square feet (93 m 2) dance floor.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWillie's_Place_staff2010-137) Willie's Place also featured BioWillie pumps. At the time, the government of the United States offered a one dollar tax credit to producers of biodiesel. As the competition grew, the tax credit was discontinued while the prices of fossil fuels continued to drop. Nelson and his partners defaulted the $4.75 million loan they took for the construction of Willie's Place. Nelson then paid $35,000 back, while a judge later rejected the request of his creditors to receive more money from him. [TravelCenters of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TravelCenters_of_America "TravelCenters of America") bought Willie's Place during its foreclosure in 2011. The BioWillie plant was then put on the market for sale. Nelson kept the trademark for BioWillie, which is sold on the islands of Maui and Hawaii. Meanwhile, Nelson owns shares of Big Island Biodiesel in Hawaii and SeQuential-Pacific Biodiesel in Oregon.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrick,_Michael2014-135)

In 2010, Nelson founded, with the collaboration of producers and filmmakers [Luck Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luck_Films "Luck Films"), a company dedicated to producing feature films, documentaries, and concerts.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChagollan2010-138) The next year, he created the [Willie's Roadhouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie%27s_Roadhouse "Willie's Roadhouse") show which aired on channel 56 of [SiriusXM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SiriusXM "SiriusXM") radio. The channel was a result of the merger of his two other channels _The Roadhouse_ and _Willie's Place_.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEOpry.com_staff2011-139) In November 2014, it was announced that Nelson would be the host of the television series _Inside Arlyn_, shot at Arlyn Studio in Austin, Texas. The thirteen-episode first season would feature artists being interviewed by Nelson and [Dan Rather](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Rather "Dan Rather"), followed by a performance. The series concept received attention from cable channels that requested to see the pilot episode.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTESwiatecki2014-140) Following the legalization of marijuana in different states, Nelson announced in 2015 through spokesman Michael Bowman the establishment of his own marijuana brand, [Willie's Reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie%27s_Reserve "Willie's Reserve"). Plans to open chain stores in the states where marijuana was legalized were announced, to be expanded state-to-state if marijuana legalization further expanded. Bowman called the brand "a culmination of (Nelson's) vision, and his whole life".[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGuardian_Music_staff2015-141)

In 2017, Nelson appeared as himself in [Woody Harrelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woody_Harrelson "Woody Harrelson")'s live film, _[Lost in London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lost\_in\_London "Lost in London")_.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTELodderhose2016-142) In June 2017, he appeared alongside Merle Haggard in the documentary _[The American Epic Sessions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_American\_Epic\_Sessions "The American Epic Sessions")_ directed by [Bernard MacMahon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_MacMahon_(filmmaker) "Bernard MacMahon (filmmaker)"). They performed a song Haggard had composed for the film, "The Only Man Wilder Than Me",[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTESolomon2017-143)[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHautzinger2017-144) and [Bob Wills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Wills "Bob Wills")'s classic "Old Fashioned Love",[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHautzinger2017-144) which they recorded live direct to disc on the first [electrical sound recording](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_sound_recording#The_electrical_era_(1925_to_1945)_(including_sound_on_film) "History of sound recording") system from the 1920s.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTELocke2017-145) It was the last filmed performance of the pair. _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ commented that "in the final performance of Sessions, Willie Nelson and Merle Haggard perform the duet 'The Only Man Wilder Than Me.' Haggard has a look of complete joy on his face throughout the session in the old-timey recording setup once used by his musical heroes."[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAppleford2017-146)

## Musical style

Nelson uses a variety of music styles to create his own distinctive blend of country music, a hybrid of jazz, pop, blues, rock and folk.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEErlewine2015-147) His style incorporates a "relaxed, behind-the-beat singing style and gut-string guitar."[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEncyclop%C3%A6dia_Britannica_staff2011-148) His "nasal voice and jazzy, off-center phrasing"[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEErlewine2015-147) has been responsible for his wide appeal, and has made him a "vital icon in country music", influencing the "[new country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music"), [new traditionalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neotraditional_country "Neotraditional country"), and [alternative country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternative_country "Alternative country") movements of the 1980s and 1990s".[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEErlewine2015-147)

### Guitars

[![Image 16: A classical guitar. There are several damages in the soundboard, near the sound hole there is a big hole and the wood is worn out in the surrounding areas of it. The guitar has several signatures on it. there is a blue and white strap in the soundhole.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e0/Trigger-Willie_Nelson.jpg/250px-Trigger-Willie_Nelson.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Trigger-Willie_Nelson.jpg)

Nelson's guitar, Trigger, has been signed by several of Nelson's friends

In 1969, the Baldwin company gave Nelson an amplifier and guitar with their "Prismatone" [pickup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pickup_(music_technology) "Pickup (music technology)"). During a show in [Helotes, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helotes,_Texas "Helotes, Texas"), Nelson left the guitar on the floor of the stage, and it was later stepped on by a drunk man.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTENelson2005-149) He sent it to be repaired in Nashville by [Shot Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shot_Jackson "Shot Jackson"), who told Nelson that the damage was too great. Jackson offered him a [Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._F._Martin_%26_Company "C. F. Martin & Company") N-20 [classical guitar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classical_guitar "Classical guitar"), and, at Nelson's request, moved the pickup to the Martin. Nelson purchased the guitar unseen for $750 and named it after [Roy Rogers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Rogers "Roy Rogers")' horse ["Trigger"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trigger_(horse) "Trigger (horse)").[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWillie_Nelson_General_Store_staff2010-150) The next year Nelson rescued the guitar from his burning ranch.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEReinert1976103-151)[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDraper1991103-152)

Constant strumming with a [guitar pick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guitar_pick "Guitar pick") over the decades has worn a large sweeping hole into the guitar's body near the sound hole—the N-20 has no [pickguard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pickguard "Pickguard") since classical guitars are meant to be played fingerstyle instead of with picks.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTENPR_staff1996-37) Its soundboard has been signed by over a hundred of Nelson's friends and associates, ranging from fellow musicians to lawyers and football coaches.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWillie_Nelson_General_Store_staff2010-150) The first signature on the guitar was [Leon Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leon_Russell "Leon Russell")'s, who asked Nelson initially to sign his guitar. When Nelson was about to sign it with a marker, Russell requested him to scratch it instead, explaining that the guitar would be more valuable in the future. Interested in the concept, Nelson requested Russell to also sign his guitar.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTENelson2005-149) In 1991, during his process with the IRS, Nelson was worried that Trigger could be auctioned off, stating: "When Trigger goes, I'll quit". He asked his daughter, Lana, to take the guitar from the studio before any IRS agent arrived there, and then deliver it to him in [Maui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maui "Maui").[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDraper1991103-152) Nelson then concealed the guitar in his manager's house until his debt was paid off in 1993.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWillie_Nelson_General_Store_staff2010-150)

## Political views and activism

Nelson has supported a number of causes. Along with [Neil Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Young "Neil Young") and [John Mellencamp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Mellencamp "John Mellencamp"), he set up [Farm Aid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farm_Aid "Farm Aid") in 1985 to assist and increase awareness of the importance of family farms, after [Bob Dylan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Dylan "Bob Dylan")'s comments during the [Live Aid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Aid "Live Aid") concert that he hoped some of the money would help American farmers in danger of losing their farms through mortgage debt.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDurchholzGraff2010134-153) The first concert included Dylan, [Billy Joel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Joel "Billy Joel"), [B.B. King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B.B._King "B.B. King"), [Roy Orbison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Orbison "Roy Orbison"), and Neil Young among many others, and raised over $9 million for America's family farmers.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDurchholzGraff2010135-154) Besides organizing and performing in the annual concerts, Nelson is the president of the board of Farm Aid.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTERichmond200094-155)

Nelson is a co-chair of the [National Organization for the Reform of Marijuana Laws](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Organization_for_the_Reform_of_Marijuana_Laws "National Organization for the Reform of Marijuana Laws") (NORML) advisory board.[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTENORML_staff2009-156) He has worked with NORML for years, promoting marijuana legalization. In 2005 Nelson and his family hosted the first annual "Willie Nelson & NORML Benefit Golf Tournament", leading to a cover appearance and inside interview in the January 2008 issue of _[High Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High\_Times "High Times")_ magazine.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHigh_Times_staff2007-157) After Nelson's arrest for possession of marijuana in 2010, he created Willie Nelson's TeaPot Party under the motto "Tax it, regulate it and legalize it!"[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEThomson2010-158) Nelson got 19 write-in votes for President of the United States in the Minnesota [Legal Marijuana Now](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legal_Marijuana_Now_Party "Legal Marijuana Now Party") presidential [primary held on March 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Minnesota_Legal_Marijuana_Now_presidential_primary "2024 Minnesota Legal Marijuana Now presidential primary"), 2024.[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-159)

In 2001, following the [September 11 attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_11_attacks "September 11 attacks"), Nelson participated in the benefit telethon _[America: A Tribute to Heroes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America:\_A\_Tribute\_to\_Heroes "America: A Tribute to Heroes")_, leading the rest of the celebrities singing the song "[America the Beautiful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America_the_Beautiful "America the Beautiful")".[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuayDamico2010[httpsbooksgooglecombooksidlx7i4YHl_NoCpgPA149_149]-160) In 2010, during an interview with [Larry King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_King "Larry King"), Nelson expressed his [doubts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9/11_conspiracy_theories "9/11 conspiracy theories") with regards to the attacks and the official story. Nelson explained that he could not believe that the buildings could collapse due to the planes, attributing instead the result to an implosion.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Reilly2010-161)

[![Image 17: A man with long white hair and white beard playing a guitar. He wears a black T-shirt, which is crossed by the red, white and blue strap of the guitar. He also wears black pants.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/84/Willie_Nelson_930_club_2012_-_12.jpg/250px-Willie_Nelson_930_club_2012_-_12.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Willie_Nelson_930_club_2012_-_12.jpg)

Nelson, and his guitar "[Trigger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trigger_(guitar) "Trigger (guitar)")", performing in 2012

Nelson supported [Dennis Kucinich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dennis_Kucinich "Dennis Kucinich")'s campaign in the [2004 Democratic presidential primaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States)_presidential_primaries,_2004 "Democratic Party (United States) presidential primaries, 2004"). He raised money, appeared at events, and composed the song "Whatever Happened to Peace on Earth?", criticizing the [war in Iraq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq_War "Iraq War").[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEReuters_staff2004-162) He recorded a radio advertisement asking for support to put musician/author [Kinky Friedman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinky_Friedman "Kinky Friedman") on the ballot as an independent candidate for the [2006 Texas gubernatorial election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_Texas_gubernatorial_election "2006 Texas gubernatorial election").[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHamilton2010-163) Friedman promised Nelson a job in Austin as the head of a new Texas Energy Commission due to his support of bio-fuels.[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBurt2005-164) In January 2008, Nelson filed a suit against the [Texas Democratic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Democratic_Party "Texas Democratic Party"), alleging that the party violated the [First](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution "First Amendment to the United States Constitution") and [Fourteenth Amendments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourteenth_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution "Fourteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution") of the [United States Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Constitution "United States Constitution") by refusing to allow co-plaintiff Kucinich to appear on the primary ballot because he had scratched out part of the [loyalty oath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loyalty_oath "Loyalty oath") on his application.[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTESelby2009-165)

Nelson is an advocate for better treatment for horses and has been campaigning for the passage of the [American Horse Slaughter Prevention Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horse_slaughter#Federal_bills "Horse slaughter") (H.R. 503/S. 311) alongside the [Animal Welfare Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_Welfare_Institute "Animal Welfare Institute").[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTENelson2007b-166) He is on its board of directors and has adopted a number of horses from _Habitat for Horses_.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHabitat_for_Horses_staff2011-167) In 2008, Nelson signed on to warn consumers about the cruel and illegal living conditions for calves raised to produce milk for dairy products. He wrote letters to [Land O'Lakes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_O%27Lakes "Land O'Lakes") and Challenge Dairy, two of the major corporations that use milk from calves raised at California's Mendes Calf Ranch, which employs an intensive confinement practice that was the subject of a lawsuit and campaign brought by the [Animal Legal Defense Fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_Legal_Defense_Fund "Animal Legal Defense Fund").[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTENelson2008-128) Nelson is seen in the film _[The Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Garden\_(2008\_film) "The Garden (2008 film)")_ supporting the impoverished community South Central Farm in Southern Los Angeles.[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKennedy2019-168)

A supporter of the [LGBT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBT "LGBT") movement, Nelson published in 2006 through [iTunes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITunes "ITunes") a version of [Ned Sublette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ned_Sublette "Ned Sublette")'s "[Cowboys Are Frequently, Secretly Fond of Each Other](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboys_Are_Frequently,_Secretly_Fond_of_Each_Other "Cowboys Are Frequently, Secretly Fond of Each Other")", that met instant success.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTENeu2006-169) During an interview with _[Texas Monthly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas\_Monthly "Texas Monthly")_ in 2013, regarding the [Defense of Marriage Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defense_of_Marriage_Act "Defense of Marriage Act") and [same-sex marriage in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_the_United_States "Same-sex marriage in the United States"), Nelson responded to a comparison the interviewer made with the [civil rights movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_Rights_Movement "Civil Rights Movement"), stating: "We'll look back and say it was crazy that we ever even argued about this". He also presented two logos with the pink equal sign, symbol of the LGBT movement. The first one, featured the sign represented with two long braids; while the second one, featured the sign represented with two marijuana cigarettes. The use of the logos became popular quickly in social networking sites such as Twitter and Facebook.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTELanger2013-170)

In June 2018, Nelson deplored the [Trump administration family separation policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trump_administration_family_separation_policy "Trump administration family separation policy").[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHudak2018-171) During his Fourth of July Picnic, he performed a song with [Beto O'Rourke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beto_O%27Rourke "Beto O'Rourke"), the Democratic candidate for the [Senate election in Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate_election_in_Texas,_2018 "United States Senate election in Texas, 2018"). Nelson endorsed O'Rourke, and received negative reactions from the conservative part of his followers.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTETaylor2018-172) On September 29, 2018, Nelson offered a free concert in Austin supporting the candidate's run. The last number he performed was "[Vote 'Em Out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vote_%27Em_Out "Vote 'Em Out")", a new track that was subsequently released as a single.[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHudak2018-171)

## Personal life

Nelson has been married four times and has eight children.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHollabaugh2010-173) His first marriage was to Martha Matthews from 1952 to 1962. The couple had three children: Lana, Susie, and Willie "Billy" Hugh Jr. The latter died by suicide in 1991.[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHall2008-174) The marriage was marked by violence, with Matthews assaulting Nelson several times,[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTECartwright2000[httpsbooksgooglecombooksidFBRbZWBZolUCpgPA276_276]-175) including one incident when she sewed him up in bedsheets and beat him with a broomstick.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGoldman2012-176) Nelson then married [Shirley Collie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shirley_Collie "Shirley Collie") in 1963. The couple divorced in 1971, after Collie found a bill from the maternity ward of a Houston hospital charged to Nelson and Connie Koepke for the birth of [Paula Carlene Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Nelson "Paula Nelson").[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTECartwright2000[httpsbooksgooglecombooksidFBRbZWBZolUCpgPA276_276]-175) Nelson married Koepke the same year, and they had another daughter, Amy Lee Nelson. Following a divorce in 1988, he married his current wife, Annie D'Angelo, in 1991. They have two sons, [Lukas Autry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lukas_Nelson_%26_Promise_of_the_Real "Lukas Nelson & Promise of the Real") and Jacob Micah.[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTERiggs2007239-177) In 2012, Nelson learned that he fathered a daughter with his friend Mary Haney. Born on January 22, 1953, Renee Butts (born Lynda Renee Barley) met Nelson and she shared a picture of both of them on Father's Day in 2016. Butts died in 2017.[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKrauser,_Emily2023-178)

Nelson owns "Luck, Texas", a ranch in [Spicewood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spicewood,_Texas "Spicewood, Texas"),[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTERolling_Stone_staff2017-179)[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEParker2014-180) and also lives in Maui, Hawaii[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKane2008-181) with several celebrity neighbors.[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrigoriadis200757-182) While swimming in Hawaii in 1981, Nelson's [lung collapsed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pneumothorax "Pneumothorax"). He was taken to the Maui Memorial Hospital and his scheduled concerts were canceled.[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKrebs1981-183) Nelson temporarily stopped smoking cigarettes each time his lungs became congested, and resumed when the congestion ended.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Hare2010-184) He was then smoking between two and three packs per day. After suffering from pneumonia several times, he decided to quit either marijuana or tobacco. He chose to quit tobacco.[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTENPR_staff2012-185) In 2008, he started to smoke marijuana with a carbon-free system to avoid the effects of smoke.[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPatoski2011-186) In 2004, Nelson underwent surgery for [carpal tunnel syndrome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carpal_tunnel_syndrome "Carpal tunnel syndrome"), as he had damaged his wrists by continuously playing the guitar.[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAssociated_Press_staff2002-187) On the recommendation of his doctor, he canceled his scheduled concerts and only wrote songs during his recovery.[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMiller_Loncaric2008-188) In 2012, he canceled a fund-raising appearance in the Denver area. He suffered from breathing problems due to high altitude and emphysema and was taken to a local hospital. His publicist Elaine Schock confirmed soon after that Nelson's health was good and that he was heading to his next scheduled concert in Dallas, Texas.[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcKinnley2012-189) After repeated instances of pneumonia and emphysema through the years, Nelson underwent [stem-cell therapy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stem-cell_therapy "Stem-cell therapy") in 2015 to improve the state of his lungs.[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeim2015-190)

During his childhood, Nelson grew interested in martial arts. He ordered self-defense manuals on [jujitsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jujitsu "Jujitsu") and judo that he saw advertised in _[Batman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman "Batman")_ and _[Superman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superman "Superman")_ comic books. Nelson started to formally practice [kung fu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kung_fu "Kung fu") after he moved to Nashville, in the 1960s.[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTENelsonShrakeShrake200055-191) During the 1980s, Nelson began training in [taekwondo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tae_kwon_do "Tae kwon do") and now holds a second-degree black belt in that discipline.[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChilton2012-192) During the 1990s, Nelson started to practice the Korean martial art [GongKwon Yusul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GongKwon_Yusul "GongKwon Yusul").[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHall2014-193) In 2014, after 20 years in the discipline, his Grand Master Sam Um presented him with a fifth-degree black belt in a ceremony held in Austin, Texas.[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChilton2014-194) A 2014 _[Tae Kwon Do Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tae\_Kwon\_Do\_Times "Tae Kwon Do Times")_ magazine interview revealed that Nelson had developed an unorthodox manner of training during the lengthy periods of time he was on tour. Nelson would conduct his martial arts training on his tour bus "The Honeysuckle Rose" and send videos to his supervising Master for review and critique.[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEZirogiannis2014-195)

In March 2021, Nelson recorded a version of the popular standard "[I'll Be Seeing You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I%27ll_Be_Seeing_You_(song) "I'll Be Seeing You (song)")" that was used on a [public service announcement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_service_announcement "Public service announcement") by the [Ad Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ad_Council "Ad Council") to encourage [COVID-19 vaccination in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_vaccination_in_the_United_States "COVID-19 vaccination in the United States").[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWeisholtz,_Drew2021-196) Earlier in January 2021, Nelson and his sister received the [Moderna COVID-19 vaccine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moderna_COVID-19_vaccine "Moderna COVID-19 vaccine").[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDoyle,_Patrick2021-197) In May 2022, Nelson postponed several shows after he contracted [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19"). Nelson's wife detailed that he was severely affected by the illness, and that he received a treatment including [Paxlovid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paxlovid "Paxlovid"), [monoclonal antibodies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monoclonal_antibody "Monoclonal antibody"), and steroids.
