_Rural flight_ is the departure of excess populations (usually young men and women) from farm areas. In some cases whole families left, as in the [Dust Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dust_Bowl "Dust Bowl") in the 1930s. Much of rural America has seen steady population decline since 1920.

### Black migration out of the South

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Demographic_history_of_the_United_States&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Black migration out of the South")]

The **Great Migration** was the movement of millions of [African Americans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Americans "African Americans") out of the rural [Southern United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_United_States "Southern United States") from 1914 to 1960. Most moved to large industrial cities, as well as to many smaller industrial cities. African-Americans moved as individuals or small groups. There was no government assistance. They migrated because of a variety of push and pull factors:[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-33)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-34)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-35)

1.   Many African-Americans wanted to avoid the lynching and racial segregation of the [Jim Crow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Crow_laws "Jim Crow laws") South and sought refuge in the supposed "Promised Land" of the North where there was thought to be less segregation.
2.   The [boll weevil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boll_weevil "Boll weevil") infestation of the [cotton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cotton "Cotton") fields of the South in the late 1910s reduced the demand for [sharecroppers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharecropping "Sharecropping").
3.   The [Great Mississippi Flood of 1927](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Mississippi_Flood_of_1927 "Great Mississippi Flood of 1927") and its aftermath displaced hundreds of thousands of African-American farm workers.

1.   Income levels were much higher in the North, with far higher wages in the service sector.
2.   The enormous growth of war industries in WW1 and WW2 created new job openings for blacks.
3.   [World War I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I "World War I") effectively put a halt to the flow of European immigrants to the industrial centers, causing shortages of workers in the factories.
4.   In the 1930s [Works Progress Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Works_Progress_Administration "Works Progress Administration"), [Civilian Conservation Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civilian_Conservation_Corps "Civilian Conservation Corps") and other relief programs in the North were more receptive to blacks. The WPA paid more in the North.
5.   After 1940, as the US rearmed for [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") (see [Homefront-United States-World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_home_front_during_World_War_II "United States home front during World War II")), industrial production increased rapidly.
6.   The [FEPC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fair_Employment_Practice_Committee "Fair Employment Practice Committee") equal opportunity laws were more enforced in the North and West.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-36)

The proportion of Americans who move across state lines fell by 50% from 1990 to 2018. Regional disparities in local economies have also grown during this time, meaning that more people remain in economically depressed areas.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-37) By 2011, migration levels were at the lowest level since [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), and were in the longest period of continuous decline in the twentieth century.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-38)

## Recent demographic trends

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Demographic_history_of_the_United_States&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Recent demographic trends")]

[![Image 3](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bb/United_States_Birth_Rates.svg/330px-United_States_Birth_Rates.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:United_States_Birth_Rates.svg)

United States birth rate (births per 1000 population).[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-39) The [United States Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau "United States Census Bureau") defines the demographic birth boom as between 1946 and 1964[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-census2006-40) (red).

In the years after WWII, the United States, as well as a number of other industrialized countries, experienced an unexpected sudden birth rate jump. During WWII birthrates had been low, as millions of men had been away fighting in WWII and this had deterred women from starting families: women also had to take the place of men in the workplace, while simultaneously fulfilling their household duties. The millions of men coming back to the US after WWII, and the couples eager to start families, led to a sharp rise in the US birth rate, and a surge in new housing construction in the suburbs and outlying areas of the cities. Since the men who came back got jobs in the workplace again, married women stayed home to take care of the house and children and let their husbands be the [breadwinner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breadwinner_model "Breadwinner model") of the household.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-41)

During the baby boom years, between 1946 and 1964, the birth rate doubled for third children and tripled for fourth children.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-WHC-42)

The total fertility rate of the United States jumped from 2.49 in 1945 to 2.94 in 1946, a rise of 0.45 children therefore beginning the baby boom. It continued to rise throughout the 1940s to reach 3.10 in 1950 with a peak of 3.77 in 1957. Declining slowly thereafter to 3.65 in 1960 and finally a steep from decline after 1964, therefore ending the baby boom.

According to statistics, the United States currently has the highest marriage rate in the developed world, as of 2008, with a marriage rate of 7.1 per 1,000 people or 2,162,000 marriages. The average age for first marriage for men is 27.4 and 25.6 years for women.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-45) The United States also has one of the highest proportions of people who do marry by age 40; approximately 85% Americans are married at 40, compared to only 60% in Sweden.

During the 1930s, the number of marriages and the marriage rate dropped steeply due to the Great Depression, but rebounded almost immediately after the Depression ended. Marriage rates increased and remained at high levels in the late 1930 to the mid-1940s. The number of marriages shot up to reach over 2 million in 1946, with a marriage rate of 16.4 per 1,000 people as WWII had ended. The average age at first marriage for both men and women began to fall after WWII, dropping 22.8 for men and 20.3 for women in 1950 and dropping even more to 22.5 and 20.1 years in 1956. In 1959, the United States Census Bureau estimated that 47% of all brides marrying for their first time were teenagers aged 19 and under. In 1955, 51.2% of women were married by their 20th birthday and 88% by their 25th birthday; 40.3% of men and 28.5% of women aged 20–24 in 1955 had never married, down from 77.8% for men and 57.4% for women in 1940.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-46)

As of 2002, 4.3% of men and 18.1% of women aged 20 are married, increasing to 37% of men and 52% of women by age 25, and then 61% of men and 76% of women by age 30.

### Population growth projections

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Demographic_history_of_the_United_States&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Population growth projections")]

The US population in 1900 was 76 million. In 1950, it rose to 152 million; by 2000 it had reached 282 million. By 2050, it is expected to reach 422–458 million, depending on immigration.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-47)

## Demographic models in historiography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Demographic_history_of_the_United_States&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Demographic models in historiography")]

[Richard Easterlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Easterlin "Richard Easterlin"), an economist who has researched economic growth in the United States, explains the growth pattern of the American population in the 20th century through fertility rate fluctuations and the decreasing mortality rate. Easterlin has attempted to explain the cause of the Baby Boom and Baby Bust through the "relative income" theory. The "relative income" theory suggests that couples choose to have children based on a couple's ratio of potential earning power and the desire to obtain material objects. This ratio depends on the economic stability of the country in which they live and how people are raised to value material objects. The "relative income" theory explains the Baby Boom by suggesting that the late 1940s and 1950s brought low desires to have material objects, as a result of the Great Depression and WWII, as well as huge job opportunities, because of it being a post-war period. These two factors gave rise to a high relative income, which encouraged high fertility. Following this period, the next generation had a greater desire for material objects; however, an economic slowdown in the United States made jobs harder to acquire. This resulted in lower fertility rates, causing the Baby Bust.

Between 1880 and 1900, the urban population of the United States rose from 28% to 40%, and reached 50% by 1920, in part due to 9,000,000 [European](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europe "Europe")[immigrants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immigration "Immigration"). After 1890 the US rural population began to plummet, as farmers were displaced by mechanization and forced to migrate to urban factory jobs. After World War II, the US experienced a shift away from the cities and into suburbs mostly due to the cost of land, the availability of low-cost government home loans, fair housing policies, and the construction of highways.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-48) Many of the original manufacturing cities lost as much as half their populations between 1950 and 1980. There was a shift in the population from the dense city centers filled with apartments, row homes, and tenements; to less dense suburban neighborhoods outside the cities which were filled with single-family homes.

The [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") is a country primarily located in North America. [Demographics of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographics_of_the_United_States "Demographics of the United States") concern matters of [population density](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_density "Population density"), [ethnicity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethnic_group "Ethnic group"), education level, [health of the populace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_health "Population health"), economic status, religious affiliations, and other aspects regarding the population.

### Earlier colonial era

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Demographic_history_of_the_United_States&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Earlier colonial era")]

Nearly all non-Native American commercial activity was run in small privately owned businesses with good credit both at home and in England being essential since they were often cash poor. Most settlements were nearly independent of trade with Britain as most grew or made nearly everything they needed—the average cost of imports for most households was only about 5-15 English pounds per year. Most settlements were created by complete family groups with several generations often present. Probably close to 80% of the families owned the land they lived and farmed on. They nearly all used English Common Law as their basic code of law and, except for the French, Dutch and Germans spoke some dialect of English. They established their own popularly elected governments and courts and were mostly self-governing, self-supporting, and self-replicating.

Nearly all colonies and, later, states in the United States were settled by migration from another colony or state, as foreign immigration usually only played a minor role after first initial settlements were established.

The New England colonists included some educated men as well as many skilled farmers, tradesmen and craftsmen. They were mostly farmers and settled in small villages for common religious activity. Shipbuilding, commerce, and fisheries were important in coastal towns. New England's healthy climate (the cold winters killed mosquitoes and other disease-bearing insects), and abundant food supply resulted in the lowest death rate and highest birth rate of any place in the world (marriage was expected and birth control was not, and a much higher than average number of children and mothers survived).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-8)

The eastern and northern frontier around the initial New England settlements was mainly settled by the [Yankee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yankee "Yankee") descendants of the original New Englanders. Emigration to the New England colonies after 1640 and the start of the [English Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_Civil_War "English Civil War") decreased to less than 1% (about equal to the death rate) in nearly all years before 1845. The rapid growth of the New England colonies (total population ≈700,000 by 1790) was almost entirely due to the high birth rate (>3%) and low death rate (<1%) per year.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-9)

The middle colonies' settlements were scattered west of [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"), [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_(state) "New York (state)") (est. 1626 by Dutch, taken over by the English in 1664) and [Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia"), [Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania "Pennsylvania") (est. 1682). The Dutch-started colony of New York had an eclectic collection of residents from many different nations and prospered as a major trading and commercial center after about 1700. Pennsylvania was dominated by the Quakers for decades after they emigrated there, mainly from the North Midlands of England, from about 1680 to 1725. The main commercial center of Philadelphia was run mostly by prosperous Quakers, supplemented by many small farming and trading communities with strong German contingents located in the Delaware River valley.

Many more settlers arrived in the middle colonies starting in about 1680, when Pennsylvania was founded, and many Protestant sects were encouraged to settle there for freedom of religion and good, cheap land. These settlers were of about 60% German and 33% English extraction. By 1780 about 27% of New York's population were descendants of Dutch settlers (55,000 of 204,000). New Jersey was home to the remaining Dutch and they constituted 14% of the population of 140,000. The rest were mostly English with a mixture of other Europeans and about 6% Blacks. New Jersey and Delaware had a majority of British with 20% German-descended colonists, about a 6% black population, and a small contingent of Swedish descendants of [New Sweden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Sweden "New Sweden"). Nearly all were at least third-generation natives.

The main feature of the economy in Virginia, Maryland and South Carolina was large plantations growing staples for export, especially tobacco and rice. Outside the plantations, land was farmed by independent farmers who rented from the proprietors, or (most often) owned it outright. They emphasized subsistence farming to grow food for their large families. Many of the Irish immigrants specialized in making rye whiskey, which they sold to obtain cash. In Maryland, by 1700 there were about 25,000 people and by 1750 that had grown more than 5 times to 130,000. By 1755, about 40% of Maryland's population was black.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-10)

From 1717 to 1775 the western frontier was populated primarily by Presbyterian settlers who migrated from Scotland and Ireland. Frontier settlers initially landed in Philadelphia or Baltimore before migrating to the western frontier for the cheaper land.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-11)

All the colonies grew mostly by natural growth, with foreign born populations rarely exceeding 10%. The last significant colonies to be settled mainly by immigrants were Pennsylvania in the early 18th century and Georgia and the Borderlands in the late 18th century, as [internal migration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internal_migration "Internal migration") (not immigration) continued to provide nearly all the settlers for each new colony or state. This pattern would continue throughout US history. The extent of colonial settlements by 1800 is shown by this map from the University of Texas map collection.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-12)

### Immigration 1791 to 1849

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Demographic_history_of_the_United_States&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Immigration 1791 to 1849")]

In the early years of the United States, immigration average about 6,000 people per year, including French [refugees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Refugee "Refugee") from the slave revolt in [Haiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haiti "Haiti"). The [French Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Revolution "French Revolution"), starting in 1789, and the [Napoleonic Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleonic_Wars "Napoleonic Wars") from 1792 to 1814 severely limited immigration from Europe. The [War of 1812](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_of_1812 "War of 1812") (1812–1814) with Britain again prevented any significant immigration. By 1808 Congress had banned the transport of slaves, slowing that human traffic to a trickle.

After 1820 immigration gradually increased. For the first time federal records, including ship passenger lists, were kept for immigration. Total immigration for the year 1820 was 8,385, gradually building to 23,322 by 1830, with 143,000 total immigrating during the decade. From 1831 to 1840 immigration increased greatly, to 599,000 total, as 207,000 Irish, even before the [famine of 1845–1849](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Famine_(Ireland) "Great Famine (Ireland)"), started to emigrate in large numbers as Britain eased travel restrictions. 152,000 Germans, 76,000 British, and 46,000 French formed the next largest immigrant groups in that decade.

From 1841 to 1850 immigration exploded to 1,713,000 total immigrants and at least 781,000 Irish who fled their homeland to escape poverty or death during the famine of 1845–1849. In attempting to divert some of this traffic to help settle Canada, the British offered bargain fares of 15 shillings for transit to Canada, instead of the normal 5 pounds (100 shillings). Thousands of poor Irish took advantage of this offer and headed to Canada on what came to be called the "coffin ships" because of their high death rates. Once in Canada, many Irish walked across the border or caught an intercoastal freighter to the nearest major city in the United States – usually Boston or New York. Bad potato crops and failed revolutions struck the heart of Europe in 1848, contributing to the decade's total of 435,000 Germans, 267,000 British and 77,000 French immigrants to America. Bad times in Europe drove people out; land, relatives, freedom, opportunity, and jobs in America lured them in.

It is probably a reasonable estimate that the foreign born population in the US reached its minimum in about 1815 at something like 100,000, or 1.4% of the population. By 1815 most of the immigrants that arrived before the [American Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Revolution "American Revolution") had died, and there had been almost no new immigration.

The total number immigrating in each decade from 1790 to 1820 are estimates.

The number of foreign born in the 1830s and 1840s are extrapolations.

Nearly all population growth up to 1830 was by internal increase; about 98.5% of the population was native-born. By 1850, this had shifted to about 90% native-born. The first significant Catholic immigration started in the mid-1840s.

### Immigration 1965 to present

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Demographic_history_of_the_United_States&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Immigration 1965 to present")]

In 1965, US immigration law changes reduced the emphasis on national origin. Prior policy favored European immigrants. The 1965 law directed that those with relatives in the US or employer sponsorship now had priority. By the 1970s, most immigrants to the US came from Latin America or Asia, rather than Europe. Since 2000, over three quarters of all immigrants to the US have come from Asia and Latin America.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-32)

## Migration within the United States

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Demographic_history_of_the_United_States&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Migration within the United States")]

In 1848, the [Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Guadalupe_Hidalgo "Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo"), concluding the Mexican War, extended US citizenship to approximately 60,000 Mexican residents of the [New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico "New Mexico") Territory and 10,000 living in [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California"). However, much like Texas, the Mexican government had encouraged immigration and settlement of these regions from groups in the United States and Europe. Approximately half of this population is estimated to have been of American origin. In 1849, the [California Gold Rush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Gold_Rush "California Gold Rush") spurred significant immigration from Mexico, South America, China, Australia, Europe and caused a mass internal migration within the US, resulting in California gaining statehood in 1850, with a population of about 90,000.

_Rural flight_ is the departure of excess populations (usually young men and women) from farm areas. In some cases whole families left, as in the [Dust Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dust_Bowl "Dust Bowl") in the 1930s. Much of rural America has seen steady population decline since 1920.

### Black migration out of the South

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Demographic_history_of_the_United_States&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Black migration out of the South")]

The **Great Migration** was the movement of millions of [African Americans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Americans "African Americans") out of the rural [Southern United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_United_States "Southern United States") from 1914 to 1960. Most moved to large industrial cities, as well as to many smaller industrial cities. African-Americans moved as individuals or small groups. There was no government assistance. They migrated because of a variety of push and pull factors:[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-33)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-34)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-35)

1.   Many African-Americans wanted to avoid the lynching and racial segregation of the [Jim Crow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Crow_laws "Jim Crow laws") South and sought refuge in the supposed "Promised Land" of the North where there was thought to be less segregation.
2.   The [boll weevil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boll_weevil "Boll weevil") infestation of the [cotton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cotton "Cotton") fields of the South in the late 1910s reduced the demand for [sharecroppers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharecropping "Sharecropping").
3.   The [Great Mississippi Flood of 1927](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Mississippi_Flood_of_1927 "Great Mississippi Flood of 1927") and its aftermath displaced hundreds of thousands of African-American farm workers.

1.   Income levels were much higher in the North, with far higher wages in the service sector.
2.   The enormous growth of war industries in WW1 and WW2 created new job openings for blacks.
3.   [World War I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I "World War I") effectively put a halt to the flow of European immigrants to the industrial centers, causing shortages of workers in the factories.
4.   In the 1930s [Works Progress Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Works_Progress_Administration "Works Progress Administration"), [Civilian Conservation Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civilian_Conservation_Corps "Civilian Conservation Corps") and other relief programs in the North were more receptive to blacks. The WPA paid more in the North.
5.   After 1940, as the US rearmed for [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") (see [Homefront-United States-World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_home_front_during_World_War_II "United States home front during World War II")), industrial production increased rapidly.
6.   The [FEPC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fair_Employment_Practice_Committee "Fair Employment Practice Committee") equal opportunity laws were more enforced in the North and West.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-36)

The proportion of Americans who move across state lines fell by 50% from 1990 to 2018. Regional disparities in local economies have also grown during this time, meaning that more people remain in economically depressed areas.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-37) By 2011, migration levels were at the lowest level since [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), and were in the longest period of continuous decline in the twentieth century.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-38)

## Recent demographic trends

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Demographic_history_of_the_United_States&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Recent demographic trends")]

[![Image 3](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bb/United_States_Birth_Rates.svg/330px-United_States_Birth_Rates.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:United_States_Birth_Rates.svg)

United States birth rate (births per 1000 population).[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-39) The [United States Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau "United States Census Bureau") defines the demographic birth boom as between 1946 and 1964[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-census2006-40) (red).

In the years after WWII, the United States, as well as a number of other industrialized countries, experienced an unexpected sudden birth rate jump. During WWII birthrates had been low, as millions of men had been away fighting in WWII and this had deterred women from starting families: women also had to take the place of men in the workplace, while simultaneously fulfilling their household duties. The millions of men coming back to the US after WWII, and the couples eager to start families, led to a sharp rise in the US birth rate, and a surge in new housing construction in the suburbs and outlying areas of the cities. Since the men who came back got jobs in the workplace again, married women stayed home to take care of the house and children and let their husbands be the [breadwinner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breadwinner_model "Breadwinner model") of the household.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-41)

During the baby boom years, between 1946 and 1964, the birth rate doubled for third children and tripled for fourth children.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-WHC-42)

The total fertility rate of the United States jumped from 2.49 in 1945 to 2.94 in 1946, a rise of 0.45 children therefore beginning the baby boom. It continued to rise throughout the 1940s to reach 3.10 in 1950 with a peak of 3.77 in 1957. Declining slowly thereafter to 3.65 in 1960 and finally a steep from decline after 1964, therefore ending the baby boom.

According to statistics, the United States currently has the highest marriage rate in the developed world, as of 2008, with a marriage rate of 7.1 per 1,000 people or 2,162,000 marriages. The average age for first marriage for men is 27.4 and 25.6 years for women.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-45) The United States also has one of the highest proportions of people who do marry by age 40; approximately 85% Americans are married at 40, compared to only 60% in Sweden.

During the 1930s, the number of marriages and the marriage rate dropped steeply due to the Great Depression, but rebounded almost immediately after the Depression ended. Marriage rates increased and remained at high levels in the late 1930 to the mid-1940s. The number of marriages shot up to reach over 2 million in 1946, with a marriage rate of 16.4 per 1,000 people as WWII had ended. The average age at first marriage for both men and women began to fall after WWII, dropping 22.8 for men and 20.3 for women in 1950 and dropping even more to 22.5 and 20.1 years in 1956. In 1959, the United States Census Bureau estimated that 47% of all brides marrying for their first time were teenagers aged 19 and under. In 1955, 51.2% of women were married by their 20th birthday and 88% by their 25th birthday; 40.3% of men and 28.5% of women aged 20–24 in 1955 had never married, down from 77.8% for men and 57.4% for women in 1940.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-46)

As of 2002, 4.3% of men and 18.1% of women aged 20 are married, increasing to 37% of men and 52% of women by age 25, and then 61% of men and 76% of women by age 30.

### Population growth projections

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Demographic_history_of_the_United_States&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Population growth projections")]

The US population in 1900 was 76 million. In 1950, it rose to 152 million; by 2000 it had reached 282 million. By 2050, it is expected to reach 422–458 million, depending on immigration.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-47)

## Demographic models in historiography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Demographic_history_of_the_United_States&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Demographic models in historiography")]

[Richard Easterlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Easterlin "Richard Easterlin"), an economist who has researched economic growth in the United States, explains the growth pattern of the American population in the 20th century through fertility rate fluctuations and the decreasing mortality rate. Easterlin has attempted to explain the cause of the Baby Boom and Baby Bust through the "relative income" theory. The "relative income" theory suggests that couples choose to have children based on a couple's ratio of potential earning power and the desire to obtain material objects. This ratio depends on the economic stability of the country in which they live and how people are raised to value material objects. The "relative income" theory explains the Baby Boom by suggesting that the late 1940s and 1950s brought low desires to have material objects, as a result of the Great Depression and WWII, as well as huge job opportunities, because of it being a post-war period. These two factors gave rise to a high relative income, which encouraged high fertility. Following this period, the next generation had a greater desire for material objects; however, an economic slowdown in the United States made jobs harder to acquire. This resulted in lower fertility rates, causing the Baby Bust.

Between 1880 and 1900, the urban population of the United States rose from 28% to 40%, and reached 50% by 1920, in part due to 9,000,000 [European](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europe "Europe")[immigrants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immigration "Immigration"). After 1890 the US rural population began to plummet, as farmers were displaced by mechanization and forced to migrate to urban factory jobs. After World War II, the US experienced a shift away from the cities and into suburbs mostly due to the cost of land, the availability of low-cost government home loans, fair housing policies, and the construction of highways.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_the_United_States#cite_note-48) Many of the original manufacturing cities lost as much as half their populations between 1950 and 1980. There was a shift in the population from the dense city centers filled with apartments, row homes, and tenements; to less dense suburban neighborhoods outside the cities which were filled with single-family homes.

Title: Linda Yaccarino is leaving Elon Musk’s X after two years as CEO

URL Source: https://www.cnn.com/2025/07/09/tech/linda-yaccarino-steps-down-x-ceo

Published Time: 2025-07-09T14:49:07.044Z

Markdown Content:
New York—

Linda Yaccarino is stepping down as CEO of X after two years leading Elon Musk’s social media company.

Yaccarino’s departure comes one day after the company’s Grok chatbot [began pushing antisemitic tropes](https://www.cnn.com/2025/07/08/tech/grok-ai-antisemitism) in responses to users. It’s not clear that the events were connected.

Her exit also comes months after Musk [sold X](https://www.cnn.com/2025/03/28/business/elon-musk-sells-x-to-xai), his social media company, to xAI, his artificial intelligence company. The move formally combined the two entities that were already closely intertwined, but raised questions about Yaccarino’s role in the new company going forward.

Ad Feedback

Yaccarino announced her exit in a [post](https://x.com/lindayax/status/1942957094811951197?s=46) on the platform, saying she is “immensely grateful” to Musk for “entrusting me with the responsibility of protecting free speech, turning the company around, and transforming X into the Everything App.”

“Now, the best is yet to come as X enters a new chapter with @xai,” she said in the post. “I’ll be cheering you all on as you continue to change the world.”

Musk replied to Yaccarino’s post with a [terse response](https://x.com/elonmusk/status/1942967206993961124): “Thank you for your contributions.”

One current X employee, who requested anonymity because they weren’t authorized to speak publicly, said Yaccarino’s exit wasn’t entirely surprising, in light of the ongoing challenges the company has faced convincing advertisers to return to the platform – something the longtime marketing executive was brought in to do.

In November 2023, Musk publicly [lashed out at advertisers](https://www.cnn.com/videos/media/2023/11/30/elon-musk-x-advertisers-boycott-platform-antisemitism-ebof-vpx.cnn) leaving the platform, telling them to “go f**k yourself.” The fallout from that outburst with brands has been “ongoing,” the employee said, and escalated with Musk’s involvement in President Donald Trump’s administration.

X’s combination with xAI also raised questions about the company’s priorities, with Musk more focused on product improvements than business operations, they said.

“There’s been a lack of clarity, internally and externally as well, of what X is supposed to be,” the employee said, adding that working with the company’s partners is more difficult “if you can’t articulate what our plan is for the next three years.”

As of Wednesday night, Musk had not made any staff-wide comments to X employees about Yaccarino’s departure, the employee said.

Yaccarino, a former NBCUniversal marketing executive, [took over](https://www.cnn.com/2023/06/05/tech/linda-yaccarino-twitter-ceo-elon-musk) from Musk as CEO of X — at the time, it was called Twitter — in June of 2023, about eight months after the billionaire bought the social media platform. She was brought on to help fix the platform’s flagging advertising business, after Musk [alienated brands](https://www.cnn.com/2022/11/04/tech/twitter-advertisers) with his controversial comments and changes to the platform.

But her tenure has been marked by repeated public relations crises, including scrutiny over antisemitic and other hateful content spreading on the platform, viral [false claims around international conflicts](https://www.cnn.com/2023/10/09/tech/musk-x-misinformation-israel-hamas-conflict) and ads that appeared alongside pro-Nazi content on the site. That led some [brands to pull their spending](https://www.cnn.com/2023/11/17/tech/lionsgate-suspends-advertising-x-musk/index.html), for [which the Yaccarino-led X sued an advertising industry group](https://www.cnn.com/2024/08/06/tech/musk-x-sues-garm-advertising-boycott) — a lawsuit Yaccarino announced in a video message to all X users, in which she decried what she referred to as a conspiracy to boycott the X platform. (The industry group, Global Alliance for Responsible Media, [shut down](https://www.cnn.com/2024/08/09/tech/elon-musk-garm-advertisers-lawsuit) days after the lawsuit was filed.)

In the years since Musk took over X, the company has also had to contend with a rush of new competitors, including Bluesky and Meta’s Threads.

Yaccarino repeatedly touted the company’s “freedom of speech, not freedom of reach” policy that aims to limit the reach of so-called lawful but awful content on the platform. Under her leadership, X also said it had rolled out additional brand safety controls for advertisers, including the ability to avoid having their ads show next to “targeted hate speech, sexual content, gratuitous gore, excessive profanity, obscenity, spam, drugs.”

But the company’s challenges escalated after X integrated xAI’s Grok chatbot into the platform, where users can ask the AI questions and bring it into conversation threads with other users. In May, Grok [erroneously brought up](https://www.cnn.com/2025/05/14/business/grok-ai-chatbot-replies) a theory of “white genocide” in South Africa in response to unrelated questions. And on Tuesday — weeks after Musk said he would rebuild the chatbot because he was unsatisfied with some of its replies that he viewed as too politically correct — the chatbot shared antisemitic tropes. In response, xAI said it removed some posts and “has taken action to ban hate speech before Grok posts on X.”

It’s not clear whether Yaccarino, as head of the social media business, had any control over Grok or the company’s other AI operations.

During her time as CEO of X, Yaccarino also faced questions about her power and influence over the company compared to Musk. The billionaire has said he is the company’s chief technology officer, leading product and technology teams, but his controversial statements and seemingly off-the-cuff policy pronouncements often seemed to leave Yaccarino on the back foot.

“Being the CEO of X was always going to be a tough job, and Yaccarino lasted in the role longer than many expected,” Jasmine Enberg, vice president at research firm Emarketer, said in emailed commentary. “Faced with a mercurial owner who never fully stepped away from the helm and continued to use the platform as his personal megaphone, Yaccarino had to try to run the business while also regularly putting out fires.”

Anne Marie Malecha, CEO of reputation and crisis management firm Dezenhall Resources, added that Musk is “one of those people that is willing to do whatever works for him during that day,” which could have put Yaccarino in a “very difficult position.”

And while X announced on-platform video podcasts with high-profile figures like Khloe Kardashian and several new finance tools, including a [partnership with Visa](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/01/28/elon-musk-x-visa-digital-wallet.html) to provide peer-to-peer payments, those features are niche offerings and the platform has not exactly become the “everything app” Yaccarino said she wanted to create.

Use of the platform has also fallen during her tenure, from 915.9 million combined active app users and unique website visitors during the month she took over to just 684.2 million last month, according to web traffic analysis firm Similarweb.

Yaccarino’s exit comes at a complicated time for Musk’s businesses, [especially Tesla](https://www.cnn.com/2025/07/08/business/tesla-troubled-financial-outlook), and his political involvement has raised questions about his ability and commitment to lead multiple companies. Her departure comes shortly after several high level exits at Tesla, including Omead Afshar, Tesla’s head of manufacturing and operations.

Musk has also recently engaged in a [high-profile feud](https://www.cnn.com/business/timeline-elon-musk-trump-x-dg) with President Donald Trump, whom he’d previously supported, that has created a rift between Musk-world and Trump-world and prompted threats from the White House against the billionaire’s companies.

“I don’t think anyone believed (Yaccarino) would make it this long,” said Malecha. “I also don’t think that anyone anticipated that Musk would become part of the political zeitgeist in the way that he did during that two-year period.”

Malecha added that Yaccarino’s exit could have been negotiated as part of X’s merger with xAI, “and, frankly, if I’m her, I wouldn’t be upset at my exit right now, based on what I’m seeing out of this AI.”

_This story has been updated with additional details and context._

_CNN’s Hadas Gold contributed to this report._

| Born | Edward Joseph Snowden June 21, 1983 (age 42) [Elizabeth City, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_City,_North_Carolina "Elizabeth City, North Carolina"), U.S. |
| Citizenship | * United States * Russia (since 2022) |
| Alma mater | * [Anne Arundel Community College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anne_Arundel_Community_College "Anne Arundel Community College") * [University of Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Liverpool "University of Liverpool") |
| Occupation | Computer security consultant |
| Employers | * [University of Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Maryland "University of Maryland") (2005) * [CIA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Intelligence_Agency "Central Intelligence Agency") (2006–2009) * [Dell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dell "Dell") (2009–2013) * [Booz Allen Hamilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Booz_Allen_Hamilton "Booz Allen Hamilton") (2013) |
| Known for | [Revealing classified U.S. Government surveillance programs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snowden_disclosures "Snowden disclosures"); in exile in Russia since June 23, 2013 |
| Spouse | [Lindsay Mills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Mills "Lindsay Mills") ​ (m.2017)​ |
| Children | 2[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-1) |
| Relatives | [Edward J. Barrett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_J._Barrett "Edward J. Barrett") (grandfather) |
| Awards | [Right Livelihood Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_Livelihood_Award "Right Livelihood Award") |

| Signature |
| [![Image 2](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4e/Edward_Snowden_signature_2013.svg/250px-Edward_Snowden_signature_2013.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Edward_Snowden_signature_2013.svg) |

**Edward Joseph Snowden** (born June 21, 1983) is a former United States [National Security Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Security_Agency "National Security Agency") (NSA) intelligence contractor who [leaked classified documents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snowden_disclosures "Snowden disclosures") revealing the existence of [global surveillance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_surveillance "Global surveillance") programs.

Born in 1983 in [Elizabeth City, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_City,_North_Carolina "Elizabeth City, North Carolina"), he attended a community college and later enrolled in a master's programme at the [University of Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Liverpool "University of Liverpool") without finishing it. In 2006 he started working for the [Central Intelligence Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Intelligence_Agency "Central Intelligence Agency") (CIA) and then moved to [Dell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dell "Dell") in 2009, where he managed computer systems for the NSA. In 2013, he worked for two months at [Booz Allen Hamilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Booz_Allen_Hamilton "Booz Allen Hamilton"), with the purpose of gathering more NSA documents.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-VanityFair-2)

In May 2013, Snowden flew to [Hong Kong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hong_Kong "Hong Kong"), and in early June he revealed thousands of classified NSA documents to journalists [Glenn Greenwald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Greenwald "Glenn Greenwald"), [Laura Poitras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Poitras "Laura Poitras"), [Barton Gellman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barton_Gellman "Barton Gellman"), and [Ewen MacAskill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ewen_MacAskill "Ewen MacAskill"). [His disclosures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snowden_disclosures "Snowden disclosures") revealed numerous [global surveillance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_surveillance "Global surveillance") programs, many run by the NSA and the [Five Eyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Five_Eyes "Five Eyes") intelligence alliance with the cooperation of [telecommunications companies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telephone_company "Telephone company") and European governments, and [prompted a cultural discussion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reactions_to_global_surveillance_disclosures "Reactions to global surveillance disclosures") about [national security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_security "National security") and individual privacy.

On June 21, 2013, the [United States Department of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Justice "United States Department of Justice") unsealed charges against Snowden on two counts of violating the [Espionage Act of 1917](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Espionage_Act_of_1917 "Espionage Act of 1917") and theft of government property,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-wapocharges-3) following which the [Department of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_State "United States Department of State") revoked his [passport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_passport "United States passport").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-KerryPassport-4) He stayed in [Sheremetyevo International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheremetyevo_International_Airport "Sheremetyevo International Airport") in Moscow for a month before [being granted asylum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden_asylum_in_Russia "Edward Snowden asylum in Russia").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-5) He became a [naturalized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naturalization "Naturalization") Russian citizen in 2022.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-:2-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-7)

In early 2016, Snowden became the president of the [Freedom of the Press Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freedom_of_the_Press_Foundation "Freedom of the Press Foundation"), a San Francisco–based nonprofit organization that aims to protect journalists from hacking and government surveillance.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-8) He also has a job at an unnamed Russian [IT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_technology "Information technology") company.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-Paid_speeches-9) In 2017, he married [Lindsay Mills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Mills "Lindsay Mills"). On September 17, 2019, his memoir _[Permanent Record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Permanent\_Record\_(autobiography) "Permanent Record (autobiography)")_ was published.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-I_was_very_much_a_person_the_most_powerful_government_in_the_world_wanted_to_go_away-10) On September 2, 2020, a U.S. federal court ruled in _[United States v. Moalin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United\_States\_v.\_Moalin "United States v. Moalin")_ that one of the [U.S. intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._intelligence "U.S. intelligence")'s mass surveillance programs exposed by Snowden was illegal and possibly [unconstitutional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unconstitutional_constitutional_amendment "Unconstitutional constitutional amendment").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-reuters.com-11)

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edward_Snowden&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Edward Joseph Snowden was born on June 21, 1983,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-BirthDate-12) in [Elizabeth City, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_City,_North_Carolina "Elizabeth City, North Carolina").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-snowdenhasdoc-13) Snowden's father, Lonnie "Lon", was a warrant officer in the [U.S. Coast Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Coast_Guard "United States Coast Guard"),[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-14) and his mother, Elizabeth, was a clerk at the [U.S. District Court for the District of Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_District_Court_for_the_District_of_Maryland "United States District Court for the District of Maryland").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-NBCNews_Snowden-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-autogenerated7-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-19) His older sister, Jessica, was a lawyer at the [Federal Judicial Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Judicial_Center "Federal Judicial Center") in [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.") His maternal grandfather, [Edward J. Barrett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_J._Barrett "Edward J. Barrett"),[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-21) a [rear admiral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rear_admiral "Rear admiral") in the Coast Guard, became a senior official with the [FBI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Bureau_of_Investigation "Federal Bureau of Investigation") and was at [the Pentagon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Pentagon "The Pentagon") in 2001 during the [September 11 attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_11_attacks "September 11 attacks").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-NBCNews_Motive_Revealed-22) Edward Snowden said that he had expected to work for the federal government, as had the rest of his family.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-BamfordWired-23) His parents divorced in 2001,[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-NBCNews_Timeline-24) and his father remarried.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-25)

In the early 1990s, while still in grade school, Snowden moved with his family to the area of [Fort Meade, Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Meade,_Maryland "Fort Meade, Maryland").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-NBCNews_Man_Who_Spilled-26)[Mononucleosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infectious_mononucleosis "Infectious mononucleosis") caused him to miss high school for almost nine months.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-BamfordWired-23) Rather than returning to school, he claims to have passed the [GED](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Educational_Development "General Educational Development") test.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-guardian-reveal-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-:4-28) He took classes at [Anne Arundel Community College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anne_Arundel_Community_College "Anne Arundel Community College").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-NBCNews_Snowden-17) Although Snowden had no undergraduate college degree,[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-Despiteresume-29) he worked online toward a master's degree in computer security at the [University of Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Liverpool "University of Liverpool") in 2011.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-30) He was interested in [Japanese popular culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_popular_culture "Japanese popular culture"), had studied the [Japanese language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_language "Japanese language"),[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-31) and worked for a now defunct start-up [anime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anime "Anime") company based in the U.S.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-33) He also said he had a basic understanding of [Mandarin Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_Chinese "Standard Chinese") and was deeply interested in [martial arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martial_arts "Martial arts"). At age 20, he listed his religion as [Buddhism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddhism "Buddhism") after working at a [U.S. military base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_American_military_installations#Japan "List of American military installations") in Japan.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-nyt-ambition-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-36)

In September 2019, as part of interviews relating to the release of his memoir _[Permanent Record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Permanent\_Record\_(autobiography) "Permanent Record (autobiography)")_, Snowden revealed to _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_ that he married [Lindsay Mills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Mills "Lindsay Mills") in a courthouse in Moscow.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-I_was_very_much_a_person_the_most_powerful_government_in_the_world_wanted_to_go_away-10) The couple's first son was born in December 2020,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-37) and their second son was born sometime before September 2022.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-wp_citizenship-38)

Snowden enlisted in the [United States Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army "United States Army") on May 7, 2004, and became a [Special Forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_special_operations_forces "United States special operations forces") candidate through its [18X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_Forces_(United_States_Army)#Special_Forces_MOS_descriptions "Special Forces (United States Army)") enlistment option.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-39) He did not complete the training[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-BirthDate-12) due to a leg injury and was given an administrative discharge[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-40) on September 28, 2004.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-41)

Snowden was then employed for less than a year in 2005 as a security guard at the [University of Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Maryland "University of Maryland")'s Center for Advanced Study of Language, a research center sponsored by the National Security Agency (NSA).[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-42) According to the university, this is not a classified facility,[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-43) though it is heavily guarded.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-44) In June 2014, Snowden told _[Wired](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wired\_(magazine) "Wired (magazine)")_ that his job as a security guard required a high-level [security clearance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Security_clearance "Security clearance"), for which he passed a [polygraph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polygraph "Polygraph") exam and underwent a stringent background investigation.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-BamfordWired-23)

### Employment at the CIA

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edward_Snowden&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Employment at the CIA")]

After attending a 2006 job-fair focused on intelligence agencies, Snowden accepted an offer for a position at the CIA.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-BamfordWired-23)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-JacobJijo-45) The Agency assigned him to the global communications division at [CIA headquarters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CIA_headquarters "CIA headquarters") in [Langley, Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Langley,_Virginia "Langley, Virginia").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-BamfordWired-23)

In May 2006, Snowden wrote in _[Ars Technica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ars\_Technica "Ars Technica")_ that he had no trouble getting work because he was a "computer wizard".[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-nyt-ambition-34) Snowden was sent to the CIA's secret school for technology specialists, where he lived in a hotel for six months while studying and training full-time.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-BamfordWired-23)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-:4-28)

In March 2007, the CIA stationed Snowden with [diplomatic cover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diplomatic_cover "Diplomatic cover") in [Geneva, Switzerland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geneva,_Switzerland "Geneva, Switzerland"), where he was responsible for maintaining computer-network security.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-BamfordWired-23)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-46) Assigned to the [U.S. Permanent Mission to the United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Mission_to_the_United_Nations "United States Mission to the United Nations") – a [diplomatic mission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diplomatic_mission "Diplomatic mission") representing U.S. interests before the [UN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations") and other [international organizations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_organizations "International organizations"), Snowden received a diplomatic passport and a four-bedroom apartment near [Lake Geneva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Geneva "Lake Geneva").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-BamfordWired-23)

According to Greenwald, while there Snowden said he was "considered the top technical and cybersecurity expert" in that country and "was hand-picked by the [CIA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Intelligence_Agency "Central Intelligence Agency") to support the president at the 2008 [NATO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO "NATO") summit in [Romania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romania "Romania")".[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-:5-48) A 2016 report from the US House of Representatives Select Committee on Intelligence said that Snowden's official position at CIA was an entry-level technical services officer.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-:4-28)

Snowden described his CIA experience in Geneva as formative, stating that the CIA deliberately got a Swiss banker drunk and encouraged him to drive home. Snowden said that when the latter was arrested for drunk driving, a CIA operative offered to help in exchange for the banker becoming an informant.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-49)[Ueli Maurer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ueli_Maurer "Ueli Maurer"), [President of the Swiss Confederation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_Swiss_Confederation "President of the Swiss Confederation") for the year 2013, publicly disputed Snowden's claims in June of that year: "This would mean that the CIA successfully bribed the Geneva police and judiciary. With all due respect, I just can't imagine it."[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-50) In February 2009, after his supervisor grew suspicious that Snowden was trying to access files he was not authorized to view, Snowden resigned from the CIA.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-from-loyal-51)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-:5-48)

In 2009, Snowden began work as a contractor for [Dell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dell "Dell"),[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-ReutersDell-52) which manages computer systems for multiple government agencies. Assigned to an NSA facility at [Yokota Air Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yokota_Air_Base "Yokota Air Base") near [Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo "Tokyo"), Snowden instructed top officials and military officers on how to defend their networks from Chinese hackers.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-BamfordWired-23) Snowden looked into [mass surveillance in China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mass_surveillance_in_China "Mass surveillance in China") which prompted him to investigate and then expose Washington's mass surveillance program after he was asked in 2009 to brief a conference in Tokyo.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-53)

During his four years with Dell, he rose from supervising NSA computer system upgrades to working as what his résumé termed a "cyber strategist" and an "expert in cyber counterintelligence" at several U.S. locations.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-DrewShaneNYT-54) In 2010, he had a brief stint in [New Delhi, India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Delhi,_India "New Delhi, India"), where he enrolled himself in a local IT institute to learn core [Java programming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Java_programming "Java programming") and advanced [ethical hacking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_hat_(computer_security) "White hat (computer security)").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-55)

In 2011, he returned to [Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryland "Maryland"), where he spent a year as system administrator and pre-sales technical engineer on Dell's CIA account. In that capacity, he was consulted by the chiefs of the CIA's technical branches, including the agency's [chief information officer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_information_officer "Chief information officer") and its [chief technology officer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_technology_officer "Chief technology officer").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-BamfordWired-23) U.S. officials and other sources familiar with the investigation said Snowden began downloading documents describing the government's electronic spying programs while working for Dell in April 2012.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-ReutersDell-52) Investigators estimated that of the 50,000 to 200,000 documents Snowden gave to Greenwald and Poitras, most were copied by Snowden while working at Dell.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-VanityFair-2)

In March 2012, Dell reassigned Snowden to Hawaii as lead technologist for the NSA's information-sharing office.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-BamfordWired-23)

On March 15, 2013—three days after what he later called his "breaking point" of "seeing the [Director of National Intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Director_of_National_Intelligence "Director of National Intelligence"), [James Clapper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Clapper "James Clapper"), directly lie under oath to Congress"[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-ARDtranscript-56)—Snowden quit his job at Dell.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-Epstein-57) Although he has said his career high annual salary was $200,000,[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-qa-58) Snowden said he took a pay cut to work at consulting firm [Booz Allen Hamilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Booz_Allen_Hamilton "Booz Allen Hamilton"),[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-qa-58) where he sought employment in order to gather data and then release details of the NSA's worldwide surveillance activity.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-SCMPJune24-59)

At the time of his departure from the U.S. in May 2013, he had been employed for 15 months inside the NSA's [Hawaii regional operations center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunia_Regional_SIGINT_Operations_Center "Kunia Regional SIGINT Operations Center"), which focuses on the electronic monitoring of [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China") and [North Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Korea "North Korea"),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-VanityFair-2) first for Dell and then for two months with Booz Allen Hamilton.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-Two-Person-60) While intelligence officials have described his position there as a [system administrator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/System_administrator "System administrator"), Snowden has said he was an infrastructure analyst, which meant that his job was to look for new ways to break into Internet and telephone traffic around the world.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-nytinfrastructure-61) An anonymous source told [Reuters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reuters "Reuters") that, while in Hawaii, Snowden may have persuaded 20–25 co-workers to give him their login credentials by telling them he needed them to do his job.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-62) The NSA sent a memo to Congress saying that Snowden had tricked a fellow employee into sharing his personal [private key](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_key_infrastructure "Public key infrastructure") to gain greater access to the NSA's computer system.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-63)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-64) Snowden disputed the memo,[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-genius_among-65) saying in January 2014, "I never stole any passwords, nor did I trick an army of co-workers."[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-WaPo01242014-66)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-live-67) Booz Allen terminated Snowden's employment on June 10, 2013, the day after he went public with his story, and three weeks after he had left [Hawaii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii "Hawaii") on a leave of absence.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-20130611usatoday-68)

The former colleague said Snowden was given full administrator privileges with virtually unlimited access to NSA data. Snowden was offered a position on the NSA's elite team of [hackers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hacker_(computer_security) "Hacker (computer security)"), [Tailored Access Operations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tailored_Access_Operations "Tailored Access Operations"), but turned it down to join Booz Allen.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-genius_among-65) An anonymous source later said that Booz Allen's hiring screeners found possible discrepancies in Snowden's résumé but still decided to hire him.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-Despiteresume-29) Snowden's résumé stated that he attended computer-related classes at [Johns Hopkins University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_University "Johns Hopkins University"). A spokeswoman for Johns Hopkins said that the university did not find records to show that Snowden attended the university and suggested that he may instead have attended Advanced Career Technologies, a private for-profit organization that operated as the Computer Career Institute at Johns Hopkins University.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-Despiteresume-29) The University of Maryland University College acknowledged that Snowden had attended a summer session at a UM campus in Asia. Snowden's résumé stated that he estimated he would receive a University of Liverpool computer security master's degree in 2013. The university said that Snowden registered for an online master's degree program in computer security in 2011 but was inactive as a student and had not completed the program.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-Despiteresume-29)

In his May 2014 interview with [NBC News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC_News "NBC News"), Snowden accused the U.S. government of trying to use one position here or there in his career to distract from the totality of his experience, downplaying him as a "low-level analyst". In his words, he was "trained as a spy in the traditional sense of the word in that I lived and worked undercover overseas—pretending to work in a job that I'm not—and even being assigned a name that was not mine." He said he had worked for the NSA undercover overseas, and for the [DIA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defense_Intelligence_Agency "Defense Intelligence Agency") had developed sources and methods to keep information and people secure "in the most hostile and dangerous environments around the world. So when they say I'm a low-level systems administrator, that I don't know what I'm talking about, I'd say it's somewhat misleading."[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-NBCNews_Motive_Revealed-22) In a June interview with [Globo TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Globo_TV "Globo TV"), Snowden reiterated that he "was actually functioning at a very senior level".[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-Globo-69) In a July interview with _The Guardian_, Snowden explained that, during his NSA career, "I began to move from merely overseeing these systems to actively directing their use. Many people don't understand that I was actually an analyst and I designated individuals and groups for targeting."[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-EditedTranscript-70) Snowden subsequently told _Wired_ that while at Dell in 2011, "I would sit down with the CIO of the CIA, the CTO of the CIA, the chiefs of all the technical branches. They would tell me their hardest technology problems, and it was my job to come up with a way to fix them."[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-BamfordWired-23)

During his time as an NSA analyst, directing the work of others, Snowden recalled a moment when he and his colleagues began to have severe ethical doubts. Snowden said 18 to 22 year-old analysts were suddenly

> thrust into a position of extraordinary responsibility, where they now have access to all your private records. In the course of their daily work, they stumble across something that is completely unrelated in any sort of necessary sense—for example, an intimate nude photo of someone in a sexually compromising situation. But they're extremely attractive. So what do they do? They turn around in their chair and they show a co-worker ... and sooner or later this person's whole life has been seen by all of these other people.

Snowden observed that this behavior happened routinely every two months but was never reported, being considered one of the "[fringe benefits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fringe_benefits "Fringe benefits")" of the work.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-Ispy-71)

### Whistleblower status

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edward_Snowden&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Whistleblower status")]

Snowden has described himself as a whistleblower,[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-snowden-wired-72) a description used by many sources, including [CNBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNBC "CNBC"),[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-snowden-cnbc-73)_[The New Yorker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_Yorker "The New Yorker")_,[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-snowden-newyorker-74) Reuters,[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-snowden-reuters-75) and _The Guardian_,[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-snowden-guardian-76) among others.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-snowden-nation-77)[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-snowden-usatoday-78)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-79) The term has both informal and legal meanings.

Snowden said that he had told multiple employees and two supervisors about his concerns, but the NSA disputes his claim.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-WPSnowdenInterview20131224-80) Snowden elaborated in January 2014, saying "[I] made tremendous efforts to report these programs to co-workers, supervisors, and anyone with the proper clearance who would listen. The reactions of those I told about the scale of the constitutional violations ranged from deeply concerned to appalled, but no one was willing to risk their jobs, families, and possibly even freedom to go to [_[sic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sic "Sic")_] through what [Thomas Andrews] [Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_A._Drake "Thomas A. Drake") did."[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-live-67)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-newyorker01232014-81) In March 2014, during testimony to the European Parliament, Snowden wrote that before revealing classified information he had reported "clearly problematic programs" to ten officials, who he said did nothing in response.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-WaPo10reports-82) In a May 2014 interview, Snowden told NBC News that after bringing his concerns about the legality of the NSA spying programs to officials, he was told to stay silent on the matter. He said that the NSA had copies of emails he sent to their Office of General Counsel, oversight, and compliance personnel broaching "concerns about the NSA's interpretations of its legal authorities. I had raised these complaints not just officially in writing through email, but to my supervisors, to my colleagues, in more than one office."[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-NBCNews_Motive_Revealed-22)

In May 2014, U.S. officials released a single email that Snowden had written in April 2013 inquiring about legal authorities but said that they had found no other evidence that Snowden had expressed his concerns to someone in an oversight position.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-83) In June 2014, the NSA said it had not been able to find any records of Snowden raising internal complaints about the agency's operations.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-84) That same month, Snowden explained that he had not produced the communiqués in question because of the ongoing nature of the dispute, disclosing for the first time that "I am working with the NSA in regard to these records and we're going back and forth, so I don't want to reveal everything that will come out."[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Snowden#cite_note-85)

Self-description as a whistleblower and attribution as such in news reports does not determine whether he qualifies as a whistleblower within the meaning of the [Whistleblower Protection Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whistleblower_Protection_Act "Whistleblower Protection Act") of 1989 (5 USC 2303(b)(8)-(9); Pub. Law 101-12). However, Snowden's potential status as a whistleblower under the 1989 Act is not directly addressed in the criminal complaint against him in the [United States District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_District_Court_for_the_Eastern_District_of_Virginia "United States District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia") (see below) (Case No. 1:13 CR 265 (0MH)).
